Investment Banking Days One edition per year, dedicated to **firms operating in the Investment Banking world**. Check out the [event page](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/meet-employers/investment-banking-days "Investment Banking Days") to find out all the info. Recruiting Dates **Five editions per year, each one dedicated to specific business fields**: - [Arts, Sport & "Recruiting Date Arts, Sport & Entertainment") - [Banking, Financial Services & "Recruiting Date Banking, Financial Services & Fintech") - [Fashion, Luxury & " Recruiting Date Fashion, Luxury & Beauty") - [Government, Public Services & International "Recruiting Date Government, Public Services & International Organizations") - [Web & IT Companies](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/meet-employers/recruiting-date-web-it-companies "Recruiting Date Web Companies") Tax&Legal Networking Event One edition per year, it is the **career event dedicated to Law and Tax Firms.** You can find more info [here](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/meet-employers/tax-legal-networking-event "Tax & Legal Networking Event"). _**How to join**_ _These initiatives are held throughout the whole academic year and participation is upon-registration only._ _**To register, please refer to You@B > Career Service menu > Events Calendar**, where you will also find the specific contact to ask for more info about the event of your interest, if needed._ _In some cases registration follows a specific process, and sometimes is limited to ad hoc categories of students and graduates: you will find information in the dedicated pages when needed._ [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/meet-employers/career-fairs#addtoany "Show all")

text: Career Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services) # In-Company Training abroad _Career programs organized at **company premises** and structured in a **theoretical part** (company presentations, speeches) and a **practical one** (business cases, group work, networking, etc.)._ _**What’s in it for you?** You will gain better understanding of employers and the job market in different Countries, join hands-on projects, engage with company representatives to dive deep into their functional areas, career possibilities, and internship opportunities._ _In-Company Training abroad programs have different timings, locations and tracks, and may vary in application deadlines and eligibility criteria._ _A **sine qua non** **condition** for being eligible and selected is having **student status** at the time of application and maintaining it **for the entire duration** of the Program._ _Here you can find more info on eligibility:_ - text: Career Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services) ![symbol of the investment banking event with a piggy # Investment Banking Days ## From 5 to 25 September 2025 _Investment Banking Days is **Bocconi University's event dedicated to the Investment Banking world** and it will be held in hybrid mode.It will be structured as follows:_ ### 8, 9 and 10 September: Round Tables Join Round Tables to hear about the experience of junior Alumni working in Investment Banking. ### 8 and 9 September: Webinars Prepare to meet with employers by attending company webinars online. ### 11 September: Networking fair on campus From 10am to 4pm, you'll have the chance to meet with company representatives in person, interact directly with recruiters, get useful information about the hiring processes and apply. ### 8 - 25 September: Digital Campaign Access a digital area to find out about participating employers, their recruiting programs and available career opportunities. ## Agenda and registration info Round Tables These initiatives give you the chance to listen from Alumni talking about their career paths in Investment Banking. title: Recognition of internships done between the Bachelor and the Master of Science programs | Bocconi University
text:
Career Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services) # Recognition of internships done between the Bachelor and the Master of Science programs **ATTENTION PLEASE! YOU'RE ACCESSING THIS PAGE VIA AN OLD LINK AND THE CONTENTS MAY BE NO LONGER VALID (LAST UPDATE: APRIL 2024).** **STARTING FROM MAY 2024, PLEASE REFER TO THE NEW CONTENTS AVAILABLE AT THE FOLLOWING LINKS FOR** [**STUDENTS**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/your-internship-start-credit-recognition "Your internship: from start to credit recognition") **AND** [**COMPANIES**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/activating-and-managing-internships "Activating and managing internships") **.** \\*\\*\\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\* The University may recognize as a curricular internship an **internship pursued after obtaining of the Bachelor of Science degree and before the beginning of the Master of science program.** You can request the Internships Office to authorize recognition of such experience through B in touch (the Office will discuss the matter with the Director of the degree course) before the end of first year teaching term (end of second semester). Below, the instructions to be followed in order to ensure recognition in your curriculum of studies of an internship pursued between the Bachelor of Science and Master programs. | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | **WHO** | | **WHAT** | | **You** | 1 | Request authorization for recognition of the experience at the Internship Office via B in touch.
At the same time, send in attachment through B in touch:
— the document underlying the internship relationship with the employer that hosted you, e.g. a contract (if the internship was not activated through Bocconi University) in Italian or English;
— an internship certificate printed on the company’s letterhead and signed by a company representative in Italian or English;
— a three-year degree diploma (if obtained at a university other than Bocconi);
— a 2-page report written by yourself analysing activities done, goals achieved and consistency with your current study path in English. | | **The Internship Office** | 2 | Evaluates the experience and/or the documentation provided, registers it on the JobGate portal and enables the request for credits (advance authorization).
_At this point the internship will appear in the "My internships" area of JobGate in the yoU@B Agenda._ | | **You** | 3 | Access JobGate in the Calendar, in the area "My internships", section "Training project", **confirm** the internship with a click on the appropriate button and request **advance authorization** with a click on the "Request for recognition of credits" button on the same page. | | **The Director of the degree course or his/her delegate** | 4 | Evaluates the internship and may grant or refuse **final validation** or, in the case of need of further information, invite you either for a personal interview or a conversation via B in touch. | | **The Academic Affairs Division** | 5 | Registers the internship in your study plan.
_Once you have obtained final recognition of the internship, you will be able to check the proper registration of the formative credits, also through the Calendar in the "My internships" area of JobGate, or in the Punto Blu in the "Career" section._ | ### Links - [Guide to the University

title: Switch from curricular to extracurricular internship after graduation | Bocconi University
text: Career Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services) # Switch from curricular to extracurricular internship after graduation **ATTENTION PLEASE! YOU'RE ACCESSING THIS PAGE VIA AN OLD LINK AND THE CONTENTS MAY BE NO LONGER VALID (LAST UPDATE: APRIL 2024).** **STARTING FROM MAY 2024, PLEASE REFER TO THE NEW CONTENTS AVAILABLE AT THE FOLLOWING LINKS FOR** [**STUDENTS**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/your-internship-start-credit-recognition "Your internship: from start to credit recognition") **AND** [**COMPANIES**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/activating-and-managing-internships "Activating and managing internships") **.** \\*\\*\\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\* An internship that begins before graduation is considered curricular (with or without credits). **From the graduation day** onwards, such internship becomes extracurricular. If your internship is **carried out in Lombardy**, due to a Bocconi policy, it remains curricular if it is completed by 59 calendar days after the awarding of the degree. Due to this policy: — if your internship is completed by 59 calendar days after the awarding of the degree, it will end regularly; — if your internship is completed after 59 calendar days after the awarding of the degree, it will be interrupted by the Internship Office on the fifty-ninth day after the graduation day. The company can then activate a new internship that will start as an extracurricular one. For this new extracurricular internship you shall commit to meet [all the requirements](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/programs/current-students/services/activating-extracurricular-internship) set out by the relevant law on extracurricular internships. If the internship **is not carried out in Lombardy,** due to the relevant regional laws’ peculiarities, please, contact the Internship Office in order to make sure that the University can act as promoting body. The University does not activate extracurricular internships in Latium and Emilia-Romagna. If the internship **is carried out outside Italy,** please, do inform in due time your Company about your graduation. "Show all")

title: Types of internship | Bocconi University
text: Career Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services) # Types of internship **ATTENTION PLEASE! YOU'RE ACCESSING THIS PAGE VIA AN OLD LINK AND THE CONTENTS MAY BE NO LONGER VALID (LAST UPDATE: APRIL 2024).** **STARTING FROM MAY 2024, PLEASE REFER TO THE NEW CONTENTS AVAILABLE AT THE FOLLOWING LINKS FOR** [**STUDENTS**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/your-internship-start-credit-recognition "Your internship: from start to credit recognition") **AND** [**COMPANIES**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/activating-and-managing-internships "Activating and managing internships") **.** \\*\\*\\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\* Internship is an on the-field training experience, not a work contract, whose governing rules, applicable in Italy, are established by current national and regional laws and regulations, and by the University. By “curricular internship” is meant an internship pursued by students before receiving their degree. A curricular internship that satisfies certain requirements may be registered in the student’s curriculum of studies ( **curricular internship for credits**). This may be done for a single internship per study course\*. \* **A** **second internship** experience worth 6 credits can be completed only for **Bachelor of Science and Law programs**, which will be recorded as an **additional internship** in the study plan. For more information, please see the Guides to the University. Additional internships, or internships that do not satisfy the requirements for recognition, are referred to as **curricular internships without credits**(if pursued before award of degree). Finally, an internship pursued after graduation is known as an **extracurricular internship**. text: Career Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services) # What to do on the first day: internship documents **ATTENTION PLEASE! YOU'RE ACCESSING THIS PAGE VIA AN OLD LINK AND THE CONTENTS MAY BE NO LONGER VALID (LAST UPDATE: APRIL 2024).** **STARTING FROM MAY 2024, PLEASE REFER TO THE NEW CONTENTS AVAILABLE AT THE FOLLOWING LINKS FOR** [**STUDENTS**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/your-internship-start-credit-recognition "Your internship: from start to credit recognition") **AND** [**COMPANIES**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/activating-and-managing-internships "Activating and managing internships") **.** \\*\\*\\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\* An internship is considered activated once the document regulating it (Progetto Formativo Individuale/Convenzione Singola di Tirocinio/Internship Agreement) has been duly signed; therefore, on the first day you must make sure that this document is printed out, signed by you and the employer and sent to the University in accordance with the prescribed procedure. In particular: The employer may **print out the document** from the page concerning your internship on the JobGate portal. You may also print out the document from the yoU@B Agenda, in the section "My internships"–"Training project". **The document must then be signed** by you and by a legal Representative of the employer or his/her delegate. In most Bocconi internship documents two signatures are required, at the penultimate and final article thereof. Once signed, **the original document must be sent to the Internship Office** in either of the following ways: - dispatch by mail/courier (see the section [Internships Office: Contacts and reception](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/programs/current-students/services/internship-office-contacts)); - hand delivery to the Bocconi Post Office, Viale Bligny 12, Monday through Friday, 8.30 am — 4.30 pm Often it is the employer who sees to the sending, but it is your responsibility to verify that it is carried out, because in the event of non-submission of the document the internship cannot be considered valid. For internships taking place outside Europe, a scan of the document submitted via B in touch (Internship) is accepted, but the original must be given to the Internship Office once the intern has returned to Italy. Finally, the Internship Office makes the document bearing all signatures available to the employer (on JobGate) and to the intern (in the Agenda, section "My internships") by uploading it in the “Attachment Area”. ### Links - [Activation through Bocconi documents]( [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services/what-do-first-day-internship-documents#addtoany "Show all")

title: Guide to curricular internships | Bocconi University
text:
Career Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/career-services) # Guide to curricular internships _**Curricular internships** are all the internships **performed by students before graduating.**_ _Curricular internships satisfying certain requirements of content, timing and duration entitle students to ask for **academic credits** to be registered in the study plan. Any other internship pursued by students that does not observe the requirements of the curricular internship with credits, or is an additional internship to the ones recorded on your study plan, is a curricular internship without credits._ ## Guide When to do your internship The University invites you to carry out such experience, whose content – in case of curricular internship with credits - must be in line with your degree program, after the completion of learning activities which are fundamental to gain basic theoretical knowledge. - **BSc students** You can participate in a curricular internship with credits starting from the end of second-year classes onwards. The minimum duration is 6 weeks full time or 8 weeks part time. As an exception, if you meet some specific academic requirements, you can complete the internship experience between the end of the teaching period of the first year and the start of the teaching period of the second year. - **MSc students** You can participate in a curricular internship with credits starting from the end of first-year classes onwards. The minimum duration is 8 weeks full time or 11 weeks part time. - **Law students** You can participate in a curricular internship with credits starting from the end of fourth-year classes onwards. The minimum duration is 8 weeks full time or 11 weeks part time. See more information about "Types of internships and similar activities” [here](https://bit.unibocconi.it/hc/en-us/sections/4403741019282-Types-of-internship-and-similar-activities). Where to do your internship Internships may take place, in Italy and abroad, at companies, public and private institutions, professional firms, international organisms, diplomatic agencies, cultural institutions and other organizations. The University reserves the right to evaluate the eligibility of the company to host the intern, as well as location and any mixed (in-person/remote) or remote (distance) modes. Bocconi also monitors the internship throughout its duration. Curricular internships with credit recognition cannot be carried out at family-owned companies. For internships abroad see more info [here](https://bit.unibocconi.it/hc/en-us/articles/18637143597970-Helpful-information-for-internships-abroad). For unpaid internship abroad see How to activate your internship and get credit recognition You always have to properly activate your internship before its beginning. text: Funding [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/funding) # Introduction to ISU Bocconi Scholarship a.y. 2025-26 - Timeline The Lombardy Region and the Ministry of the Universities and Research allocate, through the Universities, a cash benefit called the "Right to University Education Scholarship". For the Bocconi University, students enrolled in Bachelor of Science, Law programs, Master of Science and PhD programs, interested in applying for this benefit for the academic year 2025-2026, must submit an application for the "ISU Bocconi Scholarship a.y. 2025-2026". In order to submit the application for the "ISU Bocconi Scholarship a.y. 2025-2026" ( **grant, related services and supplements**) economic requirements, enrollment requirements and merit requirements (minimum number of credits to be earned for confirmation of the benefit for each year of enrollment) must be met. These requirements are available on the dedicated pages. The deadlines for submitting the application for the ISU grant are final and different for students enrolled in the first year of their BSc or Law programs, for students enrolled in the first year of their MSc or PhD, or students enrolled in years subsequent to the first (for all the study programs, BSc, Law programs, MSc and PhD). These deadlines are detailed below. [**First-year students of Bachelor of Science or Law programs**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/funding/isu-bocconi-scholarship-first-year-students-ay-2025-26 "ISU Bocconi Scholarship - First year students a.y. 2025-26") The application for the ISU Bocconi Scholarship a.y. 2025-2026 can be submitted by **first-year students** only after the submission of the single application " [**Bocconi4access to Education a.y. 2025-2026**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/applying-bocconi/bachelor-and-law-programs/funding "Funding")". For each admission session, a specific and corresponding time window exists for students to submit the funding application Application deadlines and further deadlines are as follow: - **Early Session and HEC 1st round**: January 7 - January 21, 2025 - **Winter Session and HEC 2nd round**: March 11 - April 3, 2025 - **Spring Session and HEC 3rd round**: May 20 - June 4, 2025 For the ISU Bocconi scholarship, applications will not be accepted outside of the above deadlines and from students who have not previously presented the "Bocconi4access to Education a.y. 2025-2026" application within the established deadlines. In order to assess the economic conditions of applicants for the ISU Bocconi scholarship, the Office will verify that the documentation presented in the two applications is coherent and corresponds to the economic/financial situation declared by the family. The deadline for submitting documentation concerning the non-resident or commuting status is available within the application. The final ranking will be published by the end of October 2025. text: Master of Science Program [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/master-science-program) # Annual Study Program Form Accounting and Financial Management [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/master-science-program/accounting-and-financial-management) [Placement and Program [Program The Annual Study Program Form (SUA-CdS) acts as a tool through which a study program communicates essential information. The SUA-CdS is organized into a set of tables, which are in turn divided into sections, each corresponding to a specific area: - **Table A:** Learning Objectives Contains information on consultations with representative organizations from the employment sector, professional profiles, expected job prospects, learning outcomes, admission requirements and the final exam. - **Table B:** Student Experience Encompasses the outline of the educational path and evaluation methods for knowledge and skills. It lists academic schedules, exams and graduation sessions. It provides information about core Faculty, the learning environment – including classrooms, computer labs, laboratories, study areas and libraries – and available support services. Moreover, it presents feedback data gathered from students and graduates. - **Table C:** Learning Outcomes Summarizes key statistical data regarding student admission, progression and graduation, as well as graduates' employment placement. It also includes feedback from organizations and companies with which internship agreements have been established. - **Table D:** Study Program Organization and Quality Management Illustrates the organizational structure and responsibilities of the study program and its Quality Assurance processes, activity planning, etc. The SUA-CdS is prepared and revised on an annual basis by the Study Program's Director, serving as a valuable tool for **planning**, **execution**, **administration**, **self-assessment** and **revision** of each Study Program. For more information, see the attached SUA-CdS below (in Italian only). ### Attachment - [AFM SUA-25-26](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/AFM_25-26.pdf) Accounting and Financial Management [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/master-science-program/accounting-and-financial-management) [Placement and Program [Program "Show all")

text: Master of Science Program [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/master-science-program) # Program Committee Accounting and Financial Management [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/master-science-program/accounting-and-financial-management) [Placement and Program [Program **Regulations concerning roles and make-up** The committee supports the director in ensuring the operation of the program. In particular it may express proposals regarding the management and organization of the program's educational activities and ensure a constant monitoring of the Program through the examination of statistical data provided by administrative offices. **The Program Committee is made up of:** - the Program Director who chairs it; - up to six instructors chosen by compulsory course supervisors, from within their areas; - up to three supervisor instructors of optional courses, identified by the program director; - two students from Master of Science program, elected according to the rules set out in the proper regulations. The Director has the right to summon the Program Committee, and will act as president of the Committee. The Program Committee must be summoned at least 3 times during the academic year. It also gathers any time the Director deems necessary or upon the justified request of at least 1/5 members of the same Committee. Master of Science Program [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/master-science-program) # Broaden Your Frame The Broaden Your Frame Seminar Series aim to provide a platform for discussion with people from different sectors, often deliberately unrelated to the economic, managerial, legal, and financial worlds discussed in the classroom every day. Students will have the opportunity to meet philosophers, writers, scientists, researchers, artists, historians, architects, and designers and challenge themselves with experiences and perspectives that will help them appreciate the world in its complexity. title: Enhancing Experience - Curricular Supplementary Activities | Bocconi University
text: Master of Science Program [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/master-science-program) # Enhancing Experience - Curricular Supplementary Activities Enhancing Experience - Curricular Supplementary Activities aim to develop broad-spectrum culture and are considered useful activities for entering the job market. The study plans of students enrolled in MSc programs include 2 compulsory credits dedicated to these activities (with the exception of the DSBA, CYBER, TS and AI programs, whose students can attend the Enhancing Experience and record the 2 credit points earned as extra activities). Enhancing Experiences are assigned through participation in dedicated Calls for Applications that open at different times of the year. A few days before the opening of each Call, a message is sent through the yoU@B student diary specifying the opening and closing dates. **The procedure for applying is available in the yoU@B student diary under Enhancing Experience > Call - Choice of Activity** starting from the opening day of the Call. The achievement of the 2 credits is subject to meeting the participation requirements and **passing an assessment test** **(pass or fail), which, even in the case of students registered in online activities,** **will always take place in person on campus**. The options for carrying out the tests (oral, written, multiple choice, open answer) may vary according to the activity and will be communicated at the beginning of each course. The Enhancing Experience offer is provided by the **Campus Life**, **ITEC** and **Language Center** services and by the Graduate School, and is integrated with the **Broaden Your Frame** seminar cycles and the **Media Experience** initiative. - [Campus - [ITEC]( - [Language Center]( - [Broaden Your - [Media "Show all")

title: MEDIA EXPERIENCE 2026 | Bocconi University
text: Master of Science Program [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/master-science-program) # MEDIA EXPERIENCE 2026 Do you know the rules of the media? Are you ready to use them in your future job? Do you know how to manage your media presence? Through the Enhancing Experience activity **Media Experience - English edition**, Bocconi is giving you the opportunity to develop one of the most requested and least cultivated skills in the world of management. Media Experience is a theoretical and practical training course, conducted by professional journalists and dedicated to students who want to learn the essential techniques for using media effectively. **PROGRAM:** **— Two days of seminars,** dedicated to the basics, the rules and tools of communication, introduced through practical cases and experiences. **— One day of individual training session**, with one-to-one television interviews, and subsequent check of personal performances. The training sessions will be held on **Saturdays** (morning or afternoon) after the two seminars. **Students are required to participate in only one training session** and they will be able to register through BlackBoard groups. The available training sessions are illustrated in the table below. **CURATOR:** **Andrea Cabrini** is a broadcast journalist specialized in economics. Since 2000, he has been Managing Editor of Class CNBC, a finance channel broadcast on Sky 507, and Co-Managing Editor of MF-Milanofinanza. In the past he was Editor-in-Chief and Presenter for Mediaset news broadcasting (Studio Aperto and Tg4). An expert in communication and media training, he has advised professionals and executives at leading Italian and international companies working in Italy. **ATTENDANCE AND EARNING CREDITS:** To complete the two credits, **you must attend the the two seminars** and **a training session,** preparing the materials assigned by your professors (which will be shared with you after the seminars). **CALENDAR:** Below you can find the calendar of the 2026 edition of the Media Experience Initiative: | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Media Experience Seminars 2026** | | | **Day** | **Time** | **Classroom** | | **Seminar 1** | Friday 6 February | 13.30-16.30 | N19 | | **Seminar 2** | Friday 13 February | 13.30-16.30 | N19 | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Media Experience Training Sessions 2026** | | | **Date** | **Time** | **Room** | | **Training Session 1** | Saturday 14 February | 9-13 | TBA | | **Training Session 2** | Saturday 14 February | 14-18 | TBA | | **Training Session 3** | Saturday 28 February | 9-13 | TBA | | **Training Session 4** | Saturday 28 February | 14-18 | TBA | | **Training Session 5** | Saturday 7 March | 9-13 | TBA | | **Training Session 6** | Saturday 7 March | 14-18 | TBA | | **Training Session 7** | Saturday 14 March | 9-13 | TBA | | **Training Session 8** | Saturday 14 March | 14-18 | TBA | | **Training Session 9** | Saturday 28 March | 9-13 | TBA |

text: For Employers and Partners [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners) # JobGate **What is JobGate?** JobGate is Università Bocconi’s Online Job Platform which facilitates the connection between Employers and Bocconi’s best talents. It is now designed to work on smart phones and tablets. Our professional team makes it its business to understand the needs of Employers so that Bocconi students and graduates are in the best possible position to fulfill them. **What does JobGate offer?** - Easy internship and job posting; the job profile can be enriched with a company profile, to help you better reach your target. - Applications can be received and stored directly on the portal. - Employers can create and manage their own applications’ database. - The portal allows direct access to Bocconi’s CvBook. - JobGate enables employers to simply formalize internships offered to students and graduates (Bachelor, Master of Science or Specialized Masters). **How can I access the system?** - It’s very simple: just click [here](https://employers.unibocconi.it/) and follow the step by step instructions. Please note: upon registration you will have to accept the [General concerning the use of the Portal. **How do I formalize and start an internship with a Bocconi student/graduate?\*** Should you have already identified a suitable Bachelor, Master of Science or Specialized Master candidate without posting an internship offer on JobGate, you can formalize the experience through our portal in a few simple steps. - Have you already used JobGate to formalize an internship? Please access the portal with your login details and set off the internship as usual. - Is it the first time you wish to formalize an internship with Bocconi? Please register on JobGate as a new user and specify your registration is due to the formalization of an internship for a candidate that has already been selected either “Start an internship with a known student/graduate” or “Start an internship for a Specialized Master student”\*. If necessary, we will contact you within 5 working days after the registration. NEWS: Starting from now you may set off an internship through JobGate for students and graduates from Specialized Masters. In these cases please refer to the [specific Master’s staff](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/employers/online-recruitment/request-cv-book-master-holders). **Who can I refer to for further details?** - For further details please refer to your [relationship manager](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/employers/internship-office-contacts). \\* as per Italian Law ### Links - [Employer Policies]( - [Contacts]( - [Services dedicated to Head Hunting Agencies]( [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/employersold/online-recruitment/jobgate#addtoany "Show all")

text: For Employers and Partners [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners) JobGate: internship and job posting Overview # JobGate: internship and job posting _**JobGate** is Bocconi University's job portal available to employers for **posting internship and job offers**, **managing applications**, and **accessing the University's graduate database** (CVBook)._ _JobGate is also the tool to start internship agreements with selected students and graduates: for info related to this topic, please check the web pages dedicated to_ [_internship documents_](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/activating-and-managing-internships "Activating and managing internships") _._ ## 2025 wrapped 3,900+ Active companies in JobGate posting offers or hosting internships 9,300+ Internship and job opportunities in Italy or abroad, posted on JobGate ## Discover more How to register _To access JobGate, recruiters need to register at: **employers.unibocconi.it**_ _During registration, employers need to upload in the system standard information (company name, website, registered and operative office, company contact), as well as a company presentation and a certificate of incorporation (if available)._ _At the end of registration, the recruiter will receive the credentials via email: a contact, either by phone or email, from a Bocconi Account - Employer Relationship Manager, is required to unblock the password and is aimed at sharing the general understanding of the system's functioning, the advertisement publication methods, and the company's recruitment needs._ _To use this service, the employer must accept the_ [_General Conditions_](https://login.unibocconi.it/employers/pdf/COND_GEN_ITA.pdf) _that regulate the portal._ How to access _To access JobGate, recruiters must enter their credentials at: **employers.unibocconi.it**_ _Passwords are strictly personal and cannot be transferred to third parties. All company contacts needing access to the portal can register by clicking on "Registration of a new contact" to obtain their credentials._ Posting offers Employers can publish both internship and placement offers. **Internship announcements** can be dedicated to: - **Current students** (curricular internships) - **Graduates** up to 12 months after graduation (extracurricular internships). For more information on the employer's role and responsibilities in the internship relationship (tutor, internship modality, educational project, etc.), you can visit the pages dedicated to [activating and managing internships](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners/activating-and-managing-internships "Activating and managing internships"). **Job announcements** can be dedicated to: - **Junior profiles** (positions requiring up to 3 years of experience) - **Senior profiles**(positions requiring more than 3 years of experience). The use of JobGate is free, and companies can post as much offers as they wish.The only exception is for Head Hunting Agencies, which can publish job offers for themselves and for client companies only, and internship offers for themselves only: in both cases, the limit is 12 offers per year (maximum of 2 offers simultaneously). CVBook _The CVBook Directory is the **online database of CVs of Bocconi University graduates**. The access is from the JobGate portal, and employers can use filters to sort results according to objective criterias._ DAL Project - Disabilities and Work _The **DAL Service- Disabilities and Work** supports companies in identifying and hiring Bocconi students and graduates belonging to Protected Categories. In particular, the service offers the possibility of **posting dedicated internship and job offers** on JobGate and **notifies candidates with the specific requirements**._ _Additionally, Bocconi University has joined C.A.L.D.

text: Faculty and Research Departments Overview # Departments The nine Departments ( [Accounting](https://accounting.unibocconi.eu/), [Computing Sciences](https://cs.unibocconi.eu/), [Decision Sciences](https://dec.unibocconi.eu/), [Economics](https://economics.unibocconi.eu/), [Finance](https://finance.unibocconi.eu/), [Legal Studies](https://ius.unibocconi.eu/), [Management and Technology](https://mgmt-tech.unibocconi.eu/), [Marketing](https://marketing.unibocconi.eu/), [Social and Political Sciences](https://sps.unibocconi.eu/)) were created as part of the recent reorganization process. Their formation was one of the most important parts of the process affecting the academic structure of the university. These Departments combine various but collaborative compentencies in order to build defined areas of research and teaching. title: Edvance – Digital Education Hub | Bocconi University
text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # Edvance – Digital Education Hub _The first Digital Education Hub in Italy, created to foster digital culture and innovation in higher education_ Coordinated by Politecnico di Milano and funded as part of _Mission 4 “Education and Research"_ of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP), this project **brings together several universities and Higher Education in Art, Music and Dance (AFAM) institutions in Italy.** Their ambitious goal is to develop, disseminate and consolidate advanced digital skills, while promoting the adoption of innovative and inclusive teaching methods. With more than **200 online courses (MOOCs),** Edvance offers high-quality opportunities for continuous learning and professional development.Participants can also certify their acquired skills through micro-credentials and open badges. The project is aimed at **students, faculty and professionals** interested in exploring topics such as artificial intelligence, data literacy and digital sustainability. **Participation in the courses is free of charge**: users can access the Edvance platform through their university credentials (for institutions participating in the project) or via SPID or CIE digital identification. **National Recovery and Resilience Plan (NRRP)**, Mission 4 “Education and Research” **Component 1**“Enhancement of Education Services: From Nursery Schools to Universities” **Investment** 3.4 “University Teaching and Advanced Skills” – **Sub-Investment** T3 “Digital Education Hubs (DEH)” Funded by the European Union – Next Generation EU - DEH2023-00010 Digital Education Hub\_Higher Education - Project Code: D43C23004530005 [Discover the Project Website](https://www.edvance.it/edvance/app/home) ## Bocconi MOOCs on Edvance The following MOOCs are available on the Edvance website: - **Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals**: A managerial perspective - **Generative Artificial Intelligence**: From fundamentals to business applications - **Artificial Intelligence for Business**: From idea to implementation - **Analytics and AI for Customers and Markets** - **Artificial Intelligence and Human-Machine Interaction** ## Participating Universities and AFAMs Universities - Alma Mater Studiorum – Università di Bologna - Humanitas University - Politecnico di Milano - Politecnico di Torino - Università Bocconi - Università degli Studi di Brescia - Università degli Studi di Cagliari - Università degli studi di Messina - Università di Macerata - Università di Pisa - Università di Torino - Università di Trento AFAMs - Accademia Belle Arti Bologna - Accademia di Belle Arti Venezia - Cagliari Conservatorio di Musica - Fondazione Milano [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/edvance-digital-education-hub#addtoany "Show all")

title: FRAILIFE: Child Disability and Family Life | Bocconi University
text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # FRAILIFE: Child Disability and Family Life **Grant:** ERC Starting Grant, €1.4 million **Principal Investigator:** Prof. Nicoletta Balbo **Period:** 2023-2028 Across the European Union, approximately 4% among individuals under age 16 have a disability, and over 15 million school-age children are known to have special educational needs. Disabilities limit children in their everyday activities and impact families in myriad ways. FRAILIFE aims to comprehensively analyze the effects of a child disability on family members – parents, siblings, and grandparents – in Europe, using high-quality data (registers, surveys, social media), innovative research designs and methods. By focusing on the impact of child disability on family members’ life course trajectories, health outcomes, and social participation, FRAILIFE speaks to both general family processes and the special case of Europe’s frailest families. The existing literature on families with a disabled child is scattered, built on small convenience samples, and often focused on a specific disease; the findings are inconclusive and non-generalizable. FRAILIFE elevates the evidentiary standard by: i) using a population approach, which compares families with and without a disabled child and provides opportunities to uncover heterogeneous effects; ii) going beyond simple associations between child disability and family outcomes to establish causal pathways, identify underlying mechanisms, and uncover causal effects; iii) investigating both short- and long-term consequences of child disability on families; iv) adopting a comparative perspective to uncover the moderating effects of institutions and culture. Beyond the specific insights about the networked consequences of disability, this project contributes to the field of family demography, as the analysis of extremely frail families has relevance for the general functioning of all families facing adverse events. FRAILIFE will bring families with a disabled child out of their invisibility, offering new and important insights on their functioning, characteristics, and challenges, while informing effective family-centered policy. **This website area is part of a project that has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme** **(Grant agreement No. 101077533)** ## Research Team ### Nicoletta Balbo - PI Nicoletta Balbo is the Principal Investigator of the FRALIFE project and Associate Professor of Sociology at the Social and Political Sciences Department, Bocconi University. She is also Research Fellow at the DONDENA Centre for Research on Social Dynamics and Public Policy. Her research interests focus on sociology of the family, life course, fertility decision-making, health behaviors and disability. Her research is therefore at the intersection between sociology, demography and public health. Nicoletta has published in leading demographic and sociological journals, such as Demography and American Sociological Review. [About](https://sps.unibocconi.eu/people/nicoletta-balbo) ### Silvia Palmaccio - Postdoc Silvia Palmaccio joined the FRAILIFE team in October 2024 as a full-time postdoctoral researcher. She holds a Ph.D. in Economics from KU Leuven, Belgium, and is an affiliated researcher at KU Leuven and University of Turin. Her research interests lie at the intersection of family and education economics. [About](https://www.silviapalmaccio.com/) ### Mauro Martinelli - Postdoc Mauro Martinelli is a postdoctoral researcher on the FRAILIFE team

[About](https://martinellimauro.github.io/) ### Margherita Moretti - Postdoc Margherita Moretti is a postdoctoral researcher on the FRAILIFE team since June 2025. She holds a Ph.D. in Demography from Sapienza University and is affiliated with the Helsinki Institute for Demography and Population Health, and the Max Planck – University of Helsinki Center for Social Inequalities in Population Health. Her main research interests relate to population health and mortality, the associated socioeconomic inequalities, and their links to family, intergenerational relationships, and kinship structures, including kin availability, loss, and health status. title: IMMUNE: Modelling the Impact of Human Behaviours on Infections Spread | Bocconi University
text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # IMMUNE: Modelling the Impact of Human Behaviours on Infections Spread **Grant:** ERC Consolidator Grant, €1.9 million **Principal Investigator:** Prof. Alessia Melegaro **Period:** 2021-2026 IMMUNE is a project meant to incorporate dynamic human behavior and, particularly, vaccination decisions into epidemiological models. In the envisaged new models, these elements can change as a function of internal and external factors, such as disease dynamics, vaccine availability and vaccine scares, panic, social norms and peer effects. The project, submitted to the European Research Council before the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic hit the European context, focuses on vaccine hesitancy, its determinants and its public health consequences. In 2019 the United States reported its highest number of measles cases in 25 years, while four countries in Europe - Albania, Czechia, Greece and the United Kingdom – lost their measles elimination status in 2018 following protracted outbreaks of the disease. Reports indicate that the leading causes of vaccine hesitancy are the fear of vaccine side effects, the perceived low risk of vaccine-preventable diseases, and the mistrust in health care providers. Unfortunately, providing corrective information on vaccine safety, debunking vaccine myths (such as the link between vaccines and autism) and providing information on the dangers of contracting infectious diseases has been shown to be ineffective and might even reduce vaccination intentions. Triggering altruistic behavior when the coverage level is above herd immunity and the incentive to free-ride is high and making childhood vaccinations compulsory are other approaches that are being explored. The individual’s use of the Internet provides unprecedented opportunities to investigate collective social phenomena. Micro-blogging analysis and digital monitoring sources are recognized as key information to study socio-demographic processes and human behavior and, in particular, to comprehend individuals’ sentiment towards vaccination. In parallel, mechanistic transmission models have benefited from computational advances and extensive availability of data on the mobility and sociodemographic structure of human populations. Therefore, the purpose of IMMUNE is to fill in this gap, understanding the determinants of demand for vaccine, the channels through which the information is gathered, the decision process, and the impact this will have on disease epidemiology and associated risk. The large amount of data collected during the COVID pandemic will also allow the research team to study the effects of other forms of behavior variability, such as those concerning the rules of social distancing and use of face masks, which affect the spread of a disease. **This website area is part of a project that has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme** **(Grant agreement No. 101003183)** ![ERC logo](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/images/ERC-logo.jpg) ### Discover More - [People](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/project-members-0) - [Results](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/results-0) - [Contacts](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/contacts-0) "Show all")

title: INTEGRATOR | Bocconi University
text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # INTEGRATOR **Project acronym and title** **INTEGRATOR**– Incorporating Demographic Factors into Natural Language Processing Models **Project summary** INTEGRATOR **introduces demographic factors into language processing systems**, which will improve algorithmic performance, avoid racism, sexism, and ageism, and open up new applications. What if I wrote that “winning an ERC Grant, Dirk Hovy got a sick result?”. Those familiar with the use of “sick” as a synonym for “great” or “awesome” among teenagers would think that Bocconi Knowledge hired a very young writer (or someone posing as such). The rest would think I went crazy. Current artificial intelligence-based language systems wouldn’t have a clue. “Natural language processing (NLP) technologies,” Prof. Hovy says, “fail to account for demographics both in understanding language and in generating it. And this failure prevents us from reaching human-like performance. It limits possible future applications and it introduces systematic bias against underrepresented demographic groups”. **Project description** The goal of INTEGRATOR is to develop novel data sets, theories, and algorithms to incorporate demographic factors into language technology. This will improve performance of existing tools for all users, reduce demographic bias, and enable completely new applications. Language reflects demographic factors like our age, gender, etc. People actively use this information to make inferences, but current language technology (NLP) fails to account for demographics, both in language understanding (e.g., sentiment analysis) and generation (e.g., chatbots). This failure prevents us from reaching human-like performance, limits possible future applications, and introduces systematic bias against underrepresented demographic groups. Solving demographic bias is one of the greatest challenges for current language technology. Failing to do so will limit the field and harm public trust in it. Bias in AI systems recently emerged as a severe problem for privacy, fairness, and ethics of AI. It is especially prevalent in language technology, due to language's rich demographic information. Since NLP is ubiquitous (translation, search, personal assistants, etc.), demographically biased models creates uneven access to vital technology. Despite increased interest in demographics in NLP, there are no concerted efforts to integrate it: no theory, data sets, or algorithmic solutions. INTEGRATOR will address these by identifying which demographic factors affect NLP systems, devising a bias taxonomy and metrics, and creating new data. These will enable us to use transfer and reinforcement learning methods to build demographically aware input representations and systems that incorporate demographics to improve performance and reduce bias. Demographically aware NLP will lead to high-performing, fair systems for text analysis and generation. This ground-breaking research advances our understanding of NLP, algorithmic fairness, and bias in AI, and creates new research resources and avenues. title: LOSS | Bocconi University
text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # LOSS **Grant:** ERC Consolidator Grant, €1.99 million **Principal Investigator:** Prof. Catherine De Vries Period **:** 2020-2025 The key aim of the **LOSS** project is to unravel: How economic hardship affects support for socially conservative political agendas aimed at restricting the rights of marginalised groups (ethnic linguistic and religious minorities migrants LGBTQIA + and women) and how local and national policy contexts affect this relationship. Many European societies have recently experienced growin"g prejudice towards marginalised groups and the rise in support for far-right parties advocating to restrict the rights of these groups. These developments threaten the cohesion of national and local communities across Europe. While aggregate level evidence suggests that financial crises generally coincide with increased support for far-right parties we do not understand why this happens. By developing a groundbreaking interdisciplinary theoretical framework that integrates insights about the role of loss from political science sociology social psychology and behavioural economics the LOSS project contends that experiences of economic hardship translate into specific narratives of loss that in turn trigger support for social conservative political agendas. To empirically examine the importance of narratives of loss the LOSS project employs an innovative multi-method empirical approach combining qualitative and quantitative research methodologies. To uncover the role of context the project compares five European countries (Italy, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden and the United Kingdom) that vary in the level of compensation provided for economic hardship and local contexts within these countries. More about the project: [**"How Economic Hardship Fuels Support for the Far Right"**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/news/how-economic-hardship-fuels-support-far-right) _Bocconi Knowledge_ _This website area is part of a project that has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme_ _(Grant agreement No. 864687)_ _![ERC logo](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/images/ERC-logo.jpg)_ ### Discover More - [People](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/project-members-1) - [Results](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/results-1) - [Contacts](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/contacts-1) [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/loss#addtoany "Show all")

text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # Project Members **Principal Investigator** ![Catherine De Vries](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/images/catherine-de-vries.jpeg)**[Catherine De Vries](https://www.catherinedevries.eu/)** is Dean and Professor of Political Science at Bocconi University, and she is also a Research Associate at the Dondena Centre for Research on Social Dynamics and Public Policy. Her work can be broadly situated in the areas political behaviour, political economy and EU politics, and has appeared in leading political science journals, such as the American Political Science Review and Annual Review of Political Science, and university presses, Oxford and Princeton University Press. Research Team **[![Simone Cremaschi](https://simonecremaschi.com/)** is a Postdoctoral Fellow in Political Sociology at the Dondena Centre for Research on Social Dynamics and Public Policy where he works on the European Research Council Project LOSS. More broadly, his research addresses immigrant marginalization, intergroup relations, and the social determinants of political behaviour. He holds a Ph.D. in Political and Social Sciences from the European University Institute. **![Paula Rettl](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/images/paula-rettl.JPG)[Paula Rettl](https://paularettl.github.io/)** is a Ph.D. Candidate at the Department of Social and Political Sciences at Bocconi University (Milan). Her research lies at the intersection of political economy and comparative political behavior. In particular, her research focuses on how material self-interest shapes political behavior, often in unexpected ways. She studies this topic by testing new arguments with quasi-experimental designs and survey experiments. Her regional focus is on Latin America and Europe, where she lived for extended periods. In June 2020, Paula joined the Dondena Centre as a Research Associate for the LOSS project. **![Renu Singh](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/images/renu-singh.png)[Renu Singh](https://www.renu-singh.com/)** is a faculty member in the Department of Social and Political Sciences and a research fellow at the DONDENA Centre for Research on Social Dynamics and Public Policy at Bocconi University. She has been working with the LOSS project team since March 2022. Renu is also a scholar at the O’Neill Institute for National and Global Health Law at Georgetown and an executive board member for the International Studies Association Global Health Studies Section. Previously, Renu was a research assistant professor at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology and a Fulbright fellow at the Hertie School in Berlin. Her research is motivated by interests in the relationship between political institutions, public opinion, and policy change in the context of public health policy, science policy, and global health security and governance. Renu work has been published or is forthcoming in _BMJ Global_ _Health_, _International Studies Quarterly_, the _Journal of Health_ _Politics, Policy and Law_, and _Cleaner and Responsible Consumption_, among others. Renu has a BA in Political Science and a BS in Microbiology from UMass Amherst, an MS in Public Policy and Administration from LSE, and an MA and PhD in Government from Georgetown. **![Nicola Bariletto](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/images/nicola_bariletto.jpeg)****Nicola Bariletto** is a pre-doctoral research assistant for the ERC LOSS project hosted by the Dondena research center. Previously, he was faculty at the University of Copenhagen, got a PhD from USC’s Information Sciences Institute, and a linguistics master’s in Germany. Dirk is interested in the interaction between language, society, and machine learning, or what language can tell us about society, and what computers can tell us about language. He is also interested in ethical questions of bias and algorithmic fairness in machine learning. He has authored over [70 articles](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=7xluaTAAAAAJ&hl=it&oi=ao) on these topics, including 3 best paper awards, and a tetxbook on [NLP in Dirk has co-founded and organized several workshops (on computational social science, and [ethics in NLP](https://ethicsinnlp.com/)), and was a local organizer for the EMNLP 2017 conference. **Research Team** **![Amanda Cercas Curry picture](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/images/Cercas-Curry.jpg) Amanda Cercas Curry** is a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at Bocconi University. Her research interests mainly focus on Natural Language Processing, specifically on open-domain conversational systems, their social impact and how we can develop more ethical AI across disciplines. During her PhD, she worked on abuse detection and mitigation in dialogue systems particularly when it comes to female digital assitants. text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # Results Publications [**How Foundational Narratives Shape European Union Politics**](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/JCMS-Lecture_Final.pdf) **Catherine E. De Vries (2022)** Accepted for publication in JCMS: Journal of Common Market Studies, forthcoming in 2023 Working papers [**Geographies of Discontent: How Public Service Deprivation Increased Far-Right Support in Italy**](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/Paper_Public_Services-19.pdf) **Simone Cremaschi, Paula Rettl, Marco Cappelluti, Catherine E. De Vries (2022)** Electoral support for far-right parties is often linked to specific geographies of discontent. We argue that public service deprivation, defined as poor access to public services at the local level, helps explain these patterns in far-right support. Public service deprivation increases the appeal of far-right parties by making people more worried about immigration and increased competition for reduced public services. We examine our argument using three studies from Italy, a country home to some of the most electorally successful far-right parties in the past decades. We examine cross-sectional data from municipalities (study 1), exploit a national reform forcing municipalities below a certain population threshold to jointly share local public services (study 2), and explore geo-coded individual-level election survey data (study 3). Our findings suggest that public service deprivation helps us better understand geographical differences in far-right support and the mechanisms underlying it. [**The Effects of a Wall: Gender Attitudes and Political Involvement in Unified Germany.**](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/Wall_Oct2022.pdf) **Catherine E. De Vries and Diana O'Brien (2022)** Why are women less politically involved than men? Scholars posit that gender (in)egalitarian attitudes are an important determinant of women’s engagement and participation. Yet, existing work finds only mixed support for this claim. Using the German General Social Survey (1991-2016), we examine the impact of gender egalitarian attitudes on political interest and involvement across birth cohorts from East and West Germany. We find that traditional gender attitudes are on average negatively correlated with political participation and engagement, especially among women. Women who hold gender egalitarian attitudes, in contrast, are nearly as involved in politics as their male counterparts. We then show that this finding holds when instrumenting for gender attitudes, and identify a possible individual-level mechanism underlying our findings: women’s access to education. Together, these results reveal an important barrier to gender equality and inform debates about the persistent gender gap in political involvement. [**An Anti-Feminist Backlash? Female Labour Market Participation and Gender Conservatism in Europe**]( **Paula Rettl, Simone Cremaschi, Catherine E. De Vries (2022)** This study examines how increased participation of women in the labor market affects egalitarian gender attitudes in society. We argue that increased female labor market participation might generate a anti-feminist backlash, because it triggers grievances for certain men and women. For men, increased female labor force participation intensifies competition in the labor market, especially among those who are already economically vulnerable (labor market competition channel). For women, increased female labor force participation might be also be threatening when they are not financially independent or married and thus worry about the employment of men in their household (household accounting channel). We test these conjectures in two studies. The first study uses European Social Survey data

[**​Age-Based Polarization in a Time of Ageing.**](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/IntergenerationalPolarizationCOVID-3.pdf) **Paula Rettl, Catherine E. De Vries and Francesco Billari (2022)** Across the globe, many societies are undergoing an unprecedented process of population ageing. While the share of working age people (20-64 year old) is shrinking, the share of elderly people (65 year old) is rapidly increasing. While age effects on preference formation and political behaviour are well documented, we know much less about the consequences of population ageing. We argue that while the potential for age-based polarization is generally muted due life cycle effects and family bonds, when societies age and resource competition between age groups increases, polarization between age groups is expected to increase. We examine our argument based on two studies. First, we examine existing cross-sectional survey data from over 20 European countries (study 1) to show that age-based polarization is correlated with population ageing. Second, we aim to gain causal leverage, and examine our proposed mechanism based on resource competition, using two novel survey experiments conducted during the first and second wave of the COVID-19 pandemic (study 2). Overall, our evidence suggests that increased resource competition due to population ageing has the potential to increase age-based polarization in society. (2022)** Do wartime experiences other than violence leave long-lasting political legacies? How are these legacies kept and sustained across generations and beyond those who directly experienced war? We explore these questions in Italy, a country whose democratic institutions were forged in the aftermath of a civil war fought between 1943 and 1945 by an armed resistance movement against Nazi and Fascist forces. We argue that the local presence and activity of resistance bands left anti-Nazi/Fascist legacies that shape political attitudes and behaviors today. Furthermore, we propose that these legacies are kept alive via a process of inter-generational, community-based transmission sustained on core mechanisms: (1) _memorialization_ recomposes the resistance experience into a coherent narrative that legitimizes winners and condemns losers, (2) _local anchors_ strengthen the narrative's local resonance and self-identification, and (3) _local associational networks_ maintain and reinforce this narrative and build on it to mobilize community members. We empirically explore this argument by exploiting novel data from a recent nationwide, grassroots mobilization campaign – the "Anti-Fascist Law" – aimed at banning neo-fascist propaganda. We use an integrative multi-method research design that combines statistical analysis of all Italian municipalities to make sense of the campaign's spatial patterns, with a within-case analysis of a purposively selected locality to trace the process by which legacies are kept and transmitted across generations. Our study emphasizes armed resistance as a critical source of war's long-term political legacies and improves our understanding of the mechanisms underlying the collective transmission of political memories. **Self-built Segregation, Shelter Strategies, and the Immigrant Poor** **Simone Cremaschi (2022)** How do the immigrant poor decide where to live? text: (2022)** How do the immigrant poor decide where to live? Sociologists have emphasized economic considerations to explain sorting between segregated and integrated neighborhoods. Drawing on 6 months of ethnographic fieldwork, 33 interviews, and 462 survey questionnaires collected in immigrant shantytowns in Italy, this article proposes that immigrants strategically choose between similarly marginal arrangements to maintain a positive sense of themselves. Most housing-insecure immigrants move between makeshift housing, acquaintances' houses, and public shelters in an effort to ensure future stability. Others withdraw into shantytowns for the long term, giving up hopes of inclusion and finding worth in their ability to survive without support. Building, following, and adapting "shelter strategies" allows immigrants to meet basic needs while maintaining their self-worth, but it also constrains their location choices, which helps explain how extreme socio-spatial segregation emerges and continues indefinitely. title: SAIM - A Scientific Approach to Innovation Management | Bocconi University
text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # SAIM - A Scientific Approach to Innovation Management **Grant:** ERC Advanced Grant, €1.9 million **Principal Investigator:** Prof. Alfonso Gambardella **Period:** 2021-2026 The goal of our research program is to test how and under what circumstances a "scientific" approach to decision making helps entrepreneurs and managers make more effective decisions. This approach starts with a good framing of the problem, develops models or theories that predict the outcomes of actions from logical connections between antecedents and consequences, and tests the theory using existing data or data drawn from well-defined experimental designs. We call this approach “scientific” because it overlaps to a good extent with the approach that scientists use to develop new knowledge. **This website area is part of a project that has received funding from the European Research Council (ERC) under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme** **(Grant agreement No. 101021061)** ### Discover More - [People](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/project-members-0) - [Results](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/results-0) - [Contacts](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research/erc-projects/contacts-0) "Show all")

title: Spoils of War: The Economic Consequences of the Great War in Central Europe | Bocconi University
text: Faculty and Research Research [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/faculty-and-research/research) # Spoils of War: The Economic Consequences of the Great War in Central Europe **Grant:** ERC Starting Grant, €1.49 million **Principal Investigator:** Prof. Tamás Vonyó **Period:** 2019-2024 ## The Economic Consequences of the Great War in Central Europe Spoils _of_ WAR was a collaborative research project in economic and business history awarded an ERC Horizon 2020 Starting Grant in 2018. It was hosted by the Dondena Center between 2019 and 2025. We studied economic development and industrialization in Central Europe in the late 19th and early 20th century, examining the developmental consequences of the Habsburg Empire and its disintegration after World War I. ## About Us The Project Austria-Hungary captivated generations of economic historians, for whom it promoted modern industries, modern banks and international trade. Recent comparative research revised these seminal assessments. Central Europe was economically weakly integrated, relatively backward and continued to fall behind Western industrial nations until World War I. This development gap delayed industrialization and the rise of big business. The economic impact of political disintegration in Central Europe concerned prominent contemporaries between the world wars and has long been debated by historians. These debates reached no firm conclusions. New scholarship relied on old accounts, outdated analytical approaches could not distinguish the confounding effects of changing borders, wartime disruptions and historical conditions, and a predominantly macroeconomic approach overlooked the differential impact of wartime and post-war transformations between regions, industries and individual firms. Spoils _of_ WAR aimed at filling this knowledge gap. Based on a herculean data collection effort in which we amassed regional, local and firm-level statistics from historical sources, we used modern empirical tools to assess regional economic development and the legacies of complex border effects. We examined the impact of German immigration on agricultural advancement in Hungary and of colonial railways in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the level and spatial concentration manufacturing in the Habsburg Empire before World War I. We explored the persistent socio-economics legacies of the Habsburg Military Border and economic integration within changing borders in Southeast Europe. We traced income inequality in both national and comparative contexts. Finally, we built a novel and comprehensive database of industrial war contractors to assess industrial concentration and mobilization in Austria-Hungary during the Great War and to examine the growth of big industry in Central Europe from the 1900s to the 1930s. ## Team ### Tamás Vonyó, Principal Investigator Associate Professor of Economic History, Department of Social and Political Sciences Tamás Vonyó received his PhD from the University of Oxford in 2011. He held positions at the London School of Economics and the Groningen Growth and Development Centre. He is research fellow of the Centre for Economic Policy Research and trustee of the European Historical Economics Society. His research has focused on the history of modern economic growth and the economic history of the world wars, especially in the context of Central and Eastern Europe. He is author of The Economic Consequences of the War: West Germany’s Growth Miracle after 1945, published by Cambridge

He held another postdoc position at Princeton University and a departmental lectureship at the University of Oxford. He received his PhD from the University of Chicago in 2018. His research has bridged a range of topics in comparative politics and historical political economy, particularly the developmental legacies of empires in Central and Southeast Europe. He is author to Imperial Borderlands: Institutions and Legacies of the Habsburg Military Frontier, published by Cambridge University Press. His new book, Islam, Sultans, and the Printing Press: How Absence of the Printed Word Limited Development re-examines the familiar role of religion in underdevelopment. She subsequently held research fellowships at the University of Konstanz and Humboldt University in Berlin. She joined SpoilsofWAR in 2022. Her research has focused on the development of leading firms and cartels in the electrotechnical and machine building industry and the history of electrification in Central Europe. text: the Habsburg Military Cambridge Studies in Economic History. Cambridge University Press. Extractive institutions are key features of colonialism whereby historical states exploited local populations for the benefit of the former. _Imperial Borderlands_ reveals that extractive institutions are not monolithic but entail a variety of dimensions that can directly impact development. The book proposes a conceptual framework to assess the ambivalent effect of extractive institutions, which depends on the three factors: investment, property rights, and violence. The worst outcomes for development are cases of extractivism with low state investment in infrastructure, high transformation of local society by removing property rights, and high physical coercion. To substantiate these claims, _Imperial Borderlands_ employs an interdisciplinary approach that integrates historical narrative with econometric analysis to trace the evolution of military colonialism, an institution that the Austrian Habsburgs created in the 16th century and maintained for another two hundred years in the extensive southern border of their vast territorial empire. B. Popescu (2023), [The developmental legacies of border buffer zones: the case of military colonialism](https://www.nowpublishers.com/article/Details/HPE-0045), _Journal of Historical Political Economy_ 3 (1): 31-63. How do countries in conflict manage their borders and what are the long-term implications? Little literature focuses on the developmental legacies of military buffer zones. The Habsburg Empire maintained for centuries military colonies along its southern border, where local populations provided military service in exchange for land. Using a geographic regression discontinuity design, I show that municipalities in modern-day Croatia within the former military colony have had less investment in infrastructure, lower interpersonal trust, and weaker trust in formal institutions. I argue that the intensity of imperial investment, the transformation and/or reorganization of local societies, and labor market inflexibility are key determinants in shaping these developmental legacies both in the short and long-run. S. Nikolic (with D. Chilosi), Vanishing borders: ethnicity and trade costs at the origin of the Yugoslav market, _Journal of Economic History_, accepted and forthcoming. - [EHES working paper](https://ehes.org/wp/EHES_214.pdf) This article exploits the creation of a paradigmatic multi-ethnic state, Yugoslavia, to examine whether the effect of ethnic identity on trade costs persists when borders change. We rely on a panel of over 550,000 inter-urban price gaps spanning the area of Yugoslavia before and after Yugoslav unification of 1918. Controlling for transport costs and import tariffs, we find a large but transitory border effect. Ethno-religious differences initially significantly increased trade costs, but their negative influence vanished over time, too. The decline began about twelve years before unification, involved also city-pairs that were not divided by the border, and was particularly marked in places where Yugoslav unification enjoyed strong support. These patterns support the hypothesis that Yugoslav nationalism fostered trust across ethno-religious boundaries. Our results show that political movements can change patterns of ethnic identification of traders swiftly. ### **Regional Development** S. Nikolic & T. Vonyó (with M.
