The Service organizes one-on-one counseling meetings, monitors application processes, and is the point of contact for employers seeking candidates in this category. For more information, please visit the FAQ section on yoU@B > B in Touch > 'Inclusion, Disability and Wellbeing', where you can submit your inquiry. You may also contact the [Inclusion "Inclusion Service") office to request an interview and learn more about the available services. ## Students with SLDs, ADHD and Other Specific Needs Teaching and Exams The University provides technologies that support classroom learning and individual study, including [Sensus Access](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/campus/services/sensus-access "Sensus Access") (for converting documents into accessible alternative formats) and the Blackboard Ally plug-in, in addition to textbooks in digital format. Regarding exams, compensatory and dispensatory measures are assigned according to medical documentation, which may include extra time or the use of calculators or a computer. For more information, see the _Compensatory/Dispensatory Measures During Exams: Initial Request, Types and Deadlines_ paragraph of the [Guides to the University](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/guide-university "Guide all'Università") _._ Library Services The Bocconi Library is an institution authorized by the Italian Ministry of Culture to [produce accessible copies](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/about-us/accessibility-and-inclusion) of works protected by copyright for people with SLDs. Learning Needs Help Desk The [Desk](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/campus-life/learning-needs "Learning Needs") was established to provide every student with an SLD the chance to receive individual counseling on the best study strategies to tackle the university experience. Peer to Peer Tutoring Project This [service](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/campus-life/peer-peer-tutoring-project "Peer to Peer Tutoring Project") aims to improve and optimize study abilities through peer support, provided by student volunteers who have received specific training. You may contact the Academic Specific Needs office via B in Touch > Exams > Disability and Specific Needs. "Show all")

title: Inclusion, Disabilities and Learning Disorders | Bocconi University
text: Inclusion, Disabilities and Learning Disorders Overview # Inclusion, Disabilities and Learning Disorders The **Inclusion Service** is a point of reference that aims to guarantee the same opportunities to everyone: it collaborates with other offices on campus to create a connected and unified community where everyone – students, faculty, staff and alumni – can feel welcome and included. ![Student using automatic door on Bocconi ### Students with Disabilities, SLDs, ADHD and Other Specific Needs [Find Out ![Bocconi Anti-Discrimination Counselor talking to ### Anti-Discrimination Service Desk [Find Out ## Multiculturalism ### Multifaith Space A new Multifaith Space has opened, designed to ensure that all Bocconi community members have an appropriate place to pray, sit in silence or reflect. The entrance is located at Piazza Sraffa 6 (door on the left, first floor.) The space is open from Monday through Saturday 7:30am–10pm, and on Sunday 9am–10pm. ### Student Associations As of today, there are more than 100 student associations on campus, including ones representing various international communities. [Associations](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/campus-life/student-activities/student-associations "Student Associations") offer an opportunity to engage with people from different backgrounds who share common interests, thus becoming a point of reference and mutual support. ### Ethical-Religious Meals The offering of halal, kosher and vegan meals in dining areas underscores Bocconi's commitment to recognizing and supporting the dietary needs of the entire community. Options may be related to religious, ethical and/or cultural beliefs. [Find out more about our dining areas](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/funding/dining-areas-0 "Dining areas"). ## Gender Diversity [**Bocconi Carriera Alias (Identity "Bocconi Carriera Alias (Identity Regulation)") [**All-Gender Restrooms**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/campus/buildings-and-classrooms "All-Gender Restrooms ") ## Contact Us For general information check the FAQs at yoU@B> B in Touch> Inclusion, Disabilities and Wellbeing and submit your question. The [Inclusion "Inclusion Service") office is also available for information about accessibility, support for students with disabilities and other requirements, as well as other inclusion aspects. By the score for the written and the oral, you get the final mark out of thirty. The final score is calculated as follows: 75% written part + 25% oral part. When the result score is expressed to decimal places, the result is rounded up when the decimal place is greater or equal to 0,5. The written examination and oral examination correspond to two independent certifications provided separately. title: DIPLÔME DE FRANÇAIS PROFESSIONNEL | Bocconi University
text: Language Center [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center) # DIPLÔME DE FRANÇAIS PROFESSIONNEL Bocconi University is accredited test center for international certification of Business French, namely **DFP** **Affaires B1 and B2 level** issued by **CCI PARIS ILE-DE-FRANCE.** Registration is open to students from Bocconi and other Universities or Schools. Exam sessions are generally scheduled twice per year (Spring and Autumn Session). Registration fees: - DFP level B1, € 120 - DFP level B2, € 140 ## **How to register for the exam** The applicant must: 1\. pay the registration fee through the online procedure by the deadline for “Enrollment and payment period” scheduled for the session; registration is accepted only after payment; 2\. subimit the application (via the online procedure) during the "Enrollment and payment period" scheduled for the session The registration fee will not be refunded in the case of absence on the date of examination. ## **Exam location** Via Gobbi, 5 – Language Center ## **Exam format** The exam consists of two parts : - Written computer-based test (80’ for B1 level; 2 hours for B2 level) - Oral test (Preparation: 20' for B1 level, 15' for B2 level; Presentation: 10’ for B1 level, 15' for B2 level) [Further](https://www.lefrancaisdesaffaires.fr/tests-diplomes/diplomes-francais-professionnel-dfp/affaires/) [information](https://www.lefrancaisdesaffaires.fr/tests-diplomes/diplomes-francais-professionnel-dfp/affaires/) ## **Results** Those who have passed the exam will receive an email from CCIP Paris Ile-de-France with a link to download the certification available in electronic format only. Those who have not passed the exam will be notified by the Language Center. ## **Sessions** Please note that the date of each session will be confirmed only upon reaching a minimum number of registrations. As soon as the number is reached, the session will be marked " **CONFIRMED**". Otherwise, it will not take place and the registration fee will be refunded to all registered candidates. In addition, please note that **the registration fee will not be refunded in case of absence on the date of the exam**. - [**PAYMENT**](https://uni.bocconistore.it/buy_en/)(available only during the enrollment period indicated) - [**REGISTRATION FORM**](https://forms.unibocconi.it/index.php?rif_quest=798)(available only during the enrollment period indicated) For further information, it is possible to contact us in the following mode: - **Bocconi students**: via the **B in Touch** procedure available on the [yoU@B](mailto:yoU@B "mailto:you@b") Diary, topic LANGUAGES>Discover language certificates>"Is the University test center for language certificates?" - **Students from other Universities or Schools:** via the contact form available at this [link](https://forms.unibocconi.it/index.php?rif_quest=857) | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **Exam session** | **Exam date** | **Exam place** | **Registration period** | **Exam session confirmation** | | Spring 2026 | June 2026 (date TBD) | Language Lab | TBD | | "Show all")

title: General rules for registration in student’s academic career | Bocconi University
text: Language Center [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center) # General rules for registration in student’s academic career Foreign languages are classified as follows: - **“Curricular” languages (UE languages):** - such languages are usually registered in the academic career as first/second language; cpu are included in the standard 180 /120 /300 cpu of the study plan (please find in the [Guide to the detailed information about how to choose curricular languages, minimum exit levels and teaching services); - moreover, they can be registered in the academic career as “extra activities” (4 cpu); cpu are recorded on top of standard 180/120/300 cpu of the study plan. - **“Extra” languages:** - such languages can be registered in the academic career as “extra activities” only (4 cpu); therefore cpu are recorded on top of standard 180 /120 /300 cpu of the study plan. English, Italian, French, Spanish and German are “curricular” languages. Arabic, Chinese, Japanese, Russian are “extra” languages. Portuguese is: - “curricular” language up to a.y. 2018-19: it can be choosen as first /second language up to a.y. 2018-19; - “extra” language as of a.y. 2019-20: as of 2019-20 students (any cohort) cannot choose it as first/second language any more. International certifications (curricular and extra languages) can be registered in the academic curriculum provided that they are: - officially recognized by Bocconi University (see the list below); - submitted to the Administrative Office of the Language Center before the “expiry date” which is within 3 years after sitting the international certification exam (2 years for the international test TOEFL and – as of Sept 1st 2019 – for the IELTS test as well); - submitted by the owner of the international certification (who is required to show his/her personalized Bocconi ID card); - original certifications or statement of results (with stamp and signature of the certifying agency) only are allowed for submission. International certifications must be achieved and submitted for conversion by the study plan completion date relating to the selected Graduation session or, in any case, by the deadlines set to submit applications for the selected activities. We remind that it is not possible to request the recognition of an international certificate if the curricular exam of the same language has been recorded in the academic career, or even if the written exam has been passed with a sufficient grade, until the end of the exam session, which ends after the oral exam and the grade recording. When the result score of the International Certifying Agency is expressed to decimal places, the result is rounded up when the decimal place is greater than or equal to 5. For curricular languages, an international certification whose level/typology (general, business, legal) is equal to the minimum level/typology required can be registered in student's academic career. Furthermore, an international certification whose level/typology (general, business, legal) is higher than the minimum required can be registered in place of the minimum level/typology required (i.e. when the minimum level/typology required is B1 general, then a B1 business or B2 business or higher level/typology is

Furthermore, an international certification whose level/typology (general, business, legal) is higher than the minimum required can be registered in place of the minimum level/typology required (i.e. when the minimum level/typology required is B1 general, then a B1 business or B2 business or higher level/typology is allowed; when the minimum level/typology required is B1 business, then a B2 general or B2 business or higher level/typology is allowed). Please note that the level/typology recorded in the academic curriculum is the level/typology stated by the Certifying Agency on the international certification. text: Language Center [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center) # Language Certification Recognition **Instructions to submit the request of recognition of a language certification for students enrolled in former cohorts** **(before the 2014-15 cohort in BSc Programs and CLMG and before 2018-19 cohort in MSc Programs):** - Fill out entirely the **form** available at this [link](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/ING-form-registrazione-certificazioni-v2.pdf). - Print the form filled out, sign it, specify the date and make a scan of it. - Send a scan of it with date and original signature together with a scan of the certification, using the B in Touch procedure available in the yoU@B Diary, topic: "LANGUAGES > Discover language certifications". - **Wait for the reply** by the Language Center which will indicate the outcome of the application submitted. If the form has been completed correctly and the conversion request is accepted, the grade out of 30 resulting from the conversion will be recorded indicatively within two weeks than the request date. If the form is completed incorrectly, the student will receive indication about it and he/she will have to submit a new request attaching again the form and scanned copy of the certification. It is specified that the **date of submission of the complete and correct request** must be indicated on the form. In case of inconsistency, the certification will be recorded with the **date corresponding to the complete and correct request submission**. "Show all")

title: Language Certification Recognition | Bocconi University
text: Language Center [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center) # Language Certification Recognition **The student who intends to apply for the recognition of a language certification as an alternative to the internal exam for curricular languages or as additional course, also with reference to extracurricular languages for which there is no internal exam, must follow the new procedure described below**: 1\. Verify that the certification to be recognized respects the **defined parameters**, specifically that: - the certification is listed in the ones **recognized by Bocconi**(see list of certifications and conversion tables below) - the certification can be verified online - the certification is of a **level equal to or higher** than required level. Please check information on curricular languages ​​and levels in the “Foreign Languages” chapter of the [Guide to the University](https://www.unibocconi.eu/studentguide) of your Study Program and the rules available in the "General rules for registration in student’s academic career") section) Moreover, the language certification recognition request must be submitted **within 3 years** after the date of the certification test ( **2 years** for TOEFL; **IELTS can be recognized from two years from the original test date even when it is an "IELTS One Skill retake" certification**; Goethe Zertifikat and OSD **can be recognized only if the four skills have been taken on one single date or across one year**. In any case, the certification recognition request **must be submitted within 3 years after the 1st module test sitting date**, in the event the certification has been completed in different dates). 2. **Check the grade** by consulting the tables available on below link: - [Certifications recognized for the Bachelor of Science Programs]( - [Certifications recognized for the Integrated Master of Arts in Law]( - [Certifications recognized for the Master of Science Programs]( 3\. **Submit the language certification recognition request**: exams can be recorded on the transcript starting in the enrollment in the year of studies the language subject of recognition is positioned in by filling out the application via the “ **Language certification recognition” procedure** available on the yoU@B “Language Center” widget. In the language certification recognition procedure, it is possible to download (in pdf format, no larger than 2MB): - a scan of the certificate, or - the statement of results, or - a screenshot of the online results, also including student's name and surname, certification test date and certification reference code. 4. **Wait for the reply** by the Language Center which will indicate the outcome of the application submitted through the above-mentioned procedure. It is specified that **the student has the responsibility** to carefully check the recognized certifications and rules for conversion, before submitting certification request of recognition. Submitting a certification request of conversion DOES NOT IMPLY that the application will be accepted by the Language Center. If the conversion request via the “Language certification recognition” procedure has been completed correctly and has been accepted, the grade out of 30 (or PASS for the Professional English Seminars) resulting from the conversion will be recorded indicatively within 10 working days than the request date (the

title: Language Exchange | Bocconi University
text: Language Center [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center) # Language Exchange The Language Center organizes each semester a Language Exchange for students; it is a good chance to improve a language through talking. ## **What is it?** The Language Exchange is a form of **autonomous language learning**. It is based on a mutual exchange between learners, speaking different languages in order to learn one from the other. ## **Who can participate in the Language Exchange?** The initiative is open to students enrolled in Bachelor, Master of Science, Integrated Master of Arts in Law programs and Specialized Master Programs, Exchange incoming students who already have **at least an elementary level (A2)** in the language which they would like to improve. They must be at least B2 level or mother tongue for the other exchange language. ## **When and how is possible to take part in the Language Exchange?** The Language Exchange is offered at the beginning of every semester. It will be possible to fill in the registration form on the yoU@B Student Diary, in the Language Center widget. For 2nd semester 2025-26, registrations will be open **from January 26th to February 16th 2026**. ## **How will I be informed of the name and email address of my language partner?** The information regarding your language partner, will be sent by **Bocconi email address**. ## **Is there a minimum duration for the Language Exchange?** There is not but, for the effectiveness of the initiative, we recommend to schedule weekly meetings with a duration not inferior than three months. ## **When can I meet my partner?** You and your partner can decide autonomously when to meet. ## **Who should we contact for help/support during the Language Exchange?** You can request support from the Language Lab through the B in Touch procedure available on the yoU@B Student Diary (topic: LANGUAGES > Various). ## **Is there a test at the end of the Language Exchange?** No, there is no test. At the end of the program each partner should fill in a feedback form. "Show all")

text: Language Center [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center) # Italian Survival Course Online The Language Center offers a short intensive Italian language course in distance to help foreign students interact during their first days in Italy and facilitate their integration at Bocconi. title: Supplementary Activities | Bocconi University
text: Language Center [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center) # Supplementary Activities The **Language Center** offers free courses for Bocconi students, including: - Language and culture courses - Introductory language courses - Courses to prepare for international certifications, available for both curricular and extracurricular languages - Workshops aimed at enhancing students’ academic and professional skills in English (Soft Skills Workshops) - A short online course covering the basics of the Italian language (Italian Survival Course) ## **Enrollment** **Courses** are **open to** a limited number of Bocconi students of **all Programs**, University specialized Masters, SDA Masters and PhDs, **except for the "Italian Survival Course"** online **,** which is open to first-year students (BSc, MSc, Masters) and Double Degree Incoming students with unlimited places available. Students can **enroll exclusively through the you@B Diary**, in the **“sign-up for various activities” box**. Before registering, students are strongly advised to **carefully read the complete course calendar** to avoid possible overlaps with other classes or activities. Please note that **cancellations** can only be made through the yoU@B Student Diary **within**(and not after) **the deadline indicated for the registration**. No other type of cancellation request will be accepted. Students who have not properly completed the registration process cannot be admitted to the courses. ## **Available seats** Details for each course are published online on the corresponding page (“Course details and calendar”). **Enrollment will be confirmed through a message in the yoU@B Diary** a few days before the course begins. ## **Attending and obtaining the open badge** Courses **do not grant academic credits** or additional points for graduation. **There is no final exam**. Students who attend **at least 75%** of the academic hours of the course **\*** receive an **Open Badge of Attendance** approximately 30 days after the course ends. **Attendance** is recorded at the beginning of each class through a **numeric code** provided by the instructor. **The code is valid for 10 minutes only**. **Any attendance recorded after this time will not be considered valid** and will count as an absence. Students are not allowed to leave the classroom before the end of the lesson. Any improper conduct will be sanctioned in accordance with the Università Bocconi Honor Code. **\*Exception**: theItalian Survival Course (delivered online in asynchronous mode) does not include attendance tracking and therefore does not issue an Open Badge of Attendance. ## **Exclusion list** If you are registered for a course but you **do not attend at least 25%** of the scheduled hours, you will not be able to register to any other Language Center extracurricular activity during the same semester and the following one. **Being placed on the Exclusion List twice** leads to **permanent exclusion** from Language Center supplementary activities. \* **Exception**: there is no exclusion list for the "Italian Survival Course". title: Responsible use of online resources | Bocconi University
text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Responsible use of online resources The majority of electronic resources (databases, e-journals, e-books) made available through the Bocconi Library are governed by license agreements between the Library and publishers or vendors. These define specific terms and conditions of use, i.e. authorized users, permissions and restrictions. **Access to the licensed online resources is for educational and research use only.** Here you can find a list of usually permitted and not permitted uses: - **Displaying, searching, downloading, printing and storing the licensed material** for scholarly research, educational and personal use only - **Creating a temporary link** to a journal article or a book/book chapter for use in electronic course packs or learning management systems provided proper reference to the author and source is given, and with the authorization of the Library (only authorized users can access it) - **Sharing your own IDs and password** with third parties, nor to enable anyone other than authorized user to use the licensed material - **Distributing or transmitting** (by whatever means, e.g. fax, e-mail, social networks, etc.) the licensed material to anyone other than authorized users - title: Consulting a Thesis | Bocconi University
text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Consulting a Thesis Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) [Using the Library](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/using-library) [Teaching and Research Support](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support) [What's on](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/whats) Highlights [Opening Hours](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/opening-hours) [Get in Touch](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/get-touch) [Suggestions and Complaints](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/suggestions-and-complaints) The Bocconi Library holds all the dissertations discussed at the University since the foundation, except for those related to bachelor's degree programs. This is a valuable collection that contributes to outlining the history of our University, weaving the thread of national and international history with that of the individual stories of Bocconi graduates. You can explore dissertations in the [Collections](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/collectionDiscovery?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1) tab, where you can find: - [**Bocconi University Dissertations all dissertations discussed at Bocconi University since 1977, divided between [**Dissertations and [**Dissertations Within each group you will find two boxes, one for the theses for which the author has authorized consultation ( **Authorized Dissertations**), another for those for which consultation has not been authorized ( **Unauthorized Dissertations**). In the latter case you will be able to see details about the dissertations (title, author, advisor, year), but not read the content. - [**Bocconi University Historical that contains the texts of all the theses discussed at the University from 1906 to 1977. The dissertations are displayed according to a timeline that accompanies significant moments in the history of the University and its community. Historical dissertations are undergoing an important process of restoration and digitization for preservation purposes. This project is currently in progress and has been made possible thanks to the support of generous donors. - [**Bocconi University PhD dissertations "Bocconi University PhD dissertations 1995-2002"), that collects PhD dissertations discussed at Bocconi University between 1995 and 2002. #### **How do I search for a dissertation?** Use the search bar in each section or scroll through the titles and choose the ones that interest you most. Either way, we suggest you to start with the sign in. You can also search for dissertations in [SearchLib](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/search?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1&lang=en) by author (student name or supervisor name), title or keywords within the title, but you will only be able to read dissertations for which the author has given permission for consultation. We suggest you to consult the Libguide [Consulting Dissertations](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/consulting-dissertations) to best set up your research strategies. #### **Can I read dissertations in the Library?** Sure! Theses can be consulted in the Library from the dedicated workstation in Data Room 016, located on the Library ground floor. To consult print dissertations, you may request them through [SearchLib](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/search?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1&lang=en "SearchLib"); once your request is submitted, we will contact you to schedule an appointment for assisted consultation. #### **What if I am off campus?** If you are a student or Faculty member, you can consult the theses even when you are off campus at any time. Simply sign in and ... enjoy your reading! Please note: all theses are subject to current legislation on [copyright and intellectual property rights](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/copyright "copyright and intellectual property rights"). text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Catalogues of Donations ### [Rodolfo Banfi Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/catalogobanfi.pdf "Rodolfo Banfi Collection") The collection contains about 300 works and it was donated to the Library between 2005 and 2009. Rodolfo Banfi (1919 – 1992) worked at Banca Commerciale Italiana led by Raffaele Mattioli from 1946 to 1978, directing the COMIT’s Research Department from 1972 to 1978. In 1979, he became Chairman of Medio Credito Centrale. A board member of ISTAO, the R. Mattioli Foundation, Basinvest, ICE and the Corrente Foundation, he became Chairman of ATM Milano in December 1990. ### [Ferruccio Bolchini Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/lea-CatalogoBolchini.pdf "Ferruccio Bolchini Collection") The collection contains 440 works edited between the late 19th century and 1940, all of which focus on law. Ferruccio Bolchini (1875 - 1931), Professor of Civil Law at the University of Pavia from 1903 to 1925, he was Rector of Bocconi University from 1926 to 1930. ### [Ugo Caprara Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/lea-CatalogoCaprara.pdf "Ugo Caprara Collection") The collection contains 94 works edited between the late 19th century and 1940, which focus on business economics, accounting and business. Caprara (1894 - 1990) graduated from Bocconi in 1921 began his university career a year later as assistant to the Chair of Accounting and Business Management held by Professor Zappa. In later years, he was Professor of Business Management, retiring from academics in 1969. During his university career, he was asked to join the University Board, contributing to Bocconi’s continuous development. ### [Enrico Cernuschi Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/lea-CatalogoCernuschi.pdf "Enrico Cernuschi Collection") The collection contains around 720 works edited between the late 16th century and the late 19th century. Enrico Cernuschi (1821 – 1896) was a banker and Italian patriot, and a naturalized French citizen. As a banker, he is best known for his publications on finance issues, specifically related to the monetary system known as bimetallism. ### [Giordano Dell’Amore Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/lea-CatalogoDellAmore.pdf "Giordano Dell’Amore Collection") The collection contains more than 4000 works, edited between the early 19th century and 1980. Dell’Amore (1902 - 1981) graduated from Bocconi in 1923, he was Professor of Banking at Cattolica University in Milan. Professor of Management at Bocconi and Rector from 1967 to 1973, he was also Chairman of CARIPLO and the Lombardy Provincial Government. ### [Mauro Fasiani Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/lea-CatalogoFasiani.pdf "Mauro Fasiani Collection") The collection contains around 2100 monographs and periodicals focusing on public finance and financial law. Fasiani (1900-1950), an economist and Professor of Political Economy at the University of Turin, was a student of Luigi Einaudi. ### [Eugenio Greco Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/lea-CatalogoGreco.pdf "Eugenio Greco Collection") The collection contains around 3200 works edited between the late 18th century and 1950. In 1902, the year Bocconi University was founded, Professor Maglione asked Greco (1878 - 1959), to be his assistant to the Chair in General and Applied Accounting. He taught continuously until 1938. He held the Chairs in Business Management (1918 - 1920), Finance (1920 - 1925) and Accounting (1925 - 1938). ### [Giuseppe Luraghi Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/lea-CatalogoLuraghi.pdf "Giuseppe Luraghi Collection") The collection, donated to the University by the family in 2000, contains about 260 monographs and 53 periodicals. Editor-in-chief of Rivista di Diritto e procedura penale, at the end of his career he was Professor Emeritus of Corporate Criminal Law at Bocconi. ### [Ugo Pisa Collection](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/media/attachments/lea-CatalogoPisa.pdf "Ugo Pisa Collection") The collection contains about 250 documents edited between the late 18th century and 1940. title: The Ring of Shouts: Stock Exchanges in Italy Before Borsa Italiana in Milan | Bocconi University
text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # The Ring of Shouts: Stock Exchanges in Italy Before Borsa Italiana in Milan Before the establishment of the Borsa Italiana joint-stock company, headquartered in Milan in 1998, Italy was home to ten different stock exchanges located in Bologna, Florence, Genoa, Milan, Naples, Palermo, Rome, Turin, Trieste, and Venice. Each of these was established in different years during the 19th century, often reviving local civic traditions of institutions devoted to the trading of securities and goods. **Regulated first by the commercial codes of the 1800s and later by a comprehensive law passed in 1913**, the history of stock exchanges in Italy reflects the evolving financial geography of the country. Among them, the Milan Stock Exchange - operating since 1808 - gradually emerged as the most important, followed by Rome. This trend became even more pronounced in the 1970s, when many banks began to adopt centralized order management systems, channeling most operations through Milan and relegating the other nine exchanges to handling retail clients and small local banks. **The "Open Outcry" System** Frenetic and theatrical, **stock trading in Italy relied on the "open outcry" method: the law required that buy and sell offers be shouted aloud by authorized brokers to ensure transparency and public access to trading information**. The trading floor, known as the “ _recinto delle grida_” (literally “shouting rings”) or “ _corbeille_” in the French tradition, served as the stage for stockbrokers and their assistants, intent on executing buy and sell orders. The continuous noise and confusion made verbal communication with other rooms and telephone clients difficult and unreliable. Therefore, **shouting was supplemented by a codified system of hand signals**, used to indicate different kinds of information: numerical signals for quantities and prices, alphabetic signs for company names, and symbolic gestures to represent business activities, product qualities, or general market conditions. **The Milan Stock Exchange** **This world came to an end in the 1990s with a series of reforms that replaced the open outcry system with an electronic trading platform**, a transition completed between 1992 and 1994. These reforms also ended the brokers’ monopoly over stock exchange contracts, led to the creation of investment firms known as "SIMs" ( _Società di Intermediazione Mobiliare_), and finally transferred management of the exchange from public bodies, such as the _Consigli di Borsa_, to a private entity: the joint-stock company Borsa Italiana. **Historical Documents at Bocconi Library** **Bocconi Library preserves a significant collection of resources on the activities of historical stock exchanges**, beginning with **the most complete collection in Italy of price lists from all exchanges**, comprising over a thousand volumes. The library also preserves various publications, including _**L’osservatorio della borsa**_, _**La rivista della Borsa**_ and **annual reports curated by the** _**Comitato Direttivo degli Agenti di Cambio della Borsa di Milano**_. Finally, the Library stores the rare _**Il termometro mercantile e d’industria**_, which published the quotations of four public debt securities traded on the Milan Stock Exchange in the 1830s. _The Stock Exchange in a humorous cartoon by Giovanni

title: The University in Exile: The University Internment Camps in Switzerland, 1943-1945 | Bocconi University
text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # The University in Exile: The University Internment Camps in Switzerland, 1943-1945 **After the armistice of September 8, 1943, many Italian military students—as well as civilians—sought refuge in Switzerland to avoid surrendering to the Nazi army, which was occupying Italy.** They were not considered prisoners of war or formal internees but rather refugees fleeing a collapsing nation. Initially referred to as military refugees by the Swiss Federal Council in an attempt to facilitate their legal expulsion, they were eventually accepted into Switzerland, due to the impossibility of controlling border crossings and the growing solidarity of the Swiss population. In October and November 1943, a questionnaire distributed to the refugees revealed the presence of around **1,000 students and 120 university graduates**. Like earlier cases involving refugees from Poland (1940) and France (1942), **the decision was made to offer these students the opportunity to continue their university studies**. **The Organization of the University Camps** To support this major educational and humanitarian effort, a Comité d’Aide aux Universitaires Italiens en Suisse was established in Lausanne, with the support of the _Fonds Européen de Secours aux Étudiants_ (FESE). The committee was led by Plinio Bolla, Vice President of the Swiss Federal Tribunal in Lausanne, and **Gustavo Colonnetti**, **a former professor at the Polytechnic University of Turin who had also taken refuge in Switzerland**. **Given the difficulty of enrolling the students directly in existing universities, the decision was made to create university camps with a paramilitary structure near universities in French-speaking Switzerland**, as French was the foreign language most widely known among Italian students. A special commission composed of Swiss and Italian professors selected students through oral exams based on their academic curricula. Starting in January 1944, university camps were opened in Geneva (Economics and Law), Lausanne (Engineering and Architecture), Fribourg (Humanities) and Neuchâtel (various disciplines). Each camp operated under the supervision of Lieutenant Colonel Max Zeller, who appointed an academic rector, a university faculty coordinator, and a military commander ( _chef des études_) \- a hierarchical structure typical of military organizations. Roughly half of the 1,000 applicants were admitted, and additional camps were later opened in the Bernese Oberland (notably in Huttwil and Mürren) to accommodate many of those initially excluded. The **Italian University Camp in Lausanne** became the most prominent, thanks to the leadership of **Colonnetti**, **who served as its rector**. He recruited outstanding faculty, organized lectures and cultural events, and founded the Centre for Studies on Italian Reconstruction, which he co-chaired with Luigi Einaudi. Despite the challenges posed by the students’ diverse academic backgrounds, there was a clear effort to uphold academic standards and ensure that **exams would be recognized once students returned to Italy**. To this end, a Swiss-Italian examining board was created: an Italian professor sat on each board to verify program equivalencies and translate Swiss grades into the Italian system. This allowed for the official **r** ecognition of coursework after the university camps closed between May and June 1945. **Documents in Bocconi Library and Historical

title: The University in Exile: The University Internment Camps in Switzerland, 1943-1945 | Bocconi University
text: by the students’ diverse academic backgrounds, there was a clear effort to uphold academic standards and ensure that **exams would be recognized once students returned to Italy**. To this end, a Swiss-Italian examining board was created: an Italian professor sat on each board to verify program equivalencies and translate Swiss grades into the Italian system. This allowed for the official **r** ecognition of coursework after the university camps closed between May and June 1945. **Documents in Bocconi Library and Historical Archives** At Bocconi University Library, there are **34 pamphlets published by FESE, most of which relate to courses held at the Geneva university camp, attended by 200 students and supported by prominent jurists**, including Francesco Carnelutti (who had taught Industrial Law at Bocconi from 1909 to 1912), Donato Donati, Alessandro Levi, Piero Sacerdoti and Vittorio Tedeschi, **and renowned economists, especially Luigi Einaudi** **(himself a civil refugee in Switzerland from September 26, 1943, and in Geneva from October 1944)**. The collection also includes Gustavo Del Vecchio, who had been a professor and rector at Bocconi before being removed due to the racial laws, and Amintore Fanfani. Ariberto Mignoli, who would later become a long-time professor at Bocconi and founder of the _Rivista delle Società_, wrote two pamphlets during his time as an assistant at the Geneva university camp. One was co-authored with Pietro Chiovenda and Vittorio Gattinara based on the course by Alessandro Levi, supplemented with other texts, while the other was based on the course by Georges Sauser-Hall, also supported by additional texts. Other assistants who wrote pamphlets were Vittorio Paretti on the lessons of Del Vecchio and Giuseppe Salto (a Bocconi graduate with Libero Lenti in 1940/41) based on the lessons of Édouard Folliet. In Bocconi Historical Archives (ASBOC), there is also **documentation on the exams taken by Bocconi students at the camps of Huttwil and Mürren** ( _Fondo Buste AB_ _,_ [Fascicolo Esami Svizzeri convalidati sostenuti da nostri studenti residenti provvisoriamente in Svizzera durante gli eventi In addition to the correspondence between the Italian university camp at Huttwil, Bocconi University, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs from 1944 to 1945, the file contains a list of names of students temporarily residing in Switzerland during that period. **After the war**, with the restoration of democracy and the return of the students, the Academic Council was tasked with determining the validity of exams taken in Switzerland. After extensive debate, **the Faculty Council decided to assign individual professors the task of verifying the actual preparation of students who had attended the Swiss university camps through oral exams**. _Gustavo Colonnetti (Source: Wikimedia)_ _Handout of Luigi Einaudi's lectures (Source: Bocconi Library)_ _Detail from the record of recognition of examinations taken (Source: ASBOC)_ "Show all")

title: Library opening hours 1 November | Bocconi University

title: The many sides of Angelo Sraffa: jurist, cultural organizer and bibliophile | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # The many sides of Angelo Sraffa: jurist, cultural organizer and bibliophile 17 Jul 2025, by Library & Archives A virtual exhibition exploring a central figure in Bocconi’s history Bocconi Library and Archives are pleased to present a new virtual exhibition dedicated to **Angelo Sraffa**, distinguished jurist, professor, and key figure in the life of the University. Through archival documents and bibliographic sources, the exhibition retraces the deep connection that bound Sraffa to “his” university for nearly his entire professional life: from his appointment in 1902 as Professor of Commercial Law, to his tenure as Rector, and later as a member of the University Board, from which he resigned in 1934. The exhibition also offers a unique glimpse into a lesser-known side of his personality: not only a prominent scholar and respected professional, but also a refined bibliophile. The core sections of the exhibition focus on a selection from his extensive personal library, which was partly donated to the University by his family after his death. Special attention is given to several particularly valuable groups: ancient legal texts, a _Miscellanea_ personally compiled by Sraffa, and a number of significant volumes from the humanistic segment of his collection. The result is a portrait of a man of profound humanistic culture and wide-ranging intellectual interests, whose legacy continues to resonate with the history and identity of the University. title: Discover historical documents thanks to Artificial Intelligence! | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Discover historical documents thanks to Artificial Intelligence! 26 Mar 2025, by Library & Archives Bocconi Historical Archives opens the door to history by applying AI: thanks to this new project, it is now possible to easily read hand-written texts and perform word searches on the oldest economic documents preserved at Bocconi. ### Which documents are readable with AI? We have selected seventeenth-century mercantile letters that tell the story of trade between the Tuscan Saminiati family and major Italian and European cities in the period between 1627 and 1630. ### How do I get access? The project on the Saminiati Mercantile Correspondence can be accessed on the [dedicated portal](https://app.transkribus.org/sites/saminiati). ### What can I do? On the portal dedicated to the project you will find the image of the original text alongside its transcription, and you can do word searches by locating words in the original text. ### What tool did we use? We used Transkribus, a platform created in the framework of the European project Horizon 2020, involving the collaboration of a group of European universities. For more information, write to: [archivistorici@unibocconi.it](mailto:archivistorici@unibocconi.it) [Home Library & Archives](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) "Show all")

title: Library Services for Faculty | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Library Services for Faculty 05 Sep 2025, by Library & Archives Welcome to Bocconi Library! As a new academic year is rolling out, let us provide you with an updated overview of the Library services available to support your academic activity at Bocconi. What’s there for you? 1. _**Access the Library 24/7**_ Bocconi Library is located in via Gobbi 5, but you can explore its collections and services directly from the Library website. On the [**Library homepage**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) you will find [**SearchLib**](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/search?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1&lang=en) **to** **access books, articles and more**, and the [**A-Z Databases list**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/az.php?q=) **, the quickest way to browse and access databases**. The Library offers also access to leading international [**newspapers**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/online-news-sources) and magazines, such as the Financial Times, The Economist and Il Sole 24 Ore, some of which are also available via **app**. [**Libguides**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/) are a great way to help your students find relevant resources for your discipline. They provide a selection of key databases, journals and books recommended for different subjects, topics (for example, how to use [financial databases](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/az.php?q=) or find specific data) and services. Fill in the dedicated [form](https://lib-unibocconi.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/blankIll?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1) for purchase and Inter-Library Loan requests: we shape our collections to match your research needs. 2. _**Course Reserves and teaching materials**_ The Library team can help you make required readings accessible to your students through the **Library Course Reserves** tool, integrated into your Blackboard course home page. Find out more about this 3. _**Get tailored support**_ Faculty members can get help and assistance from the Library team directly at the [**Information Desk**](https://bocconi.stackmap.com/explore/1?c=97) in the Library, or by scheduling an **online meeting** via MS Teams or Zoom. To schedule a Library meeting, please write to [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it). Each semester, the Library offers a series or on databases, research strategies, managing citations, and much more. As a faculty member, you can write to us to request **on-demand workshops** designed specifically for your class or research needs. Need to **purchase data for a research project** using your personal research funds? Contact the Library. We will support you during the whole acquisition process, from getting the quotation through the final agreement with the vendor. 4. _**Publish in Open Access**_ Bocconi University promotes **Open Access** as a key practice for making research freely available to all. **Open Access publishing** is supported through **transformative agreements** with academic publishers, allowing Bocconi authors to publish in Open Access **at zero costs**. Discover more in our [**libguide dedicated to Open Access**]( To find out further details about the Library services available to Bocconi Faculty, please consult the Library [**Service Charter**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/servicecharter). For any questions or further assistance, feel free to contact us writing to [infobiblio@unibocconi.it.](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it) [Home Library & Archives](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/news/library-services-for-faculty#addtoany "Show all")

title: Library Workshops Are Back! | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Library Workshops Are Back! 17 Feb 2026, by Library & Archives Find out where to access data and materials, manage your sources, and write citations for your thesis Our workshops are back, designed to help you make the most of the Library resources for your exams, group projects, and thesis. We offer workshops on: - Using **financial databases** to find the data you need (Bloomberg, LSEG Workspace, FactSet, S&P Capital IQ Pro, Aida) - Online tools for research and **finding materials** - **Managing your thesis sources** effectively - Writing **bibliographies** and **citations** - **Law resources** Check the full workshop schedule and register through the [_yoU@B Agenda_](https://agenda.unibocconi.it/), in the “ **Appointments**” section. title: Open Access & Copyright in the Age of AI | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Open Access & Copyright in the Age of AI 24 Sep 2025, by Library & Archives As part of Open Access Week 2025 Bocconi Library organizes, in partnership with Hertie School Library (Berlin), an event to explore the evolving relationship between Open Access (OA), copyright, and artificial intelligence (AI) in scholarly communication. The workshop will address both the opportunities and the legal and ethical challenges of AI in academic research, with a focus on access to literature, copyright compliance in AI training, and sustainable solutions that support both academic integrity and technological innovation. **When**: Thursday, 16 October 2025 2:00-5:00pm **Where**: online **How**: the event is free and it is open to all, [**registration**](https://events.unibocconi.eu/index.php?key=ev2025070081) is required **Programme** 2:00 – 2:15pm Greetings and introduction 2:15 – 2:45pm “AI and open access: transforming the way we search for, analyse and publish academic literature” Christopher Landes (Hertie School) 2:45 – 3:15pm "Understanding copyright in the age of AI: considerations for academic researchers" Christine Daoutis (University College London) 3:15 – 3:45pm “Open Access and the Illusion of Lawful Use: Copyright Challenges in AI Training” Nicola Lucchi (Pompeu Fabra University) 3:45 – 4:00pm Break 4:00 – 5:00pm Round table: Nicolò Cavalli (Bocconi University), Joanna Bryson (Hertie School), Paola Corti (SPARC Europe) The event is organized in collaboration with the network of universities of the [European Project CIVICA](https://www.civica.eu/). For more information, please contact [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it). title: Expand your search with Rapido | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Expand your search with Rapido 09 Dec 2025, by Library & Archives A new tool integrated into SearchLib that enhances Interlibrary Loan and Document Delivery services Starting today, accessing materials not available in the Bocconi Library collections is easier and faster thanks to Rapido, the new tool integrated into [SearchLib](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/search?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1&lang=en) that enhances Interlibrary Loan and Document Delivery services. ### _**How does it work?**_ 1. Start by searching in [SearchLib](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/search?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1&lang=en). 2. If you can’t find the document you need, click the banner at the top of the results to “expand your search beyond the library’s collections.” You will then access a centralized index that includes Open Access content and the holdings of libraries participating in the network. 3. To request a document, click on “Get it for me from other libraries”. If you're requesting a book chapter, make sure to provide as many details as possible. 4. If you requested a digital document, you will receive a secure download link directly to your Bocconi e-mail address. Delivery times range from just a few hours to 1–2 business days, made possible by a system that automatically routes your request to the most suitable library based on location and availability. If you requested a physical item, you’ll receive an e-mail notification when it becomes available for pickup at the Information Desk. Please note: delivery times depend on shipping, and loan periods are set by the lending library. 5. You can track the status of your requests in your personal area, under My Library Account - Requests. If you still can’t find what you need, you can access the traditional request form by clicking the banner again. ### _**Why use Rapido?**_ - **More resources**: access materials not held by Bocconi Library directly from [SearchLib](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/search?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1&lang=en). - **Integrated experience**: no external forms or platforms. Search, request, and manage everything in one place. - **Faster digital delivery**: thanks to automated processes and a global library network, articles and chapters arrive in record time. - **A more sustainable choice**: the digital format for articles and chapters helps reduce paper use, transportation, and the overall environmental impact. - **Global collaboration**: Bocconi’s collections are also shared within the Rapido network, contributing to international academic exchange. The service is free of charge and available to all students, faculty, and staff of Bocconi University. What are you waiting for? Try it now! title: Towards Milan–Cortina 2026 | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Towards Milan–Cortina 2026 02 Feb 2026, by Library & Archives A bibliographic guide to the Olympic Games In preparation for the Milan–Cortina 2026 Winter Olympic Games, the Library has prepared a **bibliographic guide** dedicated to the event, with the aim of supporting multidisciplinary academic research on the topic. The guide provides a curated selection of books, reports, journals, and websites that examine the Olympic Games primarily from an **organizational** and **management perspective**, while also considering their **historical evolution** and the **legacy** that this mega-event leaves on host territories. The guide is freely available online and includes both resources subscribed by the Library and open access material open to everyone. [**Access the guide**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/olympicgames) **Did you already know our libguides?** Over the last years, Library & Archives have published over 50 library guides ( _libguides_) to help our users navigate our resources and services. title: Online the new virtual exhibition path dedicated to L'Ufficio Moderno, 1926-1985 | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Online the new virtual exhibition path dedicated to L'Ufficio Moderno, 1926-1985 27 Jun 2025, by Library & Archives A journey through the history of an avant-garde magazine, among advertising, rationalization and business culture Bocconi Library & Archives is pleased to announce that the new virtual exhibition path dedicated to [L'Ufficio Moderno](https://virtualexhibitions.unibocconi.it/ufficio-moderno/en/1/l-ufficio-moderno-1926-1985?pageId=1), the magazine that marked an epoch in the Italian publishing and cultural landscape, is now available online. Through archive materials and historical images, the exhibition traces the entire parabola of the magazine: from its birth to its advertising campaigns - including the innovative collective initiative to promote Italian beer - to the meetings of the Gruppo Amici della Razionalizzazione in the 1930s. The exhibition also takes an in-depth look at the editorial activity of L'Ufficio Moderno in the 1950s and 1960s, with particular attention to the **National Advertising Award** and the many cultural and entrepreneurial initiatives that made it a point of reference for the world of work, communication and business organisation. The exhibition concludes with the decline and subsequent closure of the title, offering a critical look at the transformation of the role of specialist publishing after World War II. [_**Visit the online itinerary now**_](https://virtualexhibitions.unibocconi.it/ufficio-moderno/en/1/l-ufficio-moderno-1926-1985?pageId=1) An unmissable opportunity to discover - or rediscover - a fundamental page of 20th-century Italian work culture and innovation. title: Winter Break: Library Closed from Dec 21 to Jan 4 | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Winter Break: Library Closed from Dec 21 to Jan 4 10 Dec 2025, by Library & Archives Explore what’s still open to you — anywhere, anytime. The Library will be closed for [winter break](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/opening-hours "Opening Hours") from Sunday, 21 December to Sunday, 4 January included. On Saturday 20 December, Monday 5 and Tuesday 6 January, it will be open from 8.30am to 4pm (closing procedures start 30 minutes earlier). Here’s what you can still do during the period in which the Library is closed for the holidays: - _**Access e-books, e-journals, and databases**_ Most resources are available online 24/7. Search for them through our [**SearchLib**](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/search?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1&lang=en) discovery tool and access them directly. **E-books and e-journals:** look for the item you need in SearchLib and click the link to access the full text. Want to learn how to optimize your search? Check the [**SearchLib guide**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/searchlib)! **Databases:** did you know you can access most of our databases from home? Connect straight from our [**A–Z Databases**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/az.php?q=) page. Some databases require special access methods: always read the instructions provided below for each database name. Not sure which database fits your needs? Select your subject from the drop-down “subjects” menu and explore the recommended databases. **Newspapers:** stay up to date with [**digital newspapers**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/online-news-sources). - _**Borrowed books**_ If you have borrowed books, don’t worry: during the holiday period loans do not expire. You can return them after the break. - _**Working on your dissertation?**_ To get started, you can take inspiration from the dissertations discussed over the years at our University: read the [**Consulting dissertations**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/consulting-dissertations) guide to learn how to access the dissertations archive from home. Also consult our guide [**Writing your Dissertation/Thesis**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/dissertation) for suggestions on how to start gathering material for your thesis. - _**Need help while the Library is closed?**_ Check our [**LibGuides**](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/): they point you to the main resources depending on your subject area (marketing, finance, law, etc.) or on a specific topic of interest (artificial intelligence, sustainability, …). Other LibGuides are more practical, offering step-by-step instructions on how to use specific resources. Visit **B in Touch** as well: you’ll find an [**entire section dedicated to the Library**](https://bit.unibocconi.it/hc/en-us/categories/4405709230354-Library) **,** with the most frequently asked questions (and answers!). Remember to sign in. See you on Monday, 5 January at 8.30! _**Happy holidays!**_ [Home Library & Archives](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/news/winter-break-2025#addtoany "Show all")

title: Your loans now in the yoU@B student diary | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) # Your loans now in the yoU@B student diary 18 Mar 2026, by Library & Archives A new Library channel to help you keep track of due dates in a simple and integrated way From now on, loan due dates are integrated into the yoU@B student diary, making them easier to manage. Specifically: - in the **“Deadlines” section of the Calendar**, you will find automatic updates of the due dates for your current loans; - you will receive a **notification on the actual due date**. Please note that, thanks to the automatic renewal system, due dates may change over time. Books are automatically renewed for up to a maximum of 6 months in total, except in the following cases: - the item is an **exam textbook** (only one automatic one-week renewal is allowed); - the item has been **requested by another user**; - the **maximum loan period** has been reached. If you receive a due date notification, this means that no further renewals are possible. You may return books at any time using the Book return boxes (also through a delegated person), by mailing them or by contacting the Library team at the Information Desk. If there are no reservations or blocks due to overdue items, you may borrow the book again and start a new loan period. You can always check the updated status of your loans by accessing [**My Library For more information, please visit the dedicated webpage [Borrow, Renew and Return Books](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/using-library/borrow-renew-and-return-books). This new channel has been created to make communication about due dates more immediate and effective, supporting responsible loan management. Respecting due dates helps ensure fair access to the Library’s collections for the entire Bocconi community. text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Online News Sources Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) [Using the Library](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/using-library) [Teaching and Research Support](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support) [What's on](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/whats) Highlights [Opening Hours](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/opening-hours) [Get in Touch](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/get-touch) [Suggestions and Complaints](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/suggestions-and-complaints) ## Newspapers Here's a list of the most popular newspapers that you can access online. Some of them require to create an account, here you can find all the instructions: - [**Corriere della Sera (Archivio Pro)**](https://go.openathens.net/redirector/unibocconi.eu?url=https%3A%2F%2Farchivio.corriere.it) Includes all articles published on Corriere della Sera from 1876 up to now. The current edition is available from around 11 am (click on _Ricerca ultimi 7 giorni_) - [**Il Sole 24 Ore**](https://du.ilsole24ore.com/utenti/authfiles/loginaziende.aspx?caller_id=CRUI.MYDESK&user_uniqueid=crui) Access restricted to current Bocconi University and SDA members. Enter _Universita Bocconi (OpenAthens)_ as the organization's name and login with your Bocconi/SDA credentials. Scroll down the page and click on _Quotidiani_ within the section _I miei prodotti_. Registration required once a year through the dedicated form. - [**Financial Times**](https://ft.com/Bocconi) Access restricted to current Bocconi University and SDA members. Once you've registered, you can also access the newspaper through the app. Share links to articles exclusively by using any [sharing tools](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qPjJH4CRVng "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qpjjh4crvng") made available by FT. - [**The New York Times**](http://www.nytimes.com/) Access restricted to current Bocconi University and SDA members. You need a **NYT account** (academic pass) to access. Visit [accessnyt.com](http://accessnyt.com/), type in **Bocconi** as school name, click on the institution, and create your account to claim and activate your **one-year pass**. You must use your Bocconi/SDA e-mail address. Once your pass is active, you will be able to access nytimes.com from anywhere. Once you've registered, you can also access the newspaper through the NYT app. - [**The Wall Street Journal**](http://www.wsj.com/) Access restricted to current Bocconi University and SDA members. You need a **WSJ account** to access. with your Bocconi/SDA e-mail address. Once your account is active, you will be able to access WSJ.com from anywhere. Access is valid for one year. After the expiration, you can [re-activate it](https://partner.wsj.com/enter-redemption-code/UCLB8qrudjag). **ATTENTION!** You must be **on-campus** to re-activate it. Once you've registered, you can also access the newspaper through the WJS app. - [**The Economist**](https://myaccount.economist.com/s/institution-login?entity=https://idp.unibocconi.eu/entity) Access restricted to current Bocconi University and SDA members. You can also access the newspaper through the app: once you have downloaded it, click on “Log In” in the top right corner, then sign in using your Bocconi/SDA email address and selecting “Università Bocconi (OpenAthens)". ## Databases The following databases provide many additional news sources from all over the world in many languages, covering national and local newspapers, magazines, trade and professional publications, newswires, web sources: - [Factiva]( restricted to current Bocconi University and SDA members) - [Nexis Uni](https://advance.lexis.com/bisnexishome/?federationidp=PQQ7ZD67425) (Access restricted to current Bocconi University and SDA members) - [Business Source Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) [Using the Library](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/using-library) [Teaching and Research Support](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support) [What's on](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/whats) Highlights [Opening Hours](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/opening-hours) [Get in Touch](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/get-touch) [Suggestions and Complaints](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/suggestions-and-complaints) [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/online-news-sources#addtoany "Show all")

text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Ask a Librarian Teaching and Research Support [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support) Ask a Librarian [Course Reserves [Library [European Documentation Centre [Open Access](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/open-access) [Bibliographic Management [Copyright](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/copyright) ![Ask a librarian #### In-Person Support (Ask a Librarian!) If you're in the Library and need assistance, you can rely on the in-person reference service: Ask a Librarian! Visit the Information Desk in the reading rooms during the following hours: \- Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM – 6:00 PM. At the Information Desk, our specialized staff is available to assist you with: \- Databases – Guidance and support for navigating online databases and using the Data Room 015 \- Bibliographic Information – Helping you find all the print and online resources you need, including textbooks and other Course Reserves \- Loans – Borrowing and consulting Library resources, as well as requesting documents through Interlibrary Loan (ILL) ![Ask a librarian - online #### Online support If you're off-campus and need assistance, you can always reach out to the Library staff by emailing infobiblio@unibocconi.it or contacting us via B-in-Touch. You will receive an answer within 3 working days. Our team can help with: \- Guidance on using databases and support with bibliographic citation tools \- Fixing access issues for Library resources \- Finding print and online materials, including textbooks and other Course Reserves \- Orientation on Library services \- Purchase requests or document supply through Interlibrary Loan (ILL) and Document Delivery (DD) External users are also welcome to contact the Library at infobiblio@unibocconi.it. However, priority will be given to requests from members of the Bocconi Community. Please note that the Library staff does not: \- Conduct bibliographic searches or perform database queries on behalf of users \- Provide complete subject-specific bibliographies or repertories ![female student using a special #### Assistance by appointment (Library meetings) Bocconi students and Faculty members can request one-to-one support through a Library Meeting. Appointments are available in person at the Information Desk or online via Teams, depending on availability. Each session lasts 30 minutes. \- Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM To schedule a Library Meeting, email infobiblio@unibocconi.it, specifying your research needs. text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Bibliographic Management Tool Teaching and Research Support [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support) [Ask a Librarian](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/ask-librarian) [Course Reserves [Library [European Documentation Centre [Open Access](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/open-access) Bibliographic Management Tool [Copyright](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/copyright) ## RefWorks RefWorks is the bibliographic management tool ( _citation manager_) supported by the Library. It is web-based, thus allowing you to access your references from any web connected device, with no need to install any specific software. RefWorks will help you save time and maximize your efforts in collecting and track your sources. You will be able to: - create a personal database of references collected from different kind of sources, such as databases, web, and the like - organize, annotate, and tag your references - automatically build and format a bibliography in a wide range of citation styles - add references directly to your paper as you write ## How to get access to RefWorks? Follow this [link](https://refworks.proquest.com/) to sign up and access RefWorks: as a first step, you will need to create a personal account. To create it, you will need to enter your institutional e-mail (Bocconi/SDA). ## Online guides and video tutorials - [Libguide](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/refworks) - [RefWorks user guide](https://knowledge.exlibrisgroup.com/RefWorks/Product_Documentation/RefWorks_User_Guide) - [Video tutorials](https://www.youtube.com/@refworks649) ## Want to know more? Take a Library workshop! The Library periodically organizes workshops dedicated to RefWorks and aimed at students and PhD students. Find out about our courses on the page [Library or check the calendar in the [agenda YoU@B](https://agenda.unibocconi.it/)(Library section) and sign up! ## Information & Support For information and assistance write to [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it) Teaching and Research Support [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support) [Ask a Librarian](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/ask-librarian) [Course Reserves [Library [European Documentation Centre [Open Access](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/open-access) Bibliographic Management Tool [Copyright](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/copyright) "Show all")

text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Copyright Teaching and Research Support [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support) [Ask a Librarian](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/ask-librarian) [Course Reserves [Library [European Documentation Centre [Open Access](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/open-access) [Bibliographic Management Copyright _The Library copyright policy provides information on those activities and services that require knowledge and observance of copyright laws and licensing agreements governing access to digital resources._ Making photocopies and scans The law allows to make a single printed copy of an item protected by copyright, without any authorization from the rights holder, for individual study and in line with the following criteria: - journals: one article, in any case within a maximum limit of 15% of the total number of pages of the issue - books: one chapter, in any case within a maximum limit of 15% of the book’s total number of pages These are actually exceptions. Infact, for any reproduction (even partial) of a protected item, it would be necessary to obtain a specific authorization from the copyright holder. To allow photocopies of protected items (within the above-mentioned limits) on one hand and to remunerate copyright holders on the other, Universities have made an agreement with SIAE and authors’ and publishers’ associations under which Universities pay a “fair compensation”, distributed to authors and publishers. Scanning is different from photocopying and thus does not fall within the exceptions mentioned above. To scan material, you must have the explicit authorization from the copyright holders (author and/or publisher), granted personally or through a copyright clearance service. This is the procedure followed by Bocconi Library to reproduce parts of textbooks in digital format. Receiving photocopies and scans from the Library In the framework of Interlibrary Loan and Intercampus Delivery services, the Library delivers photocopies or digital documents from other libraries or from the Library physical collections to students and faculty members. In both cases the material is shared solely for personal use, for the purpose of study or research. It is therefore not permitted to reproduce these items or to send them to others by any means (fax, e-mail, sharing on social networks). Nor is it permitted to distribute copies during a lesson. If you need to share material for a course, please contact the Library ( [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@uniboccon.it)) to request reuse permission from the publisher. Studying and teaching with digital documents The Library delivers book chapters and journal articles in electronic format specified by faculty members for the preparation of exams. The documents are organised by subject. In order to grant this service the Library has requested authorizations from the legitimate copyright holders and paid for reproduction licenses. The course reserve section is password protected, therefore accessible only by the faculty members in charge of the courses and enrolled students. The texts are either downloadable or available online only, depending on license terms. However, it is important to remember that only an exclusively personal use is permitted, limited to the duration of the course. Sending documents to others or sharing them on social networks and external websites is not allowed. Consulting a thesis Theses are both
