However, it is important to remember that only an exclusively personal use is permitted, limited to the duration of the course. Sending documents to others or sharing them on social networks and external websites is not allowed. Consulting a thesis Theses are both administrative documents, as they attest the regularity of a course of study, and scholarly documents, as they are intellectual works. They come under copyright law precisely because they are the result of graduates’ creative activity. Any reproduction constitutes copyright infringement and consultation is only possible if the author granted permission when submitting the thesis. The author can allow or suspend permission at any time. Both printed and digital theses are stored in the Library. Consultation is allowed, but full or partial reproduction is strictly forbidden. Online content All digital content and objects are also protected by copyright: use of web pages and softwares must be made in the respect of the intellectual property rights of the authors. Please remember that freely accessible material is still generally subject to a license for reuse. It may, therefore, be forbidden to: - copy or modify online content - send it to third parties - share it on social media - publish it on other websites Artificial Intelligence Platforms Copyright regulations and intellectual property laws fully apply to the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and platforms. The protection of intellectual works remains fully in force, regardless of the digital or technological medium used. Unless such use falls within the exceptions provided by copyright law, it is not permitted to upload, input or use copyrighted material (such as thesis, full-text articles, images, e-books) on AI services without first obtaining permission from the rights holders, or if the terms of use of the databases from which the material was retrieved do not expressly allow it. Open Access It is important to make an informed choice about how to publish your research. Assigning the rights to publish one's work to a publisher on an exclusive basis is not always the best solution. The Bocconi Library promotes Open Access to scholarly literature by organizing training initiatives and offering advice to faculty on how to publish in open access, in line with European Commission guidelines that support this mode of publication. Bocconi Library adheres on behalf of the University to transformative agreements signed through the CARE-CRUI consortium to enable Bocconi faculty, researchers and students to publish in Open Access in hybrid journals. title: Copyright | Bocconi University
text: University to transformative agreements signed through the CARE-CRUI consortium to enable Bocconi faculty, researchers and students to publish in Open Access in hybrid journals. For more information on the contracts to which Bocconi University adheres, please see the [Open Access](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/open-access) page. Citing and referencing Citing documents is above all an act of intellectual honesty and a form of respect to the author (moral right). Universities and University libraries, as part of their mission to develop scholarly research, are responsible for disseminating appropriate citation methods. Bocconi Library regularly offers workshops on citation methods and standards. Use of images Images (e.g. photos, drawings, pictorial works, photographic reproductions of artistic work, graphs, tables reproduced as images) are works protected by copyright law, even when they are reproduced in a book, in another document or on the Internet. Partial reproduction of images may be allowed for purposes of criticism and discussion, always citing the source. If reproduction occurs for research or teaching purposes, "the use must be for illustrative and non-commercial purposes", provided that the reproduction "does not compete with the work reproduced" (art. 70 of the Italian Copyright Act). If an illustration is excerpted from a book, it is necessary to cite both the book and the original source of the image. Whether you are preparing for an upcoming exam or assigning weekly readings, you can find all the required content in one place: Course Reserves, the Library tool integrated with Blackboard. ### For Students Access your reading list directly from your course page on [Blackboard](https://blackboard.unibocconi.it/). In each list, you will find: - Books and eBooks available at the Library - Articles, case studies and book chapters in full text Why use it? - No need to search on SearchLib: everything is ready to use. Each list includes direct links to Library-subscribed online resources, along with details on the location and number of available copies for printed materials - Easy access from any device, on campus and from home For more information, take a look at our [dedicated libguide](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/coursereserves) or watch the videos below. **Where can I find textbooks and other print course materials required for exams?** If online versions of required resources cannot be purchased, the Library will acquire print copies and make them available in a dedicated open-shelf area: the Course Reserves (Textbooks) Collection, located near the Information Desk. **How long can I borrow course materials?** To make course materials easy to find, we use a color-coded system and special call numbers: - Green sticker: borrowable for 2 weeks, renewable once for 1 additional week. - Red sticker: not loanable, Library-use only. **Will I find all essential readings in the Course Reserves Collection?** The Library works actively to ensure that all required textbooks are available in the Course Reserves (Textbooks) Collection. We review and update the collection at the beginning of each academic year, checking both availability and physical condition of materials. But if you notice something is missing, please get in touch at [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it) so we can look into it. **How can I check if a required reading is available at the Library?** Just follow these steps: 1\. Login to [Blackboard](https://blackboard.unibocconi.it/) with your Bocconi credentials and access one of your courses 2\. Click on the Course Reserves tool You’ll be able to: - Browse your class’ reading list - Download or read online resources - Check the availability of print copies and request them **Need help?** If you need help, come visit us at the Information Desk during [opening hours](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/opening-hours "Opening Hours") or contact us at [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it). text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Library Workshops Teaching and Research Support [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support) [Ask a Librarian](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/ask-librarian) [Course Reserves Library Workshops [European Documentation Centre [Open Access](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/open-access) [Bibliographic Management [Copyright](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/copyright) Need to find academic articles, books and data for your research? Doubts on writing a bibliography for your thesis? Are you a faculty member interested in organising a class session on specific resources? Bocconi Library offers a **program of** **scheduled workshops** and is available for organising **on demand workshops** upon request from Faculty members. ## Our workshops Library tools Don’t miss this workshop to discover all the tools available through the Library to support you during your courses, assignments and exams! At the end of this workshop, you will know where to find all the resources and data you need and get the most out of the Library. This workshop is particularly recommended for new students, students who are starting working on their final work and for everyone who wants to get an overview on Library services and resources. **Library workshop season is over! See you at the beginning of the next Academic Year!** Databases The workshops are aimed at exploring different features and the add-ins of some of the databases subscribed by Bocconi Library. #### Upcoming Workshops | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | **TITLE** | **DATE** | **TIMETABLE** | **LANGUAGE** | **LOCATION** | | **APIs with LSEG data: explore LSEG Workspace Codebook** | 15 MAY | 2.30-3.30pm | ENGLISH | ONLINE (Blackboard) | Citations and bibliography The workshops are aimed at providing the basic skills needed to correctly cite bibliographic sources when writing academic texts (final work, papers, class assignments) and to use the citation manager software RefWorks that can help you creating citations and bibliographies automatically! **Library workshop season is over! See you at the beginning of the next Academic Year!** Law The Library offers the following workshops targeted to law students' specific needs: • **Library Tools**: to get an overview of the search tools to browse Library Law collections and explore legal databases. • **Citation**: to master citations and bibliography for your written academic texts. **Library workshop season is over! See you at the beginning of the next Academic Year!** _**Where do workshops take place?**_ Online workshops take place on Blackboard. In-person workshops take place in Library room 111, on the first floor of the Library (Gobbi 5), or in the Financial Markets Data Room (Via Sarfatti 25, basement). _**How to book?**_ Through your [yoU@B student diary](https://agenda.unibocconi.it/), “Appointments” section. Workshops are confirmed with a minimum of 4 participants. You will receive a confirmation email the day before the workshop. ## Request a workshop The Library can support faculty members in their teaching and research activities with tailored sessions for students and faculty training. Topics that can be covered include: - Library resources, including databases - Research skills - Citation and bibliography management - Open science, open access and transformative agreements Write to [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it) to discuss all the details.

text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Access to Bocconi Library & Archives ## Welcome! Library & Archives supports the Bocconi community and works every day to make information accessible and to offer services for teaching, learning, research, and inspiration. The Library is open from [Monday to Sunday](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/opening-hours). You can discover the world of the online Library 24 hours a day also off-campus and access all the services dedicated to you, entering into your personal area [sign in](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/login?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1). ## Library: - collections (print and digital): books, periodicals, statistics and research databases focusing on economics, law and social sciences - individual study seats in the reading rooms - Phone Booths: soundproof booths dedicated to online calls and meetings. You will also discover tips to manage your reservations and to solve the most common issues. Remember: **booking a study seat in the Library is mandatory for the entire duration of your stay**. Please note: if you can't see the video, click on the green lock in the bottom right corner and accept all cookies. text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Borrow, Renew and Return Books ### How to borrow and return books Watch video Learn how to use the Library self-check station to borrow and return books quickly and easily with this AI-assisted video. Please note: if you can't see the video, click on the green lock in the bottom right corner and accept all cookies. [Transcript](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/Self-check%20video%20transcript.pdf "Self-check video transcript") ## Borrowing books If you’re a member of the Bocconi Community (students, faculty, Bocconi Alumni Community, staff), you can borrow most items from the Library collections. You just need: - your Bocconi ID card or the QRcode created through the [yoU@B student Diary](https://agenda.unibocconi.it/) - the books you’ve picked up from the shelves If you need help, [ask a Librarian](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/teaching-and-research-support/ask-librarian) at the Information Desk. The external community can contact the Library team by writing to [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it) for information about books. ### For how long can I keep a book on loan? You can borrow books for **4 weeks**, except for textbooks, which can be borrowed for **2 weeks** (more information in the [dedicated libguide](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/coursereserves)). ## Renewing books We automatically renew loaned books for up to 6 months, except for these specific cases: - the book is a textbook: in this case, there is one automatic renewal of 1 week - item has been requested by someone else and must be returned - the due date would be after the expiration date of your Bocconi account If we need you to return a book, we will e-mail you with a revised due date. ## Returning books Return books using the self-service machines on the ground floor of the Library and put them in the Book return boxes. If you don't want to enter the Library, place your books into the Book return box at the Library entrance. We also accept postal returns to: **Università Bocconi. Biblioteca e Archivi. Via Ulisse Gobbi, 5 - 20136 Milano (Italia)** Please retain proof of posting until items are discharged from your Library account. ## Request books out on loan To ensure the fair circulation of material we have a process where Bocconi Library users can request a book that is on loan to another reader. When a book you have searched for is on loan it will show on [SearchLib](https://library.unibocconi.it/) as: On loan until ... To place a request on the book: 1. Sign in 2. Search for a book 3. Click on the book to display the record of the item 4. In the 'Get it' section of the record click the request option 5. Fill in any relevant information in the short form 6. Submit your request by clicking the green request option We will email you when the item is ready for you to collect. ### Access material not available: Can’t find it? service Bocconi students and faculty can use the [Can't find it?](https://lib-unibocconi.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/blankIll?vid=39UCLB_INST%3AVU1) service to get access to material not available at Bocconi Library. title: Can't Find It? (Interlibrary Loan) | Bocconi University
text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Can't Find It? (Interlibrary Loan) _Bocconi students, faculty and staff can use the Interlibrary Loan service to get access to material not available at Bocconi Library._ ## Who can use this service? All current Bocconi students and faculty with a valid Library account can use the service. Unfortunately we are unable to extend the service to Bocconi Alumni or visitors. ## How it works Interlibrary Loan (ILL) is a service that allows libraries to borrow and share documents. Books or articles not owned by the Bocconi Library can be requested from a network of partner libraries. To use the service: 1. **Search in** [**SearchLib**](https://library.unibocconi.it/discovery/search?vid=39UCLB_INST:VU1). If the document is not available in the Bocconi collections, click on the banner at the top of the results page to “expand your search beyond the library’s collections”. This will give you access to a central index that includes Open Access resources and materials from partner libraries. 2. **Request the document.** Select “Get it for me from other libraries” to submit your request: - for digital documents, you will receive a secure link in your institutional e-mail; - for print documents, you will receive an e-mail notification when they are ready for pick-up at the Information Desk. 3. **Still haven’t found what you need?** You can access the traditional Can’t find it? form by clicking the banner again. All requests are reviewed by the Library Team, also with a view to potential collection development. ## Interlending services for external libraries External libraries can [submit requests via email.](mailto:gila@unibocconi.it) The supply of books (Interlibrary Loan) and articles or book chapters (Document Delivery) complies with current copyright regulations, the licensing terms of electronic resources, and the preservation status of the documents. title: Use Online Resources | Bocconi University
text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Use Online Resources ## Accessing online resources The Library website serves as access point to our resources. At the center of the homepage, you will find all our search tools: **SearchLib** and **A-Z Database List**. [SearchLib](https://library.unibocconi.it/) is our discovery tool to browse our print and electronic collections, and beyond. SearchLib is particularly recommended for browsing academic material and request books. If you’re looking for statistics, reports or other specialistic content, you might need to look into specific databases. To do that, check out our [A-Z Database List](https://unibocconi.libguides.com/az.php?q=). This alphabetical list of all our bibliographic and numeric databases is particularly useful to check what’s available through the Library and quickly access the platforms. Next to the resource titles, you will find icons explaining access information. ## Off-campus access Even if you are off-campus you can access a number of databases, e-journals, e-books and other online resources of the Library. In order to access online material, you will need to authenticate: the authentication system is called OpenAthens. Who is entitled to off-campus access? Regularly enrolled undergraduate, Master’s and PhD students, authorized faculty members, Bocconi University and SDA staff. For information and assistance write to [infobiblio@unibocconi.it](mailto:infobiblio@unibocconi.it) ## Responsible use of online resources The majority of electronic resources (databases, e-journals, e-books) made available through the Bocconi Library are governed by license agreements between the Library and publishers or vendors. These define specific terms and conditions of use, i.e. authorized users, permissions and restrictions. **Access to the licensed online resources is for educational and research use only.** Here you can find a list of usually permitted and not permitted uses: - **Displaying, searching, downloading, printing and storing the licensed material** for scholarly research, educational and personal use only - **Creating a temporary link** to a journal article or a book/book chapter for use in electronic course packs or learning management systems provided proper reference to the author and source is given, and with the authorization of the Library (only authorized users can access it) - **Sharing your own IDs and password** with third parties, nor to enable anyone other than authorized user to use the licensed material - **Distributing or transmitting** (by whatever means, e.g. fax, e-mail, social networks, etc.) the licensed material to anyone other than authorized users - **Systematically downloading, printing and storing** an excessive portion of the licensed materials (e.g. an entire journal issue or e- book), also by use of specific software - **Exporting and using the content in artificial intelligence tools** is not permitted unless such use is explicitly authorized by the resource’s terms of use or falls within the limits of copyright exceptions, in particular the personal-use reproduction of non-substantial parts of a work (typically up to 15% of the work, by analogy with the provisions that apply to analogue reproductions) - **Removing, obscuring or modifying any copyright** author attribution or other notices included in the licensed material - Making **any use** **for commercial purposes** - Making any use that exceeds or violates the

title: Bocconi Campus Tour | Bocconi University
text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Bocconi Campus Tour ![Bocconi Campus Founded in 1902 by Ferdinando Bocconi as “Institute of Higher Education in Economics”, Bocconi University was the **first Italian University in the field**. From the original location in via Statuto, in 1941 the University moved to via Sarfatti, which at the time was outskirts of the city. The first building in via Sarfatti 25 was designed by **Giuseppe Pagano** and represents a **perfect example of rationalist architecture**. In the following years, **Giovanni Muzio** together with his son Lorenzo designed the Student House, followed by the Library. In the framework of the Strategic Plan “Bocconi 2000”, Bocconi University decided to further expand the campus and the first SDA School of Management was built by **Vittore Cerretti**, followed by the velodrome by **Ignazio Gardella** and the **Via Roentgen** building, designed by Grafton Studio and inaugurated in 2008. Finally, in 2019 Bocconi campus expanded to an area previously occupied by a **milk processing plant** through a project of urban requalification. Designed by Studio Sanaa, the new campus comprises the buildings of the new SDA School of Management, the Castiglioni student house and a new sport center. Bocconi University offers guided tours, open to the general public, of its urban campus in downtown Milan. Tour guides will tell stories about the people and architecture of the University, as well as share interesting facts about the campus and the history of Bocconi. Two types of tours are available, both in Italian and English: - **Full tour**, lasting about two hours, with access to several buildings - **Short tour**, lasting about one hour, outdoors only [More information on upcoming dates and "campus tour") [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/whats/bocconi-campus-tour#addtoany "Show all")

title: Pick your Goal! | Bocconi University
text: Library & Archives [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives) # Pick your Goal! ## A better and more sustainable world for all ### The 2020 UN Agenda for Sustainable Development The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, adopted by all United Nations Member States in 2015, provides a shared blueprint for peace and prosperity for people and the planet, now and into the future. The core are the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which are an urgent call for action by all countries in a global partnership. ### Bocconi and the UN Agenda 2030 for sustainable development Bocconi’s most direct contribution to the United Nations 2030 Agenda for sustainable development is in research and teaching, and in particular Quality Education (SDG 4), Gender Equality (SDG 5), Decent Work and Economic Growth (SDG 8), Reduced Inequalities (SDG 10), Sustainable Cities and Communities (SDG 11) and Climate Action (SDG 13). Bocconi University also contributes to the development of multiple fields of study that address, in a multidisciplinary manner, many other SDGs. ## Pick your goal! ### Bocconi Library and the UN Agenda 2030 for sustainable development The Library promotes the 17 goals of the United Nations 2030 Agenda by ensuring inclusive services and environments in a stimulating climate that meets the needs of learning, teaching, research and interaction. Now the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are even closer and visible among the collections in the reading rooms. All that it takes is to discover them together. Only the broadest and most crosscutting exchange enables the advancement of scientific research and understanding of the world: are you ready to go? ### Want to find out more about the 17 goals of the United Nations? Click on the icon to discover each goal. You will find: - A brief **description** of the goal - **Keywords** for searching relevant materials in [**SearchLib**](https://library.unibocconi.it/ "SearchLib") - The **shelves** where the books are located ### Need help? Ask the **Library team!** [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/library-archives/whats/pick-your-goal#addtoany "Show all")

title: Access to the Bocconi network through VPN | Bocconi University
text: Technology and Information Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/technology-and-information-services) # Access to the Bocconi network through VPN (Service only available for Teachers and Technical-administrative staff) A **VPN**, **Virtual Private Network**, is a private network activated between individuals, using the Internet as a public means of communication. Thanks to a VPN access server, a communication channel is created through the Internet, which carries encrypted and thus secure information. The user can therefore use the internal network and it's services from home or from any internet station as he were physically operating from the Campus. In addition, users that access Bocconi email through client applications (eg: Microsoft Outlook) can set the SMTP Bocconi server (smtp.unibocconi.it) as the default outgoing mail server when authenticating in the **VPN**. To use this service, users need to have the necessary credentials (username and password). Authentication is made by the LDAP protocol. **The service is available only for Teachers and Technical-administrative staff**. The new VPN client software and the installation instructions are available by the [Professor's Diary](https://agenda.unibocconi.it/ "PROFESSOR'S AGENDA"). For any problems or for further information, please send an email to the following address: [noc@unibocconi.it](mailto:noc@unibocconi.it) "Show all")

title: e-Learning and technology research | Bocconi University
text: Technology and Information Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/technology-and-information-services) # e-Learning and technology research **LTCC** (the Learning Technology Competence Centre) is the technology research and services office established by ICT in 1999 to support and spread the use of e-learning platforms. **LTCC** also contributes to the implementation of multimedia teaching projects of general interest to the University. **LTCC** makes its skills and technological knowhow available to both the **Faculty**'s courses and **SDA Bocconi** initiatives. It also supports the continuous training of personnel organized by **Human Resources**. This office provides **support** services to students and participants via email. It assists faculty members through **personalized training** on the technological potential of platforms. It is also in charge of activities related to the scheduling and management of access to online courses. ## **The virtual learning environment** Bocconi University uses the **Blackboard** e-learning platform to support the University's educational activities, accessible at the address [blackboard.unibocconi.it](https://blackboard.unibocconi.it/webapps/portal/execute/tabs/tabAction?tab_tab_group_id=_2_1) through university credentials. Faculty members and students can access a **virtual teaching environment** which, thanks to the use of innovative teaching methods, allows them to create, manage and follow lessons and courses interactively with the help of discussion blogs, videoconferencing, tests, online assessments and more. Furthermore, in each course present in the platform, additional tools and features are **integrated** and **available** for: - scheduling, creating and recording **videoconferences**, webinars and individual meetings remotely ( **Blackboard Collaborate Ultra**); - **preventing** plagiarism and encouraging the correct citation of resources in assignments ( **SafeAssign**); - creating and sharing **videos** of any type, with the opportunity to track user views by user or create video quizzes ( **Kaltura**); - to make use of the **Library**'s digital and physical resources ( [**Course Reserves**](https://lib.unibocconi.it/en/screens/textbooks/ "Course Reserves")); - assigning the **textbooks** required for each course ( **EGEA Content Catalog**); - using the learning platforms of the leading textbook providers ( **Pearson** and **McGraw-Hill**); - carrying out programming assignments ( **Gradescope**); - carrying out tests with advanced mathematical questions ( **WIRIS Quizzes**). Other useful tools for teaching and research that are not yet integrated into the platform: - [Microsoft Office 365](https://office.unibocconi.it/) (access allowed only to students with university credentials); - [Qualtrics - Survey system for research and teaching](https://qualtrics.unibocconi.it/) (access with university credentials). ## **Videoconferences Service** The Learning Technology Competence Centre staff is available to support you in the use of [videoconferences](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/programs/current-students/services/videoconferences) for your work, teaching and research needs. #### HELP E-LEARNING Support e-Learning for Faculty and Staff: [elearning@unibocconi.it](mailto:elearning@unibocconi.it) Support e-Learning for Students: [B in Touch](https://bit.unibocconi.it/hc/en-us/sections/4504149583122) "Show all")

title: IDEM Federation | Bocconi University
text: Technology and Information Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/technology-and-information-services) # IDEM Federation Bocconi University has joined the [IDEM Federation](https://www.idem.garr.it/en/) (IDEntity Management per l’accesso federato), the Italian Authentication and Authorization infrastructures federation for the GAAR Network, the italian network for Research and Education. GAAR coordinates the various activities and provides the central infrastructure, the services and manages the applications. IDEM is the first italian federation of Authentication and Authorization (AAI). Its goal is to allow the members of the scientific and academic community to easily access services and online content that's made available by various organizations. Joining IDEM provides users at Università Bocconi with the convenience of using institutional login information to access all the resources available through the Federation. Services that can be reached through the Federation are made available by [IDEM's partners and members](https://www.idem.garr.it/en/join/participants). For any issues and information regarding the IDEM Federation, send an email to: [idem@unibocconi.it](mailto:idem@unibocconi.it). title: Infrastructure and Systems | Bocconi University
text: Technology and Information Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/technology-and-information-services) # Infrastructure and Systems The IT infrastructure and University network systems offices have the duty of administrating the University IT system and managing the applications, hardware and software that make up the structure supporting the network. In particular, the offices manage all internal servers where all the applications used at the University are stored. Activities: - find the most advanced and secure solutions for the use of resources and information through both the cabled and wireless network infrastructures; - administration of the email service used by the University and SDA Bocconi Students, Faculty and Staff; - implementation of IT solutions set out in test projects in progress in the IT innovations area; included are the technology used for multi-videoconference systems and the podcasting service to support lessons; - administration of the University portal and the e-learning portal; administration of the internal profiling system, based on LDAP Novell; - administration of the Apple Podcast and video streaming system, as well as backup procedures; - management of software for users connected to the network used by Students, Faculty and Staff; - organizational management of Student computer labs, with constant updates of the standard and scientific application packages for all IT equipment; - implementation and management of the network connectivity at each building on the University campus. ### Related Services - - [Software at Bocconi]( "Show all")

title: Hardware Requirements | Bocconi University
text: Technology and Information Services [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/technology-and-information-services) # Hardware Requirements **Hardware Requirements** TECHNOLOGY recommends the following device features for accessing wi-fi: **_Laptop_** Wireless card compatible with the standard 802.11ac or 802.11a/b/g/n (but with a lower performance level). If your laptop has not a wireless card with these features, you can buy Wireless USB cards at a moderate price. **_Smartphone and Tablet:_** The same requirements are for smartphone and tablet as well as for laptop: preferably compatible with standard 802.11ac, or otherwise with 802.11a/b/g/n. We do not recommend the use of laptop, smartphone or tablet compatible with the only old standard 802.11b/g and 802.11b/g/n because they can only work using a frequency of 2.4 GHz and a speed of 54 Mbps. title: Services dedicated to Head Hunting Agencies | Bocconi University
text: For Employers and Partners [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/employers-and-partners) # Services dedicated to Head Hunting Agencies Services offered by Bocconi dedicated to head hunters are the following: - **Access to CV Book** Bocconi’s CV Book is a summary of the personal data, academic background, work experience and language knowledge of Bocconi recent graduates. CVs are published after each graduation session and are available for one year. - **Promotion of internship and placement opportunities** Bocconi University carefully checks the quality of opportunities posted on our portal and may opt not to offer job posting services to all those requesting it. In this regard, please consult our [Employer policies](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/employer-e-partner/employer/recruitment-online/employer-policies) which applies to both Head Hunters and its Client Companies. Head Hunters may promote placement offers both for themselves and for their client companies, but may only promote internship opportunities for themselves. In this case, internships are to be formalized through Bocconi University. Head Hunting agencies are allowed to promote up to: - 12 offers a year; - 2 offers at the same time. **Please note** that such restrictions do not include senior placement offers posted by Head Hunters. **[Access to our services](https://jobgate.unibocconi.it/home.php?lingua=eng)** For any further detail, please refer to: **Barbara Di Maggio** +39 025836.2781 [barbara.dimaggio@unibocconi.it](mailto:silvia.terrenghi@unibocconi.it) "Show all")

title: Performing Arts Night 2026 | Bocconi University
text: # Performing Arts Night 2026 11 May 2026 6:00pm - 11:30pm Via Roentgen 1 #### An evening entirely devoted to performing arts at Bocconi! A journey through the performing arts as a shared community experience, where every voice, every body, every image is a thread that binds us together. Student participating in **theater, singing, dance and filmmaking** courses organized by Campus Life, together with students from the Association **Gruppo Teatro Studenti Bocconi,** will perform in an evening celebrating the performing arts on campus. This will be followed by **the musical "Tonight We Gotta Footloose!" by BLPSA.** The evening is organized by Campus Life **in collaboration with Teatro Franco Parenti** and coordinated byProf. **Alex Turrini**, Arts & Humanities Committee with responsibility for performing arts. The Bocconi University community reveals itself through art as a living network of connections, passions, and presences. ### **Program** From 6 pm, foyer Aula Magna Roentgen ### Performing Arts Showcase The evening celebrates the journey of the workshops and student initiatives promoted by Campus Life: through distributed stages, video installations, and performance spaces, featuring theater, singing, and dance. At the beginning and at the end of the evening, the Gruppo Teatro Studenti Bocconi - directed by Marco Brambini - will present readings from the works of Stefano Benni. Each performance thus becomes a thread cast into the shared space of the community, capable of connecting stage and audience, performers and spectators, students and the public, making visible through art the network of bonds that already unites us. The workshops were led by: - **Theater**: Tobia Rossi in collaboration with Claudia Grassi, artistic collaborator. - **Choral singing**: Aleksander Zielinski - **Dance**: Marco Pelle in collaboration with Gaia Maria Lorusso, artistic collaborator. - **Filmmaking**: Tommaso Santambrogio, in collaboration with Astrid Ardenti, artistic collaborator. _Free event, registration required._ [Read more](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/events/performing-arts-night-2026#accordion-boxed-142973) Don't miss the Performing Arts Showcase [Register here!](https://events.unibocconi.eu/index.php?key=ev20260511pan) 9 PM, Aula Magna Roentgen ### Musical "Tonight We Gotta Footloose!" Get ready to dance, sing, and let yourself be swept away by the most infectious music ever. BLPSA is proud to present a rousing revival of one of the most beloved shows in the history of musical theater. title: Student Associations: 110 Ways to Experience the University | Bocconi University
text: News and Events Hub [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/hub-news-and-events) [University](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/news-categories/university) [Welcome days](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/argomento-news/welcome-days) # Student Associations: 110 Ways to Experience the University 23 Aug 2024, by Pietro Masotti, translated by Jenna Walker Associations recognized by the University range from groups related to volunteering and social work, to groups that bring together national communities; from sports to literary associations, as well as groups focusing on diplomacy and international cooperation. With over 100 official student associations, they are a great way to meet people who share your interests and put yourself to the test These days, Students for Humanity’s group chat is full of photos of a construction site. They are from a site in Wasa, Tanzania, where some of the members of the Bocconi student association are following the renovation of a school that inspired the Working for Wasa project. At the same time, more than 13 years ago, it also inspired the creation of a student group that would deal with social issues at Bocconi. Today the school hosts 70 students and represents one of the main projects that Students for Humanity (SforH) supports as a volunteer organization recognized by the Lombardy Region. "I myself was in Tanzania two years ago, helping register the facility with the local government," recalls **Anna Artese**, in her second year of the Master of Science in International Politics and Government and president of SforH. Since its inception in 2011, SforH has also grown as a Bocconi association with over 100 members and is now a point of reference among student groups focusing on social-oriented initiatives: it organizes events, promotes fundraising, participates in awareness campaigns and supports the projects of other NGOs. "But most of all we try to encourage our classmates to actively participate in the various activities," adds Anna. "And we act as an intermediary between associations that need volunteers and students who have expressed their availability. In recent years we have participated in lots of one-off initiatives, from collecting medicine for children to prison visits. More consolidated collaborations are also created when we are able to guarantee adequate and ongoing participation." "There are about 110 student associations active at Bocconi today," says **Paola Profeta**, Dean for Diversity, Inclusion and Sustainability and President of the CASA Committee that brings together the leadership of the associations but also members of the staff, academics and the Campus Life offices. "Some groups are active on general issues, others have specific interests, regarding individual countries, economic matters or social issues. It is a very interesting area that makes life on campus more exciting. It has grown over the years in terms of numbers, perhaps because the younger generations are more inclined to develop extracurricular interests and look for other people at the university they can share them with. In this sense, they can be considered part of student education, understood not only as teaching or research, but creating a context where students can put themselves to the test in developing and implementing ideas by creating a professional network and a community of

title: Student Associations: 110 Ways to Experience the University | Bocconi University
text: exciting. It has grown over the years in terms of numbers, perhaps because the younger generations are more inclined to develop extracurricular interests and look for other people at the university they can share them with. In this sense, they can be considered part of student education, understood not only as teaching or research, but creating a context where students can put themselves to the test in developing and implementing ideas by creating a professional network and a community of people. At Bocconi we try to make sure they do not become closed, exclusive circles, but that they remain as inclusive as possible." This is a topic that **Angelo Hu** – newly elected head of the Bocconi Chinese Student Association (BCSA), founded in 2010 with the aim of extending a bridge to Chinese heritage – understands well. "It is therefore not an association only for Chinese students, but it is open to anyone interested in the country and its culture," Angelo points out. For this reason, activities more related to business aspects are interspersed throughout the year with others of a more recreational nature. "For example, this year we hosted some senior members of the Alibaba group who shared with us the strategies of their success in international and online commerce, but we also celebrated several typical holidays such as the Moon Cake Festival, and of course the Chinese New Year with a Dumpling Event, during which we prepare dumplings by hand and get to eat them together." The most eagerly awaited event on the BCSA calendar is the Welcome Dinner, a dinner attended by over 200 people and which includes speeches, dance and singing performances, as well as ice breaking games. Activities also include volleyball and badminton sports challenges with other universities and winter sports, confirming that the main objective of the association is to promote cohesion and the creation of strong bonds between members. "Above all, we would like to reach out more to international students, who today represent 15% of currently enrolled students," continues Angelo. "Chinese students in particular are more likely to get to know us as soon as they arrive at Bocconi because we offer a dedicated tutoring, orientation and academic support program for them. We have also created a page on the Chinese social network Xiaohongshu (Little Red Book) that shows university residences, lecture buildings and study spaces, with vlogs that explain a typical day at Bocconi." Every year there are changes to the panorama of student associations, with some closing shop and others being founded. "Students who would like to propose a new association must submit a list with a certain number of interested classmates," explains Dean Profeta. "We evaluate their purpose, we look at whether there are other similar groups present, possibly suggesting a merger, we approve the calendar of events and we monitor that they remain active over time, i.e. that they are organizing activities. And we also promote special events, such as the Associations Fair, in which the different groups

"We evaluate their purpose, we look at whether there are other similar groups present, possibly suggesting a merger, we approve the calendar of events and we monitor that they remain active over time, i.e. that they are organizing activities. And we also promote special events, such as the Associations Fair, in which the different groups can introduce themselves on campus and to other students." It was during one of these initiatives last year that **Lea Casucci** came across a presentation by Bocconi Students for Diplomacy and International Cooperation, an organization where she is now the outgoing president. "It was my first year, but I was immediately impressed by the initiative because I already had an interest in international cooperation and it seemed like an opportunity that I shouldn’t miss." The association is active in the organization of events and conferences on the subject and it promotes contact between students and international organizations. Today there are about 70 members. Recruiting sessions are held twice a year to assess which new members should join, evaluating their motivations and skills to understand what activities they can contribute to. "But events are not reserved, many are open to all students," Lea points out. "Last year, for example, we organized a day in memory of Luca Attanasio, the Italian ambassador and former Bocconi student killed in 2021 in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There was a commemoration with Attanasio's family, followed by a panel on the impact of humanitarian aid in Central Africa with very high-profile speakers." The projects in the pipeline for the new year include organizing an exchange with SDA Bocconi on the topic of space diplomacy, and learning more about embassies and consulates in the local area." There is also no shortage of initiatives scheduled by ALBI, the Bocconi d'Inchiostro Literary Student Association. One of the oldest groups at the University, it was co-founded in 2012 by Gerardo Masuccio, now editor at Utopia. Since then, the group has been responsible for suggesting literary insights to the entire university community, promoting events with writers, poets, publishers and translators, and raising awareness of reading with various initiatives. An example of this is Bookcrossing, created in collaboration with the university: an area located near the entrance to the Bocconi Residence Hall and intended for a book exchange. In just a few months, more than 120 books have already been shared on its shelves. "We try to organize at least three or four events a month, some reserved for our internal Book Club and others also open to the whole city, such as those during BookCity," explains president **Valentina Benassi**. "As well as the event organized on the Bagutta Prize, which was held here because the historical archive of the Bagutta trattoria’s works and its literary prize is preserved at Bocconi." text: [Salta al contenuto [Entra in Bocconi](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/entrare-bocconi) [Scopri i corsi](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/corsi-di-studio) [Accedi a News ed Eventi](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/hub-news-ed-eventi) Chiudi menu per studenti iscritti Menu di sezione [Panoramica](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti) Chiudi Agevolazioni Menu di sezione [Panoramica](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti/agevolazioni) Chiudi [Contatti](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/contatti) # Servizio mensa a tariffa agevolata a.a. 2025-26 Apri per condividere Chiudi Chiudi Possono fruire del **servizio mensa a tariffa agevolata** presso uno dei **punti di ristoro** previstitutti gli studenti regolarmente iscritti ad un regolare anno di corso di un corso di laurea, corso di laurea magistrale, dottorato di ricerca che presentino le caratteristiche indicate in tabella: | | | | | --- | --- | --- | | | **Pasti a tariffa agevolata** | **Presentazione apposita domanda** | | idoneo ISU | **V** | **X** | | Ospiti a tariffa agevolata in una delle Residenze Bocconi | **V** | **X** | | Richiedenti solo servizio mensa | **V** | **V** | Gli studenti in possesso dei [**requisiti economici**](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti/agevolazioni/requisiti-economici-isu-bocconi-aa-2025-26 "Requisiti economici ISU Bocconi - a.a. 2025-26") e intenzionati a richiedere il solo servizio mensa a tariffa agevolata, **dovranno presentare apposita "Domanda di servizio mensa a tariffa agevolata"** nel periodo 14 ottobre - 21 ottobre 2025 **:** **Domanda di servizio mensa a tariffa agevolata** Il beneficio del pasto a tariffa agevolata avrà validità **dal 1 dicembre 2025 al 30 novembre 2026**. Non saranno effettuati rimborsi per eventuali importi residui non utilizzati. Invitiamo gli studenti a verificarne l'entità prima di effettuare l'acquisto soprattutto nelle ultime finestre temporali di ciascun anno accademico (ottobre e novembre). Il pasto a tariffa agevolata Lo studente che beneficia del servizio mensa a tariffa agevolata può acquistare alle tariffe più avanti indicate un pasto completo costituito, di norma da primo, secondo, contorno, pane, frutta o bevanda. Le specifiche tipologie di pasto acquistabile a tariffa agevolata vanno verificate presso il punto vendita. In ogni caso lo studente può acquistare massimo due pasti a tariffa agevolata al giorno, uno a pranzo (dalle 11:45 alle 14:30) e uno a cena (dalle 19:00 alle 20:30), secondo i periodi di apertura previsti per i singoli punti vendita. Se verranno riscontrate anomalie e/o comportamenti impropri, l’Università si riserva di effettuare le opportune valutazioni e di intervenire anche con l’eventuale revoca della possibilità di acquisto dei pasti a tariffa agevolata. Tariffe e acquisto I pasti a tariffa agevolata possono essere acquistati, nei punti ristoro previsti, esclusivamente utilizzando il tesserino Bocconi, sul quale vanno preventivamente caricati. Si ricorda che il badge è personale e non cedibile e che anche i pasti in esso caricati sono esclusivamente ad uso personale e non possono essere ceduti. Possono essere acquistati uno o più pacchetti di pasti composti da 10 pasti l’uno per gli importi **\*** sottoindicati: - 10 pasti in prima fascia ISU Bocconi € 30; - 10 pasti in seconda fascia ISU Bocconi € 38; - 10 pasti in terza fascia ISU Bocconi € 46. Una volta caricati i pasti sul tesserino questi possono esser utilizzati in numero massimo di due al giorno, uno a pranzo (dalle 11:45 alle 14:30) e uno a cena (dalle 19:00 alle 20:30), secondo i periodi di apertura previsti per i singoli punti vendita per l’acquisto di un pasto completo a tariffa agevolata. Se verranno riscontrate anomalie e/o comportamenti impropri, l’Università si riserva di effettuare le opportune valutazioni e di intervenire anche con l’eventuale revoca della possibilità di acquisto dei pasti a tariffa agevolata. **\*** Gli importi possono subire variazioni legate all'inflazione e/o cambiamenti nel servizio offerto. **Attenzione:** In caso di smarrimento e contestuale richiesta di un nuovo badge Bocconi, per accedere al servizio mensa a tariffa agevolata, è necessario inviare una mail con oggetto “Smarrimento badge Bocconi” all’indirizzo [funding@unibocconi.it](mailto:funding@unibocconi.it) per modificare la stringa del proprio badge. Si specifica che a seguito di **revoca** della Borsa di Studio ISU Bocconi, gli studenti in possesso dei requisiti economici previsti nell'a.a. successivo a quello in cui incorre la revoca e intenzionati a richiedere il solo servizio mensa a tariffa agevolata, possono inoltrare apposita domanda online nel periodo previsto, anche se non idonei alla Borsa di Studio ISU Bocconi. \\*\\* Prima finestra d'acquisto disponibile per gli studenti immatricolati al primo anno 2025/2026 - [Punti ristoro](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti/agevolazioni/punti-ristoro-aa-2025-26) Torna su [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti/agevolazioni/servizio-mensa-tariffa-agevolata-aa-2025-26#addtoany "Show all")

text: [Salta al contenuto [Entra in Bocconi](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/entrare-bocconi) [Scopri i corsi](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/corsi-di-studio) [Accedi a News ed Eventi](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/hub-news-ed-eventi) Chiudi menu per studenti iscritti Menu di sezione [Panoramica](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti) Chiudi Tecnologia e Servizi informatici Menu di sezione [Panoramica](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti/technology) Chiudi [Contatti](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/contatti) # Eduroam Apri per condividere Chiudi Chiudi Education Roaming Guarda il video Rete Wireless [Panoramica](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti/tecnologia-e-servizi-informatici/rete-wireless) [Requisiti [Condizioni e norme di Eduroam **Eduroam** ( **Edu** cation **Roam** ing) è un servizio che offre un accesso wireless sicuro alla rete. Permette a **Docenti** e **Personale tecnico amministrativo** della Bocconi che visitano un ente/istituzione che aderisce all'iniziativa, di utilizzarne la rete locale wireless (WLAN) in modo sicuro, autenticandosi con credenziali Bocconi, senza la necessità di espletare ulteriori formalità presso l'istituzione ospitante. Analogamente, tutti gli utenti provenienti da enti/istituzioni che aderiscono all'iniziativa, possono accedere alla rete wireless Bocconi, utilizzando le proprie credenziali, senza la necessità di alcuna registrazione. L'Università Bocconi aderisce alla **Federazione Italiana Eduroam**, coordinata dal **GARR**, che la rappresenta presso le altre federazioni e confederazioni. Eduroam e' un marchio registrato di [TERENA](https://www.terena.org/ "TERENA"). Eduroam è un'infrastruttura basata su una rete di server **RADIUS** che utilizza il protocollo 802.1x. Unico requisito tecnico per accedere alla rete eduroam è che il proprio dispositivo di accesso sia in grado di supportare l'autenticazione 802.1X con crittografia WPA2 / TKIP. Il nome di rete WiFi (SSID) alla quale accedere per usufruire del servizio Eduroam è: **eduroam** L'accesso alla rete Eduroam e' vincolato al rispetto del Regolamento della Federazione Italiana Eduroam. Per maggiori informazioni relative alla rete Eduroam e alla sua copertura nazionale ed internazionale si rimanda al sito della [Federazione Italiana Eduroam](https://www.eduroam.it/ "Federazione Italiana Eduroam") e al sito della [Confederazione Europea Eduroam](https://www.eduroam.org/ "Confederazione Europea Eduroam"). #### EDUROAM Per richiedere informazioni o l'accesso al servizio inviare un email all'indirizzo [**noc@unibocconi.it**](mailto:helpwifi@unibocconi.it) Rete Wireless [Panoramica](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti/tecnologia-e-servizi-informatici/rete-wireless) [Requisiti [Condizioni e norme di Eduroam Torna su [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/it/studenti-iscritti/tecnologia-e-servizi-informatici/rete-wireless/eduroam#addtoany "Show all")

text: # Free museums in Milano: the definitive guide ## Check out all the museums you can visit for free [Museums and Galleries](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-museums-milano-definitive-guide#) [Attractions](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-museums-milano-definitive-guide#) Find here the guide to all the **museums in Milano** that always offer **free entry** plus those that offer free admission on the **first Sunday of the month**, or only on **specific days and times**, and those that offer free entry for **children and youngsters**. Make the most of these opportunities to get your fill of cultural beauty. - [Museums always free in Milano](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-museums-milano-definitive-guide#blocco-redazionale-tab-10543) - [Free museums on the first Sunday of the month](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-museums-milano-definitive-guide#blocco-redazionale-tab-10546) - [Free entry to museums during the week](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-museums-milano-definitive-guide#blocco-redazionale-tab-10547) - [Free for children and teenagers](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-museums-milano-definitive-guide#blocco-redazionale-tab-10548) - [Free museum admission for disabled persons](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-museums-milano-definitive-guide#blocco-redazionale-tab-10558) - [Not-to-be-missed discounts for young persons and students](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-museums-milano-definitive-guide#blocco-redazionale-tab-10567) ### Museums always free in Milano All these museums offer **free entry to their permanent collections**. Temporary exhibitions and events may require an additional ticket: please check the museums’ official websites before your visit for further information. **Civic Museums** - [Mudec - Museum of Cultures](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/mudec-museum-cultures "Mudec - Museum of Cultures") (permanent collection) - [Palazzo Morando \| Costume Moda Immagine](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/palazzo-morando-costume-moda-immagine "Palazzo Morando | Costume Moda Immagine") - [Palazzo Moriggia \| Museo del Risorgimento](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/palazzo-moriggia-museo-del-risorgimento "Palazzo Moriggia | Museo del Risorgimento") - [Casa-Museo Boschi di Stefano](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/casa-museo-boschi-di-stefano "Casa Museo Boschi-Di Stefano") **House Museums** - [Spazio Alda Merini](https://www.spazioaldamerini.com/visita/ "Spazio Alda Merini") - [Casa Verdi](https://www.casaverdi.it/visitare-casa-verdi/visitare-casa-verdi/ "Casa Verdi") - [Museo Mangini Bonomi](http://www.museomanginibonomi.it/contacts/ "Museo Magnini Bonomi") **Other museums** - [Pirelli HangarBicocca](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/hangar-bicocca "Hangar Bicocca") - [Cimitero Monumentale](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/monumental-cemetery "Monumental Cemetery") ### Free museums on the first Sunday of the month The first Sunday of every month is **Domenica al Museo (Sunday at the Museum),** a cultural initiative launched by the Ministry of Culture: the city’s state and civic museums are open free of charge. **Civic Museums** - [Museo del Novecento](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/museo-del-novecento "Museo del Novecento") - [Castello Sforzesco museums](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/castello-sforzesco "Castello Sforzesco Museums") - [Archaeological Museum](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/archaeological-museum "Archaeological Museum") - [Gallery of Modern Art](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/galleria-arte-moderna "GAM Gallery of Modern Art") - [Museum of Natural History](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/natural-history-civic-museum "Museum of Natural History") - [Civic Aquarium](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/milanos-civic-aquarium "Civic Aquarium") - Booking is mandatory: [Palazzo Marino](https://palazzomarinomilano.madeticket.it/it/shop/biglietti "Bok to visit Palazzo Marino") **State Museums** **Please note: booking is mandatory before your visit** - [Brera Art Gallery](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/pinacoteca-di-brera "Pinacoteca di Brera") - [Leonardo's Last Supper](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/buy-your-ticket-leonardos-last-supper "Buy your ticket to Leonardo's Last Supper") (Please make your booking well in advance: visit the page for details) **Other museums** - [Gallerie d’Italia](https://gallerieditalia.com/en/milan/plan-your-visit/ "Gallerie d'Italia") ### Free entry to museums during the week #### Every first and third Tuesday of the month from 2:00 p.m. Every **first and third Tuesday of the month, from 2:00 pm onwards**, the **Milano Civic Museums** offer free entry, in addition to those that always offer free admission: - text: # 10 free things to do in Milano ## From museums with free admission to street art tours, great experiences without spending a euro (or almost) [Attractions](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-things-do-milano#) [Museums and Galleries](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-things-do-milano#) [My first trip to Milano](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-things-do-milano#) Who said nothing is free in Milano? Museums without entry fees, street art tours, Art Nouveau architecture, parks and even a visit to the opera for everyone. Here is a list of **10 things you can do without opening your wallet**. - [1\. Free museums in Milan](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-things-do-milano#blocco-redazionale-tab-123) - [2\. Discover Milan’s “Sistine Chapel”](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-things-do-milano#blocco-redazionale-tab-124) - [3\. Stroll around the Castello Sforzesco courtyard](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-things-do-milano#blocco-redazionale-tab-10721) - [10\. See an opera at the Teatro alla Scala for free (or almost)](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/free-things-do-milano#blocco-redazionale-tab-10722) ### 1\. Free museums in Milan Palazzo Morando \| Costume Moda Immagine Anselm Kiefer, The Seven Heavenly Palaces, 2004-2015. Courtesy Pirelli HangarBicocca. Pic by Agostino Osio Palazzo Morando \| Costume Moda Immagine Anselm Kiefer, The Seven Heavenly Palaces, 2004-2015. Courtesy Pirelli HangarBicocca. Pic by Agostino Osio Palazzo Morando \| Costume Moda Immagine - 1 - 2 1 / 2 There are several **museums**, [**studios and house museums**](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/house-museums "house museums in milano") in Milan that you can visit without spending a euro. The following can always be visited for free: **Palazzo Morando \| Costume Fashion Image**, **Palazzo Moriggia \| the Museum of the Risorgimento**, the **Boschi Di Stefano House Museum**, the **Francesco Messina Studio Museum** and **[MUDEC - Museum of Cultures permanent collection](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/mudec-museum-cultures "MUDEC")** which houses a large selection of finds from global cultures, ranging from the ancient Andean civilizations to the Far East. Alternatively, if you are a contemporary art fan, the **[Pirelli Hangar Bicocca](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/hangar-bicocca "Pirelli Hangar Bicocca")** hosts free installations and exhibitions featuring prominent international artists. You can also walk amongst Anselm Kiefer's permanent site-specific installation, _The Seven Heavenly Palaces_. - [The civic museums in Milano](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/civic-museums-milano) - [House Museums](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/house-museums) ### 2\. Discover Milan’s “Sistine Chapel” Santa Maria delle Grazie San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore Santa Maria delle Grazie San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore Santa Maria delle Grazie - 1 - 2 1 / 2 Not everyone realises that Milan also has its very own “ **Sistine Chapel**” that can be visited for free. As soon as you step inside **San Maurizio al Monastero Maggiore** you will be awed by the stunning array of paintings, stuccos and frescoes that cover every wall and ceiling space. With the exception of the [Duomo](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/10-1-amazing-things-milan-duomo "Duomo di Milano"), all the city churches, with their wonderful interior artworks, can be visited without an entrance fee. - [Visit the 10 major churches in Milano for free](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/10-major-churches-milano) - [Abbeys and monasteries in Milan](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/abbeys-and-monasteries) ### 3\. Admire the Monumental Cemetery Monumental Cemetery - 1 1 / 1 **Cimitero Monumentale** is an authentic open-air museum, freely accessible every day. It regularly hosts readings, concerts and organized tours. - [Find out more](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/monumental-cemetery) ### 4\. Have a Stroll in the City Parks Parco Sempione - 1 1 / 1 There are over 50 parks, green zones and gardens in Milano, and these are ideal for a relaxing break in nature. - [Best parks in Milan](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/node/2417) - [Parks around the city](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/parks-around-city) ### 5\. Hunt for Street Art around the city Street art in Ortica neighborhood: Alda Merini portrait - Istituto alberghiero Pasolini, Ortica - 1 1 / 1 Milano Street Art could surprise you around any corner, in the city centre and in the neighboroods alike. Street art hunting is free and alllows you to discover unespected places in the city. You may like: - [Our street art in Ortica neighborhood](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/street-art-ortica-memoria "Follow the itinerary") - Download the app and see street art get alive with [MAUA](https://mauamuseum.com/) \- _Museo d'Arte Urbana Aumentata_ (the website is in Italian, but the Language of art is universal). ### 6\. Discover Brera Botanical Garden Astronomical Museum seen from the Botanical Garden - 1 1 / 1 A stone's throw from the [Pinacoteca](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/pinacoteca-di-brera "Pinacoteca di Brera") art gallery, still within **Palazzo Brera** itself, you will find the **Astronomical Museum** with the Schiaparelli dome, but also a precious eighteenth-century **Botanical Garden**, open to the public and free to visit. - [Find out more](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/breras-botanical-garden) ### 7\. Jump on a tram and see Milan N. tram 1 passes in front of the Castello Sforzesco. Pic. by markino\_f85-Instagram - 1 1 / 1 Well, it's not exactly free, but it is a great low-cost experience. And most importantly it enables you to get your bearings in the city. For the price of a public transport ticket, **you can make your own tram tour of Milan**. If you get on the **n°14 tram**, which connects Lorenteggio to the Monumental Cemetery area, crossing some famous districts - [Chinatown](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/milano-sarpi-chinatown-things-to-do "5 things to do in Sarpi-Chinatown"), [Brera](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/milano-brera-things-to-do "Brera"), the city centre with the [Duomo](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/duomo-di-milano "Duomo di Milano") and [Galleria](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/galleria-vittorio-emanuele-ii "Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II"), and the [Navigli](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/navigli-milano-things-to-do "Navigli")\- you will stop close to a lot of the city’s major tourist attractions. Or, for a tram trip with a retro touch, you can catch the historic **n°1 tram** which crosses [via Montenapoleone](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/montenapoleone "Via Montenapoleone"), then passes in front of the [Teatro alla Scala](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/teatro-alla-scala "Teatro alla Scala") and the Arco della Pace. - [How to get around Milano](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/node/259) ### 8\. Art Nuveau in Milan La facciata di Casa Galimberti. Pic. by instagalluz - 1 1 / 1 [**Porta Venezia**](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/things-to-do-milano-porta-venezia "Porta Venezia") is one of the liveliest neighborhoods in Milan. But it is also one of the areas where you can see some of the most beautiful buildings in the city. This is where you have to come to discover the jewels of **Art Nuveau architecture**: the buildings around **Piazza Eleonora Duse**, the **Berri-Meregalli houses** on Via Mozart 21, Via Barozzi 7 and Via dei Cappuccini 8, **Casa Galimberti** on Via Malpighi, with its magnificent fully decorated façade, and **Casa Campanini** on Via Vincenzo Bellini 11, with its iconic entrance. - [An Art Nouveau Walk in Milan](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/art-nouveau-walk-7-stops) - [Hidden gens in Milano: discover secret places](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/itineraries/hidden-gems-milano) ### 9\. Stroll around the Castello Sforzesco courtyard Castello Sforzesco. Pic. by Andrea Cherchi - 1 1 / 1 **The Cortile delle Armi** of the **[Castello Sforzesco](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/castello-sforzesco "Castello Sforzesco")** is always open to visitors, free of charge. You can also admire the Ducal and the Rocchetta courtyards. Alternatively, every first and third Tuesday of the month, from 14:00 onwards, and every first Sunday of the month, admission to the Castello museums is also free. - [Scopri di più](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/see-and-do/venues/castello-sforzesco) ### 10\. See an opera at the Teatro alla Scala for free (or almost) Teatro alla Scala di Milano. Pic. Rudy Amisano ©Teatro alla Scala - 1 1 / 1 If you are not on the list of lucky invitees who will attend the **Prima della Scala**, every year **on December 7th**, you still have a chance to experience the magic of opera in Milan. Thanks to the **Prima Diffusa project**, a live broadcast of the special operatic event will be shown in numerous locations around the city. Apart from the opening night, if you want the unforgettable experience of seeing the opera in one of the most famous theatres in the world, you can try to get a seat in the Balcony. For almost all the shows, **La Scala**, offers **numbered tickets for seats with reduced visibility**, with significant discounts (for the opera circa 14 euros, prices can go even lower for the ballet or the symphonic concerts): you just need a lot of patience and you must join the queue in via dei Filodrammatici ( [more details here - Limited view Balcony seats](https://www.teatroallascala.org/en/box-office/tickets-prices/box-office-guidelines.html "Limited view Balcony seats tickets")). - [Find out more about the Prima](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/whats-on/all-events/la-scala-opening-night) ### You may also like - Prev - Next [![Duomo di Milano - Cathedral]( [![What to do in Milan Italy in one day? text: Ricerca per: Indice dei contenuti - [Perchè scegliere Città Studi a - [Quanto costa vivere a Città - [Città Studi e le migliori zone limitrofe per - [Come trovare l’appartamento in affitto ideale a Città - [Pro e contro di vivere a Città - [Vivere in Città Studi a Milano: servizi utili per studenti e giovani lavoratori]( - [FAQs Vivere in Città Studi a - [In conclusione: conviene vivere a Città ## Perchè scegliere Città Studi a Milano Nel cuore pulsante di una Milano sempre più dinamica e internazionale, **Città Studi** si conferma nel 2025 come uno dei quartieri più vivaci e strategici per chi cerca un’esperienza autentica da studente. Meta privilegiata per giovani provenienti da tutta Italia e dall’estero, questo quartiere rappresenta l’equilibrio perfetto tra comodità logistica, qualità della vita e vitalità culturale. Qui sorgono alcune delle istituzioni accademiche più prestigiose del Paese, come il Politecnico di Milano e diverse facoltà scientifiche dell’Università Statale, rendendo la zona il fulcro della vita universitaria milanese. Ma Città Studi non è solo studio e accademia: è anche socialità, energia e scambio culturale. Le sue strade sono animate da bar, librerie indipendenti, bistrot e locali informali che offrono spazi ideali per stringere nuove amicizie e immergersi in una comunità giovane e dinamica. Vivere qui significa potersi muovere facilmente a piedi o in bicicletta, riducendo tempi e costi di trasporto, ma anche avere tutto ciò che serve a portata di mano. In questa guida analizzeremo i motivi per cui **vivere a Città Studi** oggi conviene più che mai, con un focus specifico su affitti smart, servizi per studenti e stile di vita nel 2025. ### Quanto costa vivere a Città Studi? Nel 2025, **Città Studi rimane uno dei quartieri milanesi più accessibili** per studenti e giovani lavoratori. Cosa aspettarsi dall'affitto di un alloggio a Milano? Qualsiasi agenzia immobiliare o locatore ti chiederà di pagare un deposito cauzionale (corrispondente a 1 o 2 mesi di affitto) e, se si tratta di un'agenzia, ci sarà anche una _fee_ di agenzia. Noi di helpHousing vogliamo rendere l'esperienza di alloggio dei nostri giovani internazionali il più piacevole possibile. Per questo li assistiamo fin dall'inizio, nella ricerca dell'appartamento e durante tutto il loro soggiorno a Milano. Forniamo loro alloggi di qualità, assistenza personalizzata e molti servizi sono inclusi: wifi, servizi di pulizia e manutenzione tecnica. #### **Prezzi medi a seconda del tipo di alloggio a Milano** Puoi aspettarti di pagare tra i 500 e i 1200 euro al mese per un [alloggio per studenti a Milano.](https://helphousing.com/it/alloggio-a-milano) I prezzi variano chiaramente a seconda del tipo di alloggio. \- [Stanza in affitto a Milano](https://helphousing.com/it/alloggio-a-milano/stanze). Un appartamento condiviso in cui si vive con altri studenti è l'opzione migliore per ridurre le spese mensili. Il prezzo dell'affitto della stanza varia tra i 500 e gli 800 euro/mese. È più alto quando si tratta dei quartieri centrali e più famosi di Milano. Ma varia anche in base alle dimensioni della stanza, alle utenze incluse o meno, al bagno privato, ecc. Quindi, assicurati di leggere tutti i dettagli durante il processo di prenotazione. \- [Camere condivise a Milano](https://helphousing.com/it/alloggio-a-milano/stanze-condivise). Questa è un'opzione ancora più economica per il flat-sharing. Milano vanta un ottimo sistema di trasporto pubblico composto da metropolitana, autobus e treni urbani e autobus e treni suburbani. Puoi anche trovare diversi mezzi di trasporto alternativi ad un prezzo molto economico come taxi, Uber e car/bike/moto sharing. [Clicca qui](https://www.atm.it/it/ViaggiaConNoi/Abbonamenti/Pagine/Tipologie.aspx) per vedere tutti i tipi di abbonamenti per il trasporto pubblico ATM. I giovani sotto i 27 anni pagano solo 22,00 € al mese! Mentre la normale tessera mensile per adulti costa 39 €. #### **Viaggi locali e nazionali in treno** La rete ferroviaria italiana è buona e abbastanza veloce. Puoi viaggiare con i treni veloci e pagare circa 20 euro se prenoti i biglietti prima, ti iscrivi alle newsletter o cerchi degli sconti. In questo modo potrai visitare molte altre città italiane da Milano, come: Venezia, Roma, Torino, Firenze, Bologna o Napoli! ![](https://app.helphousing.com/upload/web/cost-of-living-in-milan-for-students-food.jpg) ### **Cibo e ristorazione a Milano** Il budget per la spesa, se compri dai supermercati locali, sarà di circa 150/200 euro al mese. Aziende come Esselunga, Lidl o Penny Market hanno alcuni dei prezzi più bassi e comunque prodotti di buona qualità. Se pranzi o ceni in un ristorante di fascia media, considera che un pasto con antipasto e piatto di pasta può costarti circa 20 euro. Se aggiungi il secondo piatto (carne o pesce), considera tra i 10 e i 20 euro in più. Ci sarà la quota fissa per il servizio, ma la mancia non è obbligatoria qui (a differenza degli Stati Uniti!) #### **Alcuni consigli per risparmiare sul cibo:** La caffetteria dell'università di solito offre pasti e bevande a buon prezzo. Ma il vero punto di forza è lo _street food_: tranci di pizza a 2 o 3 euro, sandwich deliziosi, gelati e cibo multiculturale dai vari locali della città. Nella maggior parte dei bar o pub c'è l'opzione d'asporto ed è molto più conveniente che se si sceglie di mangiare o bere al tavolo. Pertanto, se il tuo obiettivo è quello di risparmiare, puoi semplicemente ordinare e gustare a casa con i tuoi amici o fare un picnic nel bellissimo parco Sempione. Un altro modo per mangiare ad un prezzo accessibile è andare ad un aperitivo - di solito tra le 18 e le 21 - dove, se prendi un drink, a soli circa 6/10 euro puoi avere accesso ad un buffet gratuito. ### **Costo delle attività nel tempo libero a Milano** Per l'intrattenimento e il tempo libero a Milano si possono aggiungere altri 30/50 euro a settimana. [Aeroporto di Milano Linate](https://www.aeroporto.net/aeroporto-milano-linate/ "Aeroporto di Milano Linate") # Collegamenti da e per l’aeroporto di Milano Linate Tutti i mezzi pubblici e i transfer privati da e per l'Aeroporto di Milano Linate. Come arrivare nel centro di Milano e come raggiungere le località vicine. Aggiornato a aprile 2026 - Alloggi - [Noleggio - - [Voli](https://www.booking.com/flights/index.it.html?aid=311303&label=Aeroporto.net__FormTop_Tabs__Collegamenti__LIN) Cerca Hotel, B&B e Case vacanze Destinazione Cerca Data di Arrivo Data di Partenza Persone1234567891011121314151617181920 Camere1234567891011121314151617181920 Cerca L’ **aeroporto di Milano Linate** dista soltanto **7 chilometri dal centro città**, rendendolo il city airport ideale per chi vuole raggiungere Milano in brevissimo tempo dopo lo sbarco. Il mezzo più rapido è la **metropolitana M4**, completamente operativa dal 12 ottobre 2024, che porta a **San Babila in soli 12 minuti** al costo di 2,20 euro: è allo stesso tempo il collegamento più veloce e più economico disponibile. Una volta in centro è facile proseguire verso la **Stazione Centrale di Milano**, uno dei maggiori crocevia ferroviari d’Italia, oppure muoversi per la città sfruttando la capillare rete di tram, autobus e metropolitana gestita da ATM. Chi preferisce utilizzare un’ **auto a noleggio** potrà esplorare Milano e le splendide località turistiche della Lombardia con facilità: lo scalo è direttamente collegato alla **Tangenziale Est** (A51), da cui si raggiungono in pochi chilometri le autostrade A1 e A4. ## Metropolitana per il centro di Milano Dal **12 ottobre 2024**, la **linea M4 della metropolitana** (Linea Blu) collega direttamente l’aeroporto di Linate al centro di Milano, rappresentando l’opzione più veloce ed economica per raggiungere la città. La linea attraversa Milano da est a ovest con 21 fermate e un tempo di percorrenza totale di circa 30 minuti da capolinea a capolinea. ### Metro M4 – Linea Blu La fermata **Linate Aeroporto** si trova a soli 75 metri dall’ingresso del terminal, raggiungibile comodamente a piedi. Da qui, in soli **12 minuti** si raggiunge la fermata di **San Babila**, nel cuore del centro storico, dove è possibile cambiare con la **linea M1** (rossa) per proseguire verso Duomo, Cadorna o la Stazione Centrale. La M4 offre anche interscambi strategici con la **linea M2** a Sant’Ambrogio e con il **servizio ferroviario suburbano** alla fermata Forlanini FS, utile per chi deve prendere treni regionali. Altre fermate di interesse sono Dateo, nelle vicinanze di Porta Venezia, e Tricolore. Il servizio è operativo tutti i giorni dalle **05:40 alle 00:20 circa**, con una frequenza di un treno ogni **3-6 minuti**. Il **biglietto ordinario** costa **2,20 euro** ed è valido per 90 minuti dalla convalida, durante i quali è possibile utilizzare anche bus, tram e altre linee metro. È disponibile anche un **abbonamento giornaliero a 7,60 euro**. I biglietti si acquistano alle macchinette automatiche presenti in stazione, tramite l’app ATM Milano, o con pagamento contactless direttamente ai tornelli. [ATM Milano](https://www.atm.it/) ## Autobus dall'aeroporto al centro di Milano L’ **aeroporto di Linate** è ben collegato con la Stazione Centrale di Milano e con il centro città attraverso diversi servizi di autobus.
