title: Graduate Selection Criteria | Bocconi University
text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Graduate Selection Criteria Exchange Program 2026-27 Selection is based on **merit** evaluation, taking into consideration the following elements: - Student academic weighted credit average ( **WA):** 50% - Number of credits earned ( **NC)** divided by the maximum number of credits that can be earned ( **MAX NC):** 20% - Final degree grade for the Bachelor program - **Laurea Triennale**: 30% The score formula will be the following: The result will be then multiplied by 1000. That will be your final score. The calculation of credits thus includes all the exams of the 1st year - 1st semester - study plan officially taken by **February 3rd, 2026** (included), end of the ordinary exam session. Exams which are not part of the 1st year - 1st semester study plan( **internship, languages, anticipated exams and anticipated curricular supplementary activities)** are not included. Students can indicate up to 10 exchange destinations in order of preference. The Study Abroad office will elaborate the ranking, according to the above-mentioned criteria. Each student will be assigned to the first destination for which there are still places available among the ones s/he listed in her/his application in order of preference. **Please note:** - Courses subdivided in moduleswill be considered as **separated courses** for the academic requirements and exchange score calculation. - If applicants have equal final scores for a specific destination and there is one last slot available, the students' preferences linked to the destination will be used as criteria in order to set the ranking. In case of equal preferences, priority will be given to the student who applied earlier (considering hh:mm:ss). "Show all")

text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Law Requirements Exchange Program 2026-27 Bocconi law students have the chance to join the Exchange Program during the 4th **or** 5th year of their Integrated Master of Arts in Law. The **application** opens once a year, during the **3rd** and **4th year.** Students can be selected for the Exchange Program **only once** for the entire study cycle. Academic Requirements To be eligible for the Exchange Program all students need to meet the following academic requirements: - **GPA**: minimum 22/30 of average weighted on credits, the average is not rounded. - **3rd year students credits**: at least 100% of 1st year and 60% of 2nd year credits registered; - **4th year students credits**: at least 100% of 1st year, 60% of 2nd year credits and 60% of 3rd year credits registered. Please note that: - The calculation of GPA and credits is based on Bocconi exams taken **by the end of the winter exams session**: 3rd February 2026 for the AY 2026/27 selection. **Make sure all your grades are registered** in your Study Plan before the Exchange Program application closes, as only those exams will be considered for the rankings; - If you would like to convert the English certificate to have the exam passed in your Bocconi career and counting for the Exchange program score, it is essential to do it in advance, and in any cases before February 3rd 2026. For further instructions and timeline, please visit the Bocconi [Language Center's website](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center/certificates/language-certification-recognition); - **3rd year students**: exams which are not part of the 1st, 2nd year study plan and 3rd year - 1st semester - study plan are not included; - **4th year students**: exams which are not part of the 1st, 2nd, 3rd year study plan and 4th year - 1st semester - study plan are not included; - **Courses subdivided in modules** will be considered as separated courses for the minimum academic requirements and exchange score calculation; - Some destinations might require a specific minimum GPA. When necessary, the details can be found on the destination brochure. Language Requirements **Minimum** language requirements are sufficient to apply for all the destinations that do not state further requirements other than the language of selection inside the destination brochure. title: Law Selection Criteria | Bocconi University
text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Law Selection Criteria Exchange Program 2026-27 Selection is based on merit evaluation, taking into consideration the **student's academic weighted average** and the **number of** **credits** registered up to February 3rd, 2026: **Student WA + \[0.1 x (Student NC - MIN NC required)\]** 0.1 points will be attributed to every applicant from any Degree Program for each credit above the minimum number of credits required: - For **3rd year** students: 100% of 1st year and 60% of 2nd year credits registered; - For **4th year** students: at least 100% of 1st year , 60% of 2nd year credits and 60% of 3rd year credits registered. These points will be added to the weighted credit average, calculated according to the above criteria. The calculation of credits thus includes all the exams officially taken by **February 3rd, 2026** (included), end of the ordinary exam session. Students can indicate up to 10 exchange destinations in order of preference. The Study Abroad office will elaborate the ranking, according to the above-mentioned criteria. Each student will be assigned to the first destination for which there are still places available among the ones s/he listed in her/his application in order of preference. **Please note:** - Courses subdivided in moduleswill be considered as **separated courses** for the minimum academic requirements and exchange score calculation. - If applicants have equal final scores for a specific destination and there is one last slot available, the students' preferences linked to the destination will be used as criteria in order to set the ranking. In case of equal preferences, priority will be given to the student who applied earlier (considering hh:mm:ss). "Show all")

title: Start of the mobility | Bocconi University
text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Start of the mobility Exchange Program 2026-27 **To prepare yourself for the semester abroad, there are some important things you will need to check:** Before the application **Safety** we remind you to read the **Bocconi Students Travel Risk Policy**(on yoU@B – International SOS) and access **International SOS** services, which include: - Before leaving: information about the country of destination; - while abroad: advice on health and security issues; - in case of emergency: assistance in case of medical or security emergency. Before the application, we encourage you to seek information about the countries you want to apply to and for which you could potentially be selected, by browsing through International SOS portal including **Country Guides** and **Travel, Security and Medical Risk Ratings**. **International SOS is not a medical insurance** and does not replace your personal medical insurance. **Passport/Visa** Please check the immigration policies of the countries you are applying to, and ensure you have a **valid passport**. If a passport and/or visa is required, you will be asked to provide a copy of your valid passport immediately after the selection process to issue the necessary documents. If your passport expires during or within six months after the end of your study abroad program, please renew it as soon as possible. After the selection **Host School Application** Most of the host schools have very strict deadlines for applications (for enrolment, courses selection, accommodation, etc). Please check your e-mail daily as the Study Abroad Office (or the Partner School directly) will forward you instructions and forms/documents to be filled in and returned. **Insurance** Please check the insurance policies of the host country. In case needed, you will have to provide an insurance coverage for your exchange period abroad. Some schools require to purchase their own insurance plan, in some cases upon arrival. **Scholarships** Students selected for those European Universities which take part in the **Erasmus+** Programme will automatically benefit from getting the scholarship. If you are a grantee, you will be required to submit some documents to our Office. For further information, please check: [Erasmus+ Scholarship and [B in Touch](https://bit.unibocconi.it/hc/en-us/categories/4407572389778-Funding). Other international mobilities may have scholarships assigned on a need basis and upon availability of funds.​ For further information, please check [Fees and Funding office website](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/funding). **Enroll in your next academic year** Just like students not participating in the Exchange Program you will need to enroll in the next academic year and choose the elective courses (check the timeline on the Student Administration Center website). However, Exchange Students (who may insert tentative elective choices) have the chance to change their electives choice once back from the exchange period, after the Academic Recognition procedures.​ [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/international-mobility/exchange-program/start-mobility#addtoany "Show all")

Conversion tables imply a one-to-one correspondence between every Partners grades and a Bocconi one. They are based on information given by Partner Schools about their grading distribution (percentages, curves of distribution, description of grades and if any Country specifics) and compared to Bocconi grading system. Being based on such one-to-one association, **some Bocconi grades cannot find any correspondence on some Partners' grading scales**; therefore, **you must be aware that not all the 13 Bocconi grades or the laude (from 18 to 30/30) can be assigned.** After selection, it will be possible to see, through Punto Blu, the conversion table of the school you have been selected for. To access the conversion table from Punto Blu, you can select the "International Mobility" option from the right menu, then choose "Mobility Calls," position yourself, and click on the magnifying glass icon to the right of the "Exchange Program call" while scrolling through the various tabs of the "Call Details." title: Undergraduate programs in Italian: Requirements | Bocconi University
text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Undergraduate programs in Italian: Requirements Exchange Program 2026-27 Bocconi undergraduate students have the chance to join the Exchange Program during the 3rd year of their bachelor's degree. The **application** opens once a year, during the **2nd year** of the study cycle. Academic Requirements To be eligible for the Exchange Program all students need to meet the following academic requirements: - **GPA**: minimum 22/30 average weighted on credits, the average is not rounded. - **Credits**: at least 60% of 1st year credits registered Please note that: - The calculation of GPA and credits is based on Bocconi exams taken **by the end of the winter exams session**: 3rd February 2026 for the AY 2026/27 selection. **Make sure all your grades are registered** in your Study Plan before the Exchange Program application closes, as only those exams will be considered for the rankings; - If you would like to convert the English certificate to have the exam passed in your Bocconi career and counting for the Exchange program score, it is essential to do it in advance, and in any cases before February 3rd 2026. For further instructions and timeline, please visit the Bocconi [Language Center's website](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/language-center/certificates/language-certification-recognition); - Exams which are not part of the 1st year and 2nd year - 1st semester - study plan are not included, as they must be taken during the ordinary exam session; - Courses subdivided in moduleswill be considered as separated courses for the minimum academic requirements and exchange score calculation; - Some destinations might require a specific minimum GPA. When necessary, the details can be found on the Brochure; - If the applicant moves from a bachelor's degree course to another one, exams which are not part of the 1st year and 2nd year - 1st semester - of the NEW study plan are not included. Language Requirements **Minimum** language requirements are sufficient to apply for all the destinations that do not state further requirements other than the language of selection inside the destination brochure. In addition to the minimum requirements for the Exchange program, some partner universities have **additional** language requirements. You can check them in our destination brochure. Please read carefully **both** sections below: To be eligible for the Exchange Program it is always required to have a minimum level of English, French, German, Spanish or Portuguese according to the institutions you are applying for. **Level B2** or higher for **English**, proved by **one** of the options listed below **:** - International Certification: IELTS or TOEFL - University Language Exam **Level B1** or higher for **French, German and Spanish,** proved by **one** of the options listed below: - Citizenship - International Certification - University Language Exam - Enrollment in the Bocconi Second Language Course - Secondary School Diploma – Please contact the Study Abroad office providing any document which can be useful to evaluate your case **Level A2** or higher for **Portuguese,** proved by **one** of the options listed before or by the enrollment to the Bocconi Language

title: Undergraduate Selection Criteria | Bocconi University
text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Undergraduate Selection Criteria Exchange Program 2026-27 For undergraduate students, including students in the BSc in Global Law, selection is based on merit evaluation, taking into consideration the **student's academic weighted average** and the **number of** **credits** pertaining to the 1st year study plan and 2nd year - 1st semester - study plan and registered up to **February 3rd, 2026**. **Student WA + \[0.1 x (Student NC - MIN NC required)\]** 0,1 points (0,098 for CLEACC; 0,102 for BAI, BESS and BEMACS) will be attributed to every applicant from any Degree Program for each credit above the minimum number of credits required (60% of 1st year credits registered). These points will be added to the weighted credit average, calculated according to the above criteria. Students can indicate up to 10 exchange destinations in order of preference. The Study Abroad office will elaborate the ranking, according to the above-mentioned criteria. Each student will be assigned to the first destination for which there are still places available among the ones s/he listed in her/his application in order of preference. **Please note:** - Courses subdivided in moduleswill be considered as **separated courses** for the academic requirements and exchange score calculation. - If applicants have equal final scores for a specific destination and there is one last slot available, the students' preferences linked to the destination will be used as criteria in order to set the ranking. In case of equal preferences, priority will be given to the student who applied earlier (considering hh:mm:ss). "Show all")

text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Exchange Program The Exchange Program offers students a unique international experience, allowing them to spend a term abroad at one of our 293 partner universities in 56 countries across five continents. Through our bilateral agreements, students attending the program will carry out a study term, without paying tuition fees at the host school. However, students are responsible for covering their own travel expenses, accommodation, meals, and any other associated costs. Scholarships, such as those offered by ISU and Erasmus, are available. Courses completed at the partner institution can be recognized, subject to specific rules and procedures that students must adhere to. Students can access the Exchange Program only once during a study program, through an application, upon possession of specific requirements. The Program entails a selection, with subsequent publication of the ranking, which takes place annually. For more details, please refer to the sections below. title: Academic recognition | Bocconi University
text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Academic recognition Integrated Master of Arts in Law (AY 2025-26) **EXAMS RECOGNITION** Students applying to the Free Mover Summer can recognize **only one** course, which will be registered the Bocconi academic career with a grade out of thirty. In case there is no indication of a grade, it will not be possible to recognize the exam (i.e.: pass/fail grading system is not valid). Before the Summer Program The partner school course you wish to attend must have a corresponding Bocconi course and it has to be approved by the Degree Program Director The program must be approved **before** the Summer Program begins. It is the student's responsibility to verify that the recognized course is coherent with his/her Bocconi study plan. Once the Recognition platform is available, you must send the recognition request to the Degree Program Director in order to obtain his/her preliminary approval. In order to do so you need to **upload** to the platform an overall description of the Summer course you wish to attend. The Degree Program Director has to receive all the major information on the course (e.g. course description - objectives, contents, lectures and/or special workloads, written/oral exam, the number of credits assigned to the course and/or the number of classroom and lecture hours, the local instructor's contacts). After the Summer Program Upload the partner school’s official transcript of records (mentioning course, grade and credits) to the Recognition platform and proceed with the recognition. Exams that CANNOT be recognized are: - foreign language exams and computer tests; - courses that are not coherent with the student's study plan; - list of courses for which credits cannot be granted if taken abroad (please refer to the Guide to the University). text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Free Mover Semester Graduate Please refer to the a.y. 2024-25 Guide, in order to get all the necessary information in terms of: academic and language requirements, possible destinations, application procedure and timeline, academic recognition. Requirements Only qualified students can apply for the Free-Mover experience and they are required to prove the following before departure: - **Course year**: the period abroad must be the 1st or 2nd semester of the 2ndyear; - **Credits**: at least **16 credits** of their 1st year registered before semesters departures (the Exchange Program rules on credits apply). - **Language Requirements**: Language of instruction of the Host University - the Exchange Program language applies\* - at Level B1 or higher for all languages EXCEPT English language which must be at a minimum Level B2 (obtained with a minimum grade of 24/30) or higher. - The language of selection indicated by Università Bocconi in the Exchange Program destinations is to be considered **compulsory** also for the Free-Movers. In addition, each hosting School has its own requirements which have to be fulfilled by the applicant. Destinations The lists provided on this page are designed to assist current Bocconi students in finding a suitable partner university for the Free-Mover Semester since most of the partner schools do not accept free-movers if they have already an Exchange agreement with Bocconi. The universities listed in the pdf document "possible destinations" are those **who have accepted** Bocconi Students in the past. This does not guarantee these schools will accept students in the future. Schools which inform Bocconi that they **do not** accept Free-Movers students are listed in a different pdf document. The following information may help students decide which universities offer the most suitable courses for their study plan. **Faculty:** This indicates the faculties opened in the past at each partner university. For example, Law only means only Bocconi law students may apply. **Level:** Indicates whether each partner accepted undergraduate or graduate or law students from Bocconi or both. **Language:** The language required - but not the additional requirements if any - is the same as that indicated by Università Bocconi for the Exchange Program and it is compulsory **also** for the Free-Movers. In addition, we strongly advise students to check if there is a link for each country to the relevant Government visa information website. These contain current advice about visa procedures for each country and should be used as the primary source of information about visas. The list of foreign Universities is to be considered as **the only valid list** in terms of possibility of recognition of the tuition received by Free-Mover Semester students at foreign institutions. Any other destination must be endorsed ex-ante, on a case-by-case basis, by the Study Abroad Office. The request, accompanied by a **letter of motivation** and information material on the University selected, has to be presented before enrolling in the foreign university as a Free-Mover Semester student and sent to the Study Abroad Office through B in Touch. title: Free Mover Semester | Bocconi University
text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Free Mover Semester Students interested in spending a semester abroad without participating in the Exchange Program can enroll as **Free-Movers** ( **Fee-paying Visiting Students** or **Independent Students** or **Contract Students**) at some foreign Universities where they can study for a semester on a fee-paying basis. The difference between the Free-Mover and the Exchange is the admission process which is freely defined by the host institutions and out of any Bocconi responsibility or involvement. On top, Bocconi has its own process since a maximum of 10 students in each destination will be authorized to recognize their courses taken abroad during their Free-Mover Semester. This number considers the entire a.y. (considering both first and second term). Bocconi click day will be each year in May. Please be aware that admission processes abroad may have **different timelines**. Students are strongly advised **not to undertake any binding financial commitment** before the release of the updated information and/or having secured their place at Punto Blu. Please refer to the Guides available in the following sections for each degree level. Please note that the Free-Mover Semester initiative is **not** open to the following Degree courses: BSc in International Politics and Government, MSc in International Management Global Experience and MSc in Finance Global Experience Track as they have already a guaranteed Exchange experience. For A.Y. 2026-27 ### Timing and deadlines - Deadline for obtaining the minimum credits and uploading the language certificates (if required to satisfy the minimum language requirement): **at least** **5 working days before departure** - Publication of possible destinations and guides: **18 March 2026 (last update 4 May 2026)** - Click day, opening days - Integrated Master of Arts in Law: **5 May 2026 at 12 pm (Italian time)** - Bachelor in Global Law: **6 May 2026 at 12 pm (Italian time)** - Undergraduate programs: **7 May 2026 at 12 pm (Italian time)** - Graduate program: **8 May 2026 at 12 pm (Italian time)** - System closure for departures in 2026-27: **1 February 2027** - Confirmation: Students must inform the Study Abroad Office via B in Touch once they have uploaded the required documents on Punto Blu. **Please note that:** - Students who withdraw from the Exchange Program cannot apply for the Free-Mover Semester. - Students who are in waiting list for the Exchange Program can apply for the Free-Mover Semester but, if they apply for this initiative (by reserving a place at Punto Blu), their name will be removed from the waiting list by the Study Abroad staff and will not be contacted any further. **Check the appropriate Guide for a successful experience abroad and in order to get all the necessary information in terms of requirements, destinations, procedures, timeline, and academic recognition.** [**Undergraduate "Undergraduate Guide") [**Bachelor in Global Law "Bachelor in Global Law Guide") [**The Free Mover Semester Cycle of Life**](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/FREE%20MOVER%20_CycleOfLife_2026.pdf "The Free Mover Semester Cycle of Life") [**Graduate "Graduate Guide") [**Law "Law Guide") ## How we support you Our role in the Free Mover process includes: \-

Participation in a program in the summer of the first year, second year or before will not be recognized, as well as the participation in a program in the summer of the fifth year. The application to the Free Mover Summer will be on-hold and the recognition platform will not be available until the Bocconi requirements are met. If an applicant does not meet the requirements before the beginning of the Summer Program, the application to the Free Mover Summer will be declined. title: Free Mover Summer - How to apply | Bocconi University
text: International Mobility [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-mobility) # Free Mover Summer - How to apply Integrated Master of Arts in Law (AY 2025-26) _**Latest update - April 16, 2026**_ Students wishing to attend a Summer Program in **Summer 2026** will have to formally apply at Punto Blu **starting from April 27, 2026 and no later than July 17, 2026**. **The relevant dates will be updated on this page once available.** Entry requirements and travel restriction to enter the Host Country must be verified by students themselves prior to departure, in order to guarantee that the Program is carried out in compliance with applicable health requirements and visa law. Students are responsible for the Host School tuition fees, travel, board and lodging expenses during the Summer Program. Participants are also required to be covered by a comprehensive international sickness and accident insurance policy while abroad. Before the Application - **check** if you meet the Bocconi the requirements (see "Free Mover Summer Law") section); - **check** if you meet the partner school requirements; - **ensure** you can meet the partner school application deadlines and procedures; - **check** if the course you want to attend and recognize is coherent with your Bocconi study plan; How to Apply **Apply** to the Free Mover Summer at Punto Blu, uploading: 1\. a valid English certificate - if not already registered in your career (see "Free Mover Summer Law") section); 2\. the ‘Free Mover Summer 2026 - Student info' document (available below). It is necessary to **save** the application receipt. - [Free Mover Summer 2026 - Student info](https://www.unibocconi.it/sites/default/files/Free_Mover%2BSummer%2B2026_Student_info_0.docx) After the Application The Study Abroad Office will **check** if you meet the Bocconi academic and language requirements and will **send** you a notification once the recognition platform is available in your yoU@B diary. Through this tool you can **send** a recognition request for the course you wish to attend during the Summer Program to the Director of the Integrated Master of Arts in Law for the course with or without correspondence, in order to obtain his/her preliminary approval. Please be aware that - during the request procedure - you are required to attach a detailed course syllabus or to provide the website link related to the course. After the Bocconi recognition **approval**, you can carry out the **partner** school enrolment procedures. While applying to the Free Mover Summer, students can indicate **one Summer Program only.** "Show all")

title: International Networks | Bocconi University
text: About Us [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/about-us) International Networks Overview # International Networks Bocconi University is committed to providing students with an educational experience that **goes beyond national borders**, preparing them to address challenges and explore opportunities on a global scale. Through collaboration with academic institutions and networks worldwide, Bocconi offers students access to a truly international perspective. Our **exchange programs**, **Double Degrees** and **other study abroad opportunities** allow students to immerse themselves in diverse cultures, acquire intercultural skills and develop a deeper understanding of the geopolitical and economic dynamics shaping the global business landscape. Since our first exchange agreements in 1974, our network has continuously expanded, providing students with increasing opportunities overseas. Our extensive global network includes **290** **partner schools** in **55 countries** across six continents. Additionally, Bocconi proudly holds founding membership in prestigious networks such as the CEMS, PIM - International Management Network, the Themis Law Network and CIVICA, the European University of Social Sciences. ![Partner's Schools ### Partner Schools [Explore](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/about-us/international-networks/partner-schools) ![group of international ### Erasmus+ [Explore](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/international-mobility/erasmus-scholarship) ### Network and Alliances [Explore](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/about-us/international-networks/network-and-alliances) [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/about-us/international-networks#addtoany "Show all")

text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Current students Overview # Current Students As a member of the Bocconi community, you now have access to a wide range of resources designed to support international students. The University offers an abundance of opportunities — from guidance on immigration procedures and information on work permits, to a dynamic array of campus activities — and we encourage you to make the most of them throughout your studies here. ## Important to Know ### Permit of Stay Renewal If you are a **NON-EU student**, you must **keep your immigration status updated**. The Permit of Stay (Permesso di soggiorno) must be renewed at least 60 days before the permit expires. For detailed information on how to renew your residence permit, click the button below. Renew your residence permit at the following link: ### Requesting Official Academic Transcript Before renewing your Permit of Stay to remain a student in Italy, you must request an **Official Academic Transcript** (for immigration purposes) certifying that you have **successfully passed** at least one exam for the first renewal and at least two exams for each subsequent renewal of the permit, except for in circumstances beyond one’s control. You may request the transcript using the cert@B procedure, available on the **yoU@B Diary** \> **Certificates**. The process usually takes 4 working days, therefore it is suggested to submit your request well before your permit renewal appointment. ### Working as a Student in Italy Non-Italian citizens with a residence permit for study are allowed to work in order to support themselves financially. In the case of **subordinate work**, the law (art. 14, par. 4, DPR 394/99) requires that the job shall not exceed 20 hours per week, which may also be cumulated over 52 weeks. Part-time work can either be “vertical” or “horizontal", meaning you can work 20 hours per week for 12 months or up to 40 hours per week for 6 months, considering that the annual limit is 1,040 hours. This is because your primary activity in Italy must be studying. Please also keep in mind that any work contract cannot extend beyond the validity of your student residence permit. ### Getting an Internship in Italy As clarified in the Italian National Labor Inspectorate note of 14 February 2023, **a residence permit for study allows students to take part in all curricular traineeships (internships)** included in their degree program or professional training for which the permit was issued. Since traineeships — curricular or extracurricular — are not considered employment, the legal limits on work activities do not apply (see section 'Working as a Student in Italy'). Bocconi has built strong, long-standing relationships with leading Italian and international companies as well as institutions. Through these connections, the University actively supports graduates as they transition into the job market. Discover more about Bocconi Career Services here: ### Job Seeking Permit #### (Permesso Attesa Occupazione) The Job Seeking Permit allows non-EU students — who possess an accredited undergraduate/graduate degree, PhD or post-graduate specialized degree — to remain in Italy for a period of maximum 12 months and search for a job. You can **convert** your Permit of Stay for study to a Job Seeking Permit (Permesso Attesa Occupazione), as long as you begin the process **two months before your current permit of stay expires.** For detailed information on how to do so, please go to the **Relocation and Immigration** section on **BinTouch** in your yoU@B Agenda. ## Bocconi Student Life As an international student, your university experience goes far beyond the classroom. Student life at Bocconi is vibrant, multicultural and safe, with the city center of Milan minutes away. You can enhance your skills at the Language Center and IT Education Center, stay active at the state-of-the-art Bocconi Sports Center, show your school spirit with the latest apparel from the Bocconi Shop, and much more. Campus Life Campus Life is the ultimate hub for cultural, artistic, social and volunteer activities at Bocconi. In addition to supporting student associations, the University also provides counseling services and initiatives on self-empowerment and wellbeing — helping students make the most of their university experience. Click [here](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/campus-life) for upcoming activities and opportunities on campus! Language Center The Language Center at Bocconi develops and coordinates foreign language courses, proposing both curricular and extra-curricular options to help students prepare for exams and earn certifications. It also provides various services to promote learning, such as tutoring and language exchanges. Click [here](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/welcome-days/language-center-glance) to find out more about the Language Center! IT Education Center The IT Education Center (ITEC) oversees ICT education at Bocconi University, providing supplementary courses and certifications, with faculty drawn from top ICT professionals and tutors selected from Bocconi’s finest students. Click [here](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/welcome-days/it-education-center-glance) to see what else the ITEC has to offer! Sports Sports are an integral part of Bocconi’s urban campus, supported by modern facilities featuring an Olympic-size swimming pool, fitness and wellness areas, an elevated running track, various playing courts, and much more. The Bocconi Sports Team is the University’s athletics organization, offering year-round opportunities for both individual and team athletes to participate in intramural or national games and tournaments. Click [here](https://www.bocconisport.eu/en) to learn more about the Bocconi Sports Center! Its editorial system also includes one of Italy’s largest independent bookstores, offering a wide range of academic, professional, non-fiction and fiction titles in both Italian and English. text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Freshly enrolled students - When you arrive [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/freshly-enrolled-students-when-you-arrive) # Permit of Stay **Within 8 working days** of their arrival in Italy, all **NON-EU** citizens who hold a valid student visa for Italy must apply for a **permit of stay for study purposes** (Permesso di soggiorno per motivi di studio). The permit of stay is issued by the Police (Questura - Ufficio Immigrazione). Applicants must submit their application through the Post Office (Poste Italiane). N.B. Regular freshmen students who are applying for a First Permit of Stay will be able to **pick up a Permit of Stay Kit** at any post office or during Welcome Days starting from the 20th of August at the B in Touch Point (Piazza Sraffa 11) until stocks are exhausted. _**IMPORTANT!**_ 1. According to Italian legislation, **you are required to provide the University with your Permit of Stay and subsequent renewals**. All information on how to proceed are available on [yoU@B](https://youatb.unibocconi.it/) Student Diary. 2. If your Schengen Permit of Stay does not cover the entire period of mobility in Italy or if this period **is superior to 360 days**, you must instead apply for a Permit of Stay in Italy. 3. **Non-EU incoming exchange students** holding a **Schengen permit of stay for study purposes issued by a European Union country (Schengen Area)**, that allows for the exemption from the entry visa and covers the entire mobility period (less than 360 days), do not have to apply for the permit of stay while in Italy. They must instead fill in a [**declaration of and submit it within 8 working days from their arrival at any Police Station in Milan (the one closest to Bocconi University is located at Via Tabacchi 6). You must always carry a copy of the declaration of presence, as you may be asked to show it in case of police checks. For all further information you can refer to the dedicated section of **BinTouch** on your YoU@B agenda (Relocation and Immigration>First Permit of Stay and Fiscal Code) or to the [YesMilano website](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/study/how-to/residence-permit-students). The document should be submitted by the host in person to the local Police station ("Commissariato di zona" of the area where you live) or sent via: • certified mail (“PEC”) to [immig.quest.mi@pecps.poliziadistato.it](mailto:immig.quest.mi@pecps.poliziadistato.it) • registered mail (raccomandata A/R) to the local Police station ("Commissariato di zona" – Ufficio Immigrazione). It must be dated and signed by the person who provides the accommodation, together with a copy of the student’s and the host’s ID, and a copy of their residence permit (if a non-EU citizen) - Post office receipt + receipt of payment of €70,46 paid at the Post Office for the permit of stay - During the appointment, students will have to specify their home address in Milan For further information, please visit: [http://www.portaleimmigrazione.it/](http://www.portaleimmigrazione.it/) [http://www.interno.it/](http://www.interno.it/) [http://www.poste.it/](http://www.poste.it/) [http://www.poliziadistato.it/](http://www.poliziadistato.it/) Collecting your Permit of Stay After successfully completing the two steps of the application for the Permit of Stay, students will receive the next appointment at the Immigration Office for the collection of their permit of stay. Only students with an Italian phone number will receive a confirmation via SMS from the Police. Once you're notified that your Residence Permit Card is ready for collection, visit the designated location (as instructed in the notification). Bring with you: a valid **passport** \+ **original residence permit application receipt.** It is possible to track the status of the Permit of Stay application on the [Portale Immigrazione website](https://www.portaleimmigrazione.it/ELI2ImmigrazioneWEB/Pagine/StartPage.aspx) by accessing it with the user ID and password found on the Permit of Stay post office receipt ("ricevuta"). **IMPORTANT**: when typing your password, do not include the dash (-). _Please make sure to regularly check the Portale Immigrazione for updates and confirmation of your appointment._ Post Offices closest to Bocconi - Via Cordusio, 4 (Central Post Office of Milan) - **English, Spanish and Chinese speaking staff**. text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Freshly enrolled students - Before you arrive [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/freshly-enrolled-students-you-arrive) # Academics Deep dive into the Bocconi University academics world. Find below all practical core details on deadlines, class and exam schedule according to your student profile. Regular Students Before the beginning of your academic year at Bocconi, check out: - The [Guide to the University](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/guide-university "Guide to the University") with respect to your specific degree course - [Timetable calendar](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/timetables-calendars-and-rooms/academic-calendar "Academic Calendar") with the key dates for the academic years - [Course profiles](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/courses-offered-academic-programs-2025-2026-ay "Courses offered in Academic Programs 2025-2026 a.y. ") based on your specific program - Surf your [yoU@B](https://youatb.unibocconi.it/) Student Diary! A reserved area online available to all Bocconi students. Through yoU@B, students can receive information from the University, use online services dedicated to teaching, administer some activities in their academic careers, register to exams, check dates, times and rooms for both exams and graduation sessions, check class timetables and so on. Remember to log in and enter your student ID number as the username and your password. All enrolled students will receive an e-mail granting them access to their yoU@B Diary. It may include a mix of courses of the 1° and the 2° year of the Bocconi MSc program, according to the courses' matching between Bocconi and Home School. Bocconi credit system is ECTS equivalent. Before the beginning of the academic year, you will be asked – if foreseen by your individual study plan – to choose your electives at Bocconi, with the possibility to change 2° semester electives during the “add/drop period” in January. title: Fiscal code | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Freshly enrolled students - Before you arrive [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/freshly-enrolled-students-you-arrive) # Fiscal code The Italian tax code ("codice fiscale") is an alphanumeric code of 16 characters issued for free by the Revenue Agency to identify Italian citizens and foreign citizens. The Revenue Agency is a non-economic public body that is mainly responsible for collecting tax revenues, providing services and assistance to taxpayers. **N.B.: The tax code you find in the ISEU certificate, the one you can see in the portal during the admission process or on your YoU@B agenda is not the official one but is automatically generated. To obtain the official one, you must request it from the Italian Revenue Agency as it is the body in charge of issuing the Fiscal Code.** You will need your own "codice fiscale" to: - open a bank account - register at the National Healthcare Service (SSN) - apply for the health card - sign other type of contracts (i.e. phone number) International students can apply for a Fiscal Code once in Italy in one of the Revenue Agencies/Agenzia delle Entrate. Find further information on that [at this link](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/study/how-to/get-italian-tax-code-codice-fiscale). In addition to this procedure, if you are an international BSc or MSc student (including Double Degree students), you can request a “Codice Fiscale” through a special agreement between the Revenue Agency and Bocconi. Around mid-July, instructions on how to request your fiscal code through this procedure will be shared with all regularly enrolled BSc and MSc students. Please note that this service will be available for a limited time only and is reserved to students that are at least 18 years old when the procedure is activated. [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/freshly-enrolled-students-you-arrive/fiscal-code#addtoany "Show all")

title: Health Services | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Freshly enrolled students - Before you arrive [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/freshly-enrolled-students-you-arrive) # Health Services All international students are required to have appropriate health insurance. In Italy, the National Health System is provided by a public health care service (SSN). Only foreign citizens with a valid permit of stay when needed may apply for the service offered by the ASL (local branch of the National Health Care Service). Learn more on the **Italian National Health System** on the [YesMilano webpage](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/study/how-to/national-health-service-students-step-step). ## Medical Services Emergency Rooms **Single Emergency Number: 112** Access to the hospital Emergency Room is regulated by an urgency assessment system, triage, which identifies priorities for providing care. Upon arrival at the emergency room, individuals receive an immediate assessment of their level of urgency by health workers, with the assignment of a color code that establishes the priority of access to care based on the severity of the case and regardless of the order of arrival at the hospital. Each patient is assigned a color code based on the clinical severity assessed: - Red code: very critical, life threatening, top priority, immediate access to treatment. - Yellow code: moderately critical, presence of evolving risk, potentially life threatening, non-deferrable service. - Green code: not very critical, no evolving risks, deferred service. - White code: non-critical, non-urgent patients. After the triage, the emergency room doctor completes the patient's clinical assessment, confirming or adapting the code assigned at entrance, based on the findings made. If, after medical intervention, the patient is discharged with a White Code (as it has been clinically shown that the service provided was not urgent), a €25.00 fee must be paid. All services provided that are identified by the emergency room doctor's clinical assessment as Green, Yellow or Red Codes are free. **When accessing the Emergency Room, you should:** - bring your Health Card/Regional Services Card or at least your Fiscal Code card, as well as any certificates exempting payment. - bring your health records from any previous hospital admissions, laboratory or additional tests, etc. - know the names and details of any treatments in use. **How to find the Emergency Room closest to you:** [SALUTILE Pronto is an app from the Lombardy Region which can be used to consult the list of all Emergency Rooms in the Lombardy Region. You can also see the number of people queuing at that time and the crowding index. You can view the facilities closest to you on the map and get directions to the chosen Emergency Room. Download the application for free and you can: > see the number of patients waiting, divided by priority code (Red, Yellow, Green and White); > check the crowding index of the facility compared to available resources; > get directions to the nearest facility. The Continuity of Care Service (Continuità Assistenziale, formerly Guardia Medica) intervenes during the hours when general practitioners' offices are closed, for illnesses that cannot be treated by an attending physician the following day, therefore in the event that it cannot be postponed. At the end of the medical examination, the doctor issues a completed two-copy information form (form M). One copy is intended for the attending physician (or the health facility, in case of hospitalization) and the other is kept by the Continuity of Care doctor. **Phone numbers to access the service** To contact a Continuity of Care Doctor by phone, call: 800 193 344 Milan area 800 103 103 West Milanese and Rhodense area 848 800 804 Melegnano and Martesana area 800 940 000 Lodi area The Service is available from 8:00am to 8:00pm on pre-holidays, holidays, Saturdays and Sundays and from 8:00pm to 8:00am every night. Provide the technical operator with the information required to request intervention, namely: > Full name, age and address; > General information of the caller and any relationship with the patient (if a different person); > Type of problem, signs and symptoms and time of their occurrence The technical operator will then put the individual in contact with the local doctor on duty. **The doctor may intervene in the following ways:** > Limited to telephone advice; > Ask the user to go to the Continuity of Care Center for an outpatient assessment; > Carry out a home visit, if, in his/her opinion, the patient's clinical condition requires it; > Refer the patient to more appropriate facilities and/or activate an Emergency Service through the Single European Emergency Number 112, if the condition cannot be managed at home. **The doctor may provide:** - Pharmaceutical prescriptions for non-deferrable treatment and covering a cycle of treatment not exceeding 48-72 hours; - Certification of ill health limited to the days coinciding with the holiday, pre-holiday and night shifts of the Continuity of Care Service. **The doctor will NOT provide:** - Nursing services not related to the medical examination; - Prescription renewals for ongoing treatments; - Non-deferrable registrations from other doctors in the SSN prescription book; - Certificates for sporting activities; - Certificates for returning to school; - Certificates of ill health for non-shift workers; - Stitches; - Prescription of diagnostic-instrumental tests or specialist visits. The medical center will mainly meet the needs of non-residents in Milan and those who have difficulty accessing the services of their general practitioner. - The medical center is NOT an emergency service. In the event of an emergency, you should always call 112, the European emergency number, or the Bocconi emergency number, +39 02 5836.2121, which will activate the ambulance service if necessary. - This is a first-level internal medicine service, which can carry out medical examinations with a medical report and provide medications and prescriptions (however, it will NOT be able to issue prescriptions covered by the National Health Service, as by law they can only be issued by your general practitioner/family doctor). - This service is only available to members of the Bocconi community and cannot be extended to others (family members and acquaintances). Timelines, procedures and contact information will be available in the Health and Safety widget in the yoU@B Diary and on the Intranet; please write to [hse@unibocconi.it](mailto:hse@unibocconi.it) for any questions you may have. Stationing of Croce Bianca Ambulance Considering the daily presence of over 15,000 people on our campus, the University has decided to guarantee the ongoing daily presence of the Associazione Croce Bianca Milano Onlus. An ambulance with two health workers is available Monday through Friday from 9:30am to 5:30pm. They can provide first aid/healthcare monitoring to anyone who comes to the infirmary, located on the mezzanine floor at Via Bocconi 12 (e.g. taking vital signs and assessing the need for transport to an emergency room). In addition, the presence of Croce Bianca Milano allows prompt interventions in the event of a health emergency (accident/illness) on our campus. The ambulance service can be activated by calling the Bocconi University emergency number on campus: +39 02.5836.2121. Individual Counseling Service Bocconi offers a free Individual Counseling service, which aims to help you identify and resolve situations of difficulty and discomfort, as well as develop your personal resources, through a track tailored for you. The service is available in Italian, English or French. title: Italian and Bocconi Academic System | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Freshly enrolled students - Before you arrive [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/freshly-enrolled-students-you-arrive) # Italian and Bocconi Academic System The Italian Education System is made of a 13-year cycle of pre-university education (5-year elementary school cycle, 3-year middle school cycle and 5-year high school cycle). The University reform of 1999 transformed the organization of the Italian university, changing the structure of both the study plan and the degree programs in the fields of Economics and Management from one long four-year cycle to the so-called 3 plus 2, divided into two cycles (undergraduate and graduate). The two study cycles are to be considered separate; at the end of each, a final exam is required, as well as the awarding of a diploma and the certification of the title obtained. Once the 3-year cycle has been completed the student can decide whether to enter the job market or continue the university studies by enrolling in a graduate program (Master of Science or a Specialized Master). In addition, Bocconi University's School of Law offers a five-year Integrated Master of Arts in Giurisprudenza (“Law”) program in Italian. To access the university education system, there are some governmental requirements that must be fulfilled. Each university has then its own access requirements and educational approach. Since the start of the Bocconi University graduate programs, the selection process has been distinct from that of the undergraduate one; therefore, admission to an undergraduate degree program does not imply the automatic admission to a Master of Science program. Check Bocconi [access requirements](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/applying-bocconi "Applying to Bocconi"). You must have a 12-year diploma. If you have an 11-year diploma it must be integrated with 1 full year of university. There are then specific requirements for different type of diplomas: - American diploma with a minimum of 3 APs - IB full diploma (no IB certificates) - British diploma with minimum 3 A Levels and at least 6 GCE If your home country educational system requires a qualifying exam for university admission applicants must pass this exam to access the Italian University System as well. For all further information, please visit [this "Secondary School Diplomas") To access admissions to a Master of Science program, students must hold a Bachelor Diploma (1st cycle qualification) that must be suitable and valid for the purposes of accessing a 2nd cycle of studies (like a Master of Science Program is). Bocconi University deems as valid a Bachelor Diploma (I-level degree/undergraduate Program) with at least: - 180 educational credits (ECTS) - a length of at least 3 years - not professional - comparable to an Italian Bachelor Program - issued by a foreign University that is recognized within the educational system of the Country issuing the degree which allow continuing studies in a post-graduate (II level) program (i.e. an undergraduate degree issued by a US University in Greece must be recognized as valid for the purposes of continuing studies in a post-graduate program in the United States). For all further information, visit [this "Valid Recognized Qualifications") In Bocconi,

title: Italian and Bocconi Academic System | Bocconi University
text: - not professional - comparable to an Italian Bachelor Program - issued by a foreign University that is recognized within the educational system of the Country issuing the degree which allow continuing studies in a post-graduate (II level) program (i.e. an undergraduate degree issued by a US University in Greece must be recognized as valid for the purposes of continuing studies in a post-graduate program in the United States). For all further information, visit [this "Valid Recognized Qualifications") In Bocconi, exams and assessments are marked out of thirty (for exams) or given a pass/fail grade and are always individual. A mark of between 0 and 17 out of thirty is considered unsatisfactory. A mark of between 18 and 30 out of thirty is considered satisfactory. The examining board may award "lode" (cum laude) to students who are awarded thirty out of thirty (30/30). A 30 "cum laude" is awarded the value of 31. The assessment methods may be different for attending and non-attending students. Students are considered "attending" if they meet the course attendance requirements established by the faculty member. Registration for written oral, partial exams and seminars is compulsory and exams are held in person on Campus. Withdrawing from an exam is equivalent to not taking the exam. Handing in written exam papers (whether they are partial or general exams) specifically means accepting the mark the teacher gives the paper, no matter what it is. For all further details, please refer to the [Guide to the University](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/current-students/guide-university "Guide to the University") "Show all")

title: Academics for exchange students: Course selection | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Academics for exchange students: Course selection The **Course Selection** for the Fall semester of the AY 2026-2027 will run from **August 24-26, 2026,** through the yoU@B student diary at [**agenda.unibocconi.it**](https://agenda.unibocconi.it/ "agenda.unibocconi.it") **.** Courses will be assigned on a **first come-first served** basis and no waiting list will be available. To maximize your chances of securing classes, we recommend staying flexible and expanding your pre-approved tentative course list to include backup options, in case you are unable to register for your preferred classes. Exchange students will also have the possibility to change their study plan during the **Add/Drop period** scheduled between **September 7 and 15**, 2026\. After the Add/Drop deadline **no changes** will be allowed on your study plan. **All courses** included in the students' study plans **will appear** in their Official Bocconi final **transcripts**. Since exchange students can choose from courses across all years and Degree programs, class schedule **overlaps** may occur. Class groups with the same course code may have different schedules and may be assigned a different number of credits. In case you need assistance in building your study plan, you can contact the [**Academic Advisors**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/programs/current-students/services/academic-advisors). **STUDY PLAN GUIDELINES** 1. Exchange students must enroll in a **minimum of 1 and a maximum of 5 courses** per semester while at Bocconi and must ensure that they also satisfy their home university requirements. 2. **Undergraduate** students can select only courses at the undergraduate level (identified with code 30xxx). **Graduate** students are allowed to choose both undergraduate (30xxx) and graduate (20xxx/21xxx and 50xxx) courses. 3. Students who wish to complete all their exams during the first exam session must **ensure** there are no schedule conflicts among their exams. The exam schedule is available at the following link 4. If **two** final **exams** are scheduled on the **same** day and at the same **time**, students can select both courses and sit the exams in **different available exam sessions**. Bocconi University has multiple exam sessions, with Fall semester exams held in December, January and February and Spring semester exams held in May, June/July. **Additional Course Selection Rules**: · **Language courses**: exchange students **cannot** **add language courses** to their study plan · **Attending vs. non-attending**: students may complete courses as either attending or non-attending. There is no need to specify this status when selecting courses, as it is managed directly with the instructor after the start of classes. Students must follow the instructions outlined in the course syllabi or explained by the instructor in class **Course restrictions**: - some courses have specific prerequisites: carefully review the **"Suggested Background Knowledge"** section in the [course profile](https://didattica.unibocconi.eu/ts/tsn_ord_ir.php) section. - some courses might have overlapping contents/program: students should consult instructors to determine whether they can take both courses simultaneously. **Special Programs Requirement** s **CEMS** students are required to select their courses from the [**CEMS specific list**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/programs/current-students/services/courses). For further information on CEMS requirements, please refer to [cems@unibocconi.it](mailto:cems@unibocconi.it) **THEMIS students** can find further information about courses approved by the THEMIS network

title: Academics for exchange students: Exams | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Academics for exchange students: Exams Exchange students are allowed to take exams during the available **official exam sessions,** within their exchange period and **on Bocconi** **premises** only. Students who sit and pass all the exams of their study plan during the first available exam session are free to leave campus starting from the **Earliest Departure Date**. Check the Earliest Departure Date on the [**Academic Calendar**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/programs/current-students/services/academic-calendar-exchange-students). Students are entitled to sit and re-sit exams during the second exam session as well. Exam re-sits are allowed **only in case of failure**. **Registration** for each exam must be carried out within **4 working days** prior to the exam date (Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays are not included), through the yoU@B agenda, in order to have the grades registered. Exam dates and registration deadlines are available at [**this webpage**](https://didattica.unibocconi.eu/esami/index.php). Exams can be either oral or written; some courses might foresee mid-terms. More than one exam may be scheduled on the same day. Exam **rooms** are posted on the student's yoU@B agenda the afternoon of the working day before the exam. **Grades** are assigned on a scale of **30/30**: - 0 to 17: failing grades - 18 to 30: passing grades Exams that award a passing grade cannot be re-sat, while failed exams can be attempted again in the next available session within the exchange period. "Show all")

title: Academics for exchange students: MBA courses | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Academics for exchange students: MBA courses **MBA level** incoming **exchange** students at Bocconi will be eligible to take **graduate (MSc) courses** offered within the Bocconi exchange course catalogue. For a **limited** number of students, however, Bocconi offers the opportunity to take some **MBA courses** belonging to the **SDA Bocconi** School of Management MBA curriculum. These courses are offered in English, and they might change every year, therefore additional information will be provided as the course start date approaches. Students regularly enrolled in the SDA MBA program will have prioritized access, therefore enrollment into MBA classes **cannot be guaranteed** in advance. Places are **limited** and assigned on the basis of the student’s CV, which will be evaluated by the SDA Bocconi MBA office. MBA students will directly be contacted before the course selection with detailed information. "Show all")

title: Academics for exchange students: Transcript of Grades | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Academics for exchange students: Transcript of Grades Incoming exchange students who are enrolled in the exchange program at Bocconi University are provided with instructions on how to autonomously access their **official Bocconi University digital transcript**. After each exam session, the transcript will be updated with the exam results, as soon as these grades are officially registered in the Bocconi systems. This process is not automatic, and might require some time. **Please note**: grades obtained during midterms will not appear on the transcript; only final exams grades will be listed. An official PDF version of the digital transcript will be sent to each partner university Coordinator, at the end of the semester. **Hard copies** are sent to our partner universities **ONLY upon request**. To ensure the security and authenticity of e-transcripts, these documents are released through the Bocconi system and can be verified at this The conversion of Bocconi grades is managed by the student’s home university, based on their grading conversion criteria. title: Fiscal Code's request | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Fiscal Code's request The Italian Tax Code (“ **Codice Fiscale**”) is a personal alphanumeric code (combination of numbers and letters) used to recognize individuals in Italy. It is required when dealing with public offices and/or the public administration. The “Codice Fiscale” is not compulsory. However, incoming exchange students need to obtain one to open a bank account, sign specific contracts (i.e. phone line), register for the National Healthcare Service (SSN). **Please note**: according to the Italian Revenue Agency guidelines, exchange students who are not registered as temporary residents in Milano are [**not** required](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/study/how-to/get-italian-tax-code-codice-fiscale#paragraph-11861) to obtain a fiscal code in order to sign a rental contract. The Codice Fiscale must be requested **after** arrival in Italy. Exchange students can follow the application procedure at this [link](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/study/how-to/get-italian-tax-code-codice-fiscale). The fiscal code application procedure is **free**. Please note that Bocconi University does not provide exchange students with a codice fiscale, and that the one generated automatically through the Bocconi application and the Universitaly application is invalid. [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students/fiscal-codes-request#addtoany "Show all")

title: Getting Around | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Getting Around Please **check out this** [**link**](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/how-get-milano) **if you want to know more on how to get to Milan.** **PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION** Milan public transportation system is managed by Azienda Trasporti Milanesi ( **ATM**) and offers 5 **metro** lines and several **tram** and **bus** lines. More information on how to get around the city with **public transportation** as well as on tickets at this [**link**](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/subway-trams-and-buses). ATM tickets can be purchased directly on a tram, bus or metro contactless with a credit or a debit card. More information on the [**ATM website**](https://www.atm.it/EN/VIAGGIACONNOI/Pages/default.aspx). Students can apply for an **ATM transportation card**, an electronic, rechargeable pass which allows you to travel throughout the Milan urban area by ATM subway, buses and trams. ATM offers different kinds of cards in order to meet all travelers' needs, including a monthly, unlimited pass. Please visit [**ATM website**](https://www.atm.it/en/ViaggiaConNoi/Abbonamenti/Pages/Tesseraelettronic.aspx) for more information. **SHARING MOBILITY** In the last years Milan has embraced several **sharing mobility services** by pursuing a more sustainable and livable city lifestyle. Students can find how to use **bike, car sharing, motorscooter and kick scooter sharing** apps at [**this webpage**](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/articles/kick-scooter-bike-motorscooter-sharing-rental). **CAR** Students who wish to **explore Milan by car** can find useful information **on parking** and **traffic restrictions** and regulations at this [**link**](https://www.yesmilano.it/en/car-sharing). **TAXI/CABS** Milan **cabs** are white. Late night, Sunday and extra-luggage surcharges are applied. Not every taxi accepts credit cards, we suggest to verify in advance. If in doubt of the price, ask the driver for an estimate before getting in ( **for booking**: Radio Taxi 02 8585; Taxiblu 02 4040 or Yellow Taxi Multiservice 02 6969). There are **fixed fares** from and to the airports, more info [**here**](https://intaxi.it/tariffe-taxi-milano/). **TRAINS** The **main stations** in Milan are Stazione Centrale, Milano Rogoredo and Milano Garibaldi. Remember to get your ticket before your journey as ‘on-board tickets’ are subject to a surcharge. Remember also to **validate** your **ticket** (if it is a paper ticket) by stamping it through the validating machines at the track platform or around the stations. Expired or not validated tickets are subject to fines. If you **did not** **validate** your ticket, contact immediately the ‘on board’ representative. [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students/getting-around#addtoany "Show all")

title: Health Insurance | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Health Insurance Before their arrival, students should ensure they are properly **covered** in case they require **medical care during their stay in Italy**.Bocconi University does not provide students with an insurance policy.Students shouldcheckif the social security scheme in their country of residence covers the cost of medical treatment in Italy. **EU citizens**: be sure to bring the **European Health Insurance Card** ( **EHIC**), which entitles the holder to get necessary treatment at the same cost as citizens of the host country. The card is valid only for **state-provided services**, asprivate healthcare is not covered. We recommend that , before departure, students verify with the social security administration of their home country how to obtain the card and which services are covered. EU citizens can also apply for **Form S1**. They should obtain their S1 form from the healthcare institution of their home country **before departure**. Students should confirm eligibility with the social security institution of their country of residence, as requirements may vary between EU member states. **Non-EU citizens**: before leaving their home country these students are strongly advised to obtain **health** **insurance with international coverage.** To apply for a Permit of Stay, students will be required to prove that they are covered for medical expenses for the entire duration of their stay in Italy. [More…](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students/health-insurance#addtoany "Show all")

For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Italian Language Courses ### **Italian Language Crash Course** **Kick off your exchange experience with a 2-week immersive Italian Crash Course!** Before Bocconi classes begin, you’ll have the chance to start learning Italian while meeting fellow exchange students from around the world and building your first friendships in Milan. title: Medical Assistance | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Medical Assistance #### **Euromedica** Health center located at **Viale Bligny 11**. After signing up for an annual membership card at the **cost of €12**, students, faculty and staff have a **10%** discount on specific outpatient services. For further information [click here](https://www.euromedica-assistance.com/). #### **Individual Counseling** A **Counseling and Self-Empowerment** desk is available to students, to support their psychological well-being and help them develop greater self-awareness of their personal resources. Individual counseling (offered in Italian, English or French) aims to help **identify** and **resolve** situations of **difficulty** and **discomfort**, while also strengtheningtheir personal resources, through a personalized pathway developed together. Further **information** available [**here**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/programs/current-students/services/counseling). #### **Health Services** For further information about **health services** and the on-campus medical center during your stay in Italy visit [**this webpage**](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/freshly-enrolled-students-you-arrive/health-services "Health Services"). title: Visa Process for exchange students | Bocconi University
text: For International Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students) Incoming Exchange Students [Overview](https://www.unibocconi.it/en/international-students/incoming-exchange-students) # Visa Process for exchange students All non-EU exchange students must apply for a **Student Visa** before coming to Italy. To learn more about visa application deadlines and **requirements**, visit [http://vistoperitalia.esteri.it/home/en.](https://vistoperitalia.esteri.it/?lang=it_IT "this link") A guided procedure will help you find out whether you need to apply for a visa and where - based on your nationality, country of residence, reasons for visit and length of stay. Depending on your situation, you may be required to apply for a visa in your home country, in your country of residence or in the country where you are currently studying. Visa requirements may vary. The official Acceptance Letter, issued by Bocconi University, is always required. **Application Process** Students must complete a 2-step process: - Pre-register and submit the application on the Universitaly portal (mandatory) at [ "Original URL: https://www.universitaly.it/. Click or tap if you trust this link."). This application is different and separate from the Bocconi Exchange Program online application. _Please note: the procedure to complete the Universitaly application for the Academic Year 2026–2027 is not yet open; a specific communication will follow with detailed instructions on this mandatory step._ - Apply for a Study Visa: procedures may vary from Consulate to Consulate. Students should follow the instructions provided on the website of the Consulate where they plan to apply. We recommend that students review visa procedures and start searching for a **visa appointment well in advance**. Please note that, according to the Italian Authorities and ministries, acceptance into the exchange program does not guarantee the issuance of a visa. The decision is made solely by the relevant diplomatic mission, Consulate or Embassy. Universitaly _Please note: the procedure to complete the Universitaly application for the Academic Year 2026–2027 is not yet open; a specific communication will follow with detailed instructions on this mandatory step._ Pre-register on the Universitaly portal at [ "Original URL: https://www.universitaly.it/. Click or tap if you trust this link.") To register, click on " **First steps in Italy**" box in the homepage and follow the registration guide. After that click on “ **Pre-enroll now**" that will appear in your personal area. You will be asked to fill out a **3 step-form**: **STEP A**: - complete the form with your personal data: it must be entered exactly as shown on your passport. **STEP B**: - fill out the form with your passport number and expiration date, then upload it (the page with your personal data only) - upload a passport-size picture of your face - select the country and the Italian Embassy or Consulate where you will be requesting your visa; then in the section “specify the reason for the visa application” type in “I want to spend a period of mobility for study/traineeship (e.g. Erasmus)” - select the University (Università Commerciale Luigi Bocconi), select Corsi Singoli in “course type” drop-down list - in the “course name” tab, type in “Exchange Program” **STEP C**: - as an exchange student, in this section you
